result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the state layer (demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts) imports this SFC's type, holds its instance, and mutates the component's private state through defineExpose, with the handle published on the app-wide ADMIN_PORT_KEY surface (useAdminUsers.ts:14/:27/:95/:117/:132/:146; usePalettePorts.ts:123/:197; AdminPane.vue:27/:134; AdminUsersPanel.vue:389). It is the only finding that inverts a layer and the root of L-3 (the port carries adminUsersPanelRef solely to serve it). Its new consequence this pass is a real state divergence: onAdminDeleteUserPalette (useAdminUsers.ts:112-125) updates the panel's copy but never remotePalettes, while its sibling onAdminDeletePalette (:106) does — so an admin delete performed from this panel leaves the deleted palette rendering in Browse. Curing L-1 deletes a port member, a defineExpose, an inverted import edge, a latent module cycle, five masking `?.` swallows, and that divergence in one move.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the sub-claims I checked and proved SOUND rather than asserted — including one r1 hypothesis I killed by measurement. (1) PUBLIC SURFACE IS DOGFOODED HONESTLY: the subject imports @mkbabb/value.js not at all, and across its whole 55-module measured closure the only library specifier is @mkbabb/value.js/color — a published entry in package.json#exports; demo-wide there are 51 library imports across 5 published subpaths and zero relative imports into src/ (`grep -rn 'from "(\../)*src/' demo` -> no matches); vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES the self-alias set from package.json#exports, so it structurally cannot resolve a specifier a real consumer could not write. No false proof of the public API here. (2) NO DUPLICATE GLASS-UI INSTANCE from the barrel/subpath split (r1 left this open): `grep -l "dialog-TNRDkcE4" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.js` -> command-*.js, dialog.js, glass-ui.js, search.js — one shared chunk, one component definition, one dialogStageContext; the running dev server loads 9 pre-bundled glass-ui chunks total on this route. L-5 is therefore a structural defect, not a runtime cost. (3) THE THREE-PARALLEL-useDark SUSPECT IS CURED (r1 left it unexamined): all 9 sites import useGlobalDark from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dark; the only survivors are two stale COMMENTS describing the historical race (useMarkdownColors.ts:16, useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76). (4) NO component->boot and no feature->shell edge is written by this file — its 11 imports touch vue, glass-ui, lucide and four demo trees; the boundary violation that exists (L-2) is written by the shell into the feature. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax discipline is clean (:199 import type; :186/:200-203 genuine value imports). (7) demo/shared/ is not a new contrivance — it predates this component and L-8's cure moves a file INTO it. (8) Reactive props destructure is idiomatic (:205-220, default on loadError; emptyCount at :241 stays reactive); the single edict-7 miss is at the mount site (AdminPane.vue:27/:134) and is a SYMPTOM of L-1 — useTemplateRef cannot express a borrowed ref, which is the indictment. (9) NO a11y defect on this route is attributable to this component: all four safari matrices report the same 4 small tap targets (an input and three 22x22 buttons "Switch to slug"/"Generate new slug"/"Cancel"), every one in demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue; overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, main 1 on all four; the roving-tabindex / Full-Keyboard-Access delta (MT-F022) is confirmed not a library-structure concern and is not counted. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/` (six-file component folder + four `card/composables/`), plus judgment of the decomposition itself
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1/C-2 together: PaletteCard's entire per-colour action surface is inert AND unstyled. glass-ui 7.0.0's `WatercolorDot` declares `inheritAttrs: false` and renders a hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">` — so SwatchHoverMenu's `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` are all silently discarded (measured: `tagName: SPAN`, `ariaLabel: null`, `pointerEvents: none`, hit-test resolves to the wrapper div, popover count 0→0 on click, Playwright reports `<div class="relative"> intercepts pointer events`). The only surviving route — the hover Teleport — carries class `.floating-panel`, which exists nowhere in the demo or in glass-ui 7.0.0: it was deleted in commit `c84504d3` (2026-03-25) under the false claim "now provided by @import @mkbabb/glass-ui/styles". Measured live: `position: static`, `background: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `box-shadow: none`, `z-index: auto`, rect `{x:-195, y:844, w:390, h:40}` in a 390×844 viewport at scrollY 0 — a transparent, unpositioned block at the end of `<body>`, half off the left edge. Add / Edit / Copy have had no working route on any pointer class for four months. Zero tests expand a card, so nothing caught it.

defects.defect: The swatch is not an interactive element: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` are all discarded by glass-ui `WatercolorDot`, which declares `inheritAttrs: false` and renders a hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true">` with inline `pointer-events: none`. Swatch click is dead on fine pointers; the reka-ui `PopoverTrigger as-child` touch path is dead identically (as-child props arrive as fallthrough attrs); every swatch is nameless and aria-hidden.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20,29-36 (props sent) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (declared props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} — no `tag`) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js:80 `inheritAttrs: !1,` and :102-110 renders `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", … pointerEvents:"none"})` · live measurement: {"tagName":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tagAttr":null,"attrs":["data-v-292b9032","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"],"pointerEvents":"none","tabIndex":-1,"parentTag":"DIV","parentAttrs":["class=relative"]} · click probe: {"hitTest":"DIV.relative","panelsBefore":0,"panelsAfterClick":0} · Playwright actionability: `<div class="relative"> intercepts pointer events` (5000ms timeout)
defects.mechanism: glass-ui 7 contract break absorbed silently: a child with `inheritAttrs:false` swallows every fallthrough attr/listener/ARIA the consumer sends, and the consumer invents a `tag` prop the child never declared — semantics asserted in source, absent in the DOM
defects.reproduction: 1) seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with a local palette before boot; 2) load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; 3) click a card to expand; 4) `document.querySelector('.watercolor-swatch')` → SPAN, aria-hidden=true, aria-label null, pointer-events none; 5) dispatch a click at the swatch centre → `document.querySelectorAll('.floating-panel').length` stays 0
defects.proposedCure: Move the semantics to the consumer, not the primitive: SwatchHoverMenu renders its own `<button type="button" :aria-label>` and mounts `<WatercolorDot>` inside it as the pure decoration it already is (its `aria-hidden` + `pointer-events:none` then become correct by construction). One element, one file; removes all dependence on a `tag` prop glass-ui never offered. Adding `tag` to glass-ui would be the edict-4-compliant alternative but violates KISS — a wrapping `<button>` buys the same thing for free.

defects.defect: `.floating-panel` — the class the swatch hover popover is built on — does not exist in the demo or in glass-ui 7.0.0. It was deleted in commit c84504d3 (2026-03-25) with the message "Delete dock.css, floating-panel.css, glass.css, transitions.css; now provided by @import @mkbabb/glass-ui/styles". It is not provided. The panel renders `position: static` (making `positionPanel`'s inline top/left inert), fully transparent, with no shadow/radius/z-index, appended at the end of `<body>`, half off the left edge.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:42 `class="floating-panel"` · `grep -rln "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → no matches · live computed style: {"position":"static","top":"0px","left":"0px","zIndex":"auto","background":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","boxShadow":"none","borderRadius":"0px"}, panelRect {"x":-195,"y":844,"w":390,"h":40} in viewport {"w":390,"h":844} at scrollY 0, parent BODY · `git show c84504d3^:demo/@/styles/floating-panel.css` recovers: `/* Floating panel — used by PaletteCard swatch popover & PaletteCardMenu (Teleported) */ .floating-panel { position: fixed; z-index: var(--z-overlay); border-radius: var(--radius-xl); border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border)/0.6); background: hsl(var(--card)/0.75); backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.3); box-shadow: var(--glass-shadow-elevated); pointer-events: auto; animation: floating-panel-in …; }`
defects.mechanism: a migration commit deleted a demo-local stylesheet on an unverified claim that the upstream package supplies it; the JS positioning code (viewport coords, written for `position: fixed`) was left behind and is now writing inert values onto a static element
defects.reproduction: 1) seed a local palette; 2) /#/palettes; 3) expand a card; 4) real-mouse hover a swatch wrapper; 5) `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.floating-panel')).position` → "static", backgroundColor → "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)", getBoundingClientRect() → {x:-195, y:844}
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT re-add a demo-local floating-panel.css — that reinstates the very fork the migration meant to absorb, and a popover is a component-type glass-ui already owns (edict 4). Retire the hand-rolled Teleport branch entirely and render the reka-ui `Popover` on BOTH pointer classes, driving `:open` from `useHoverPopover` on fine pointers. That single removal deletes `positionPanel`, deletes the `floatingStyle` prop and its type drift, deletes the aria-hidden panel (C-9), and cures C-6.

defects.defect: A malformed palette colour destroys the whole pane: `safeFirstColor` calls `certifyAccentInk`, which handles `parseCssColor`'s `!ok` result but not its THROW. `parseCssColor` throws a TypeError on the entire empty-argument colour-function class (`oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()`, `hwb()`, `color()`, `rgba()`, whitespace variants, case variants), and the API persists any string up to 200 chars with no colour validation.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:226-230 (`firstColor` → `safeCss` → `certifyAccentInk`) bound at :144 · demo/color-session/ink.ts:38-43,130-143 (handles `!parsed.ok`, not the throw) · api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` — no colour validation · vite-node probe over 18 inputs: `threw: 13 / 18`, e.g. `"oklch()" => THREW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` · exact-call probe (node AND live browser via `import('/@fs/…/demo/color-session/ink.ts')`): `certifyAccentInk("oklch()", 0.45) => THREW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` while `"#888"` and `"not-a-color"` return normally · live: seeding colors[0].css="oklch()" and loading /#/palettes replaced the pane with "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')"
defects.mechanism: a Result-returning parser that is actually partial — it throws instead of returning `{ok:false}` for a whole input class — so every caller's `!ok` degenerate is bypassed; this is the standing R1 crash class reaching a render-path computed over unvalidated remote data
defects.reproduction: `npx vite-node` on `import { certifyAccentInk } from 'demo/color-session/ink.ts'; certifyAccentInk('oklch()', 0.45)` → TypeError. Live: seed `localStorage['color-palettes']` with `{version:1,palettes:[{id:'x',name:'M',slug:'m',isLocal:true,colors:[{css:'oklch()',position:0}],createdAt:…,updatedAt:…}]}`, reload /#/palettes.
defects.proposedCure: Fix the parser at the root, not the call site: `parseCssColor` must return `{ok:false}` for the empty-args class (this is R1 from the π parser-proof gate and it is still live). `certifyAccentInk` already carries the correct degenerate — nothing in PaletteCard should change. Independently, `api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts` should refine `css` through the same parser so unparseable colours never persist.

defects.defect: The card's primary action — expand — is keyboard-inoperable. `role="article"` div with `@click`, no `tabindex`, no `@keydown`, no alternative affordance; the only focusable descendant is the "Palette menu" button. Compounding: `v-bind="press.handlers"` binds `useLiquidPress`'s `onKeydown`/`onKeyup`/`onBlur` to an element that can never be focused — three of eight bound handlers are structurally dead.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:5-27 (div role=article, v-bind press.handlers, @click emit) · PalettesPane.vue:91 / BrowsePane.vue:102 wire that click to `toggleExpand` · live measurement across 3 cards: {"tabIndex":-1,"cardIsFocusable":false,"focusableDescendants":1,"focusableNames":["Palette menu"]} · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js handlers block `b = (e) => e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " "` with onKeydown/onKeyup/onBlur
defects.mechanism: click-on-a-div as the primary affordance: the container correctly avoids `role="button"` (it houses nested controls) but never provides the named interactive child that should carry the action, so the whole expanded region is gated behind a control keyboard users cannot reach
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with seeded palettes; `document.querySelectorAll('[role="article"]')[0].tabIndex` → -1; tab through the card — the only stop is "Palette menu"; no key press expands the card.
defects.proposedCure: Give the action a name and an element: make the palette title a real `<button>` that emits `click` (it is already the semantic label of the card and already carries a click handler for rename), leaving the container a plain `article` whose click stays a mouse-only convenience. This simultaneously cures C-10, since the title stops needing an unconditional `.stop`.

defects.defect: `ActionFeedback` never re-arms its dismissal timer and never clears it on unmount. Because `showFeedback` sets an already-true `visible` ref, the watcher does not fire and the new message inherits the previous message's remaining countdown; and no `onUnmounted` cleanup exists, so a pending timeout fires into a destroyed component and writes to a dead card's state.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:37-47 (`watch(() => props.visible, …)`) · PaletteCard.vue:238-242 `showFeedback` sets `feedbackVisible.value = true` (no-op when already true) · BrowsePane.vue:226-265 fires showFeedback from 4 async paths against the same card · executable vitest probe (@vue/test-utils + fake timers, host mirrors PaletteCard.vue:123-128), both tests PASS: "visible 100ms after 2nd message: false" (promised 2500ms, delivered 100ms) and "timers pending before unmount: 1 after unmount: 1"
defects.mechanism: watching a boolean edge to drive a timer whose identity is really the MESSAGE, plus a raw module-scope `setTimeout` handle with no lifecycle cleanup
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config <probe cfg>` on a mount of ActionFeedback via a host replicating PaletteCard's wiring: showFeedback('Saved!','success'); advanceTimersByTime(2400); showFeedback('Delete failed','error'); advanceTimersByTime(100) → visible === false. Second test: showFeedback then unmount() → vi.getTimerCount() still 1.
defects.proposedCure: The component is a timed toast, so the boolean is the wrong subject: watch message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and register `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better still, hoist the dismissal to the caller and let ActionFeedback be pure presentation — that also removes the `update:visible` round-trip back into the parent.

defects.defect: `useHoverPopover.onHover` reads `e.currentTarget` inside a `nextTick` callback, after the event handler has returned and the DOM has reset it to null. Produces an intermittent unhandled TypeError; and the coordinates it computes are inert anyway because the target element is `position: static` (C-2). The `as Element` cast is what let the null through the type system.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:26-31 `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element))` and :20-24 `positionPanel` calls `swatchEl.getBoundingClientRect()` · captured from the running app's console: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')  at positionPanel (…/useHoverPopover.ts:18:25)  at …/useHoverPopover.ts:26:18` · panel inline style after the throw: `top: 0px; left: 0px; transform: translateX(-50%)` (the untouched reactive defaults)
defects.mechanism: reading a DOM Event property with dispatch-scoped lifetime from a deferred callback; whether it survives depends on microtask-checkpoint timing (real hovers usually survive, programmatic dispatch never does), and a non-null assertion cast hides the hazard from tsc
defects.reproduction: Expand a card, then dispatch `new PointerEvent('pointerenter', {pointerType:'mouse'})` on a swatch wrapper from an already-async context → console TypeError with the stack above; the panel's inline top/left stay at 0px.
defects.proposedCure: Capture `const el = e.currentTarget as Element` inside the synchronous handler body and close over the local — the cast then reflects reality. Moot if C-2 is cured by adopting the reka-ui `Popover`, which positions itself and makes `positionPanel` deletable.

defects.defect: `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` forces both consumers to maintain a component-instance map, and both register it with `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[key] = el)"`. Vue calls a function ref with `null` on unmount, so the `el &&` guard makes teardown a no-op: nothing is ever deleted. The reactive map grows for the session lifetime, retaining dead component instances and, through them, whole subtrees, spring instances, hover closures and Palette objects.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` · BrowsePane.vue:94 and PalettesPane.vue:84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` · BrowsePane.vue:209 / PalettesPane.vue:177 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})` · growth drivers: BrowsePane.vue:140 `pm.loadMoreRemotePalettes()` paging, plus filter/sort re-keys
defects.mechanism: an imperative `defineExpose` handle as the feedback channel forces an identity map on every host; the `el &&` truthiness guard silently discards Vue's unmount signal, and the `(el: any)` cast hides the null from tsc
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-level certainty rather than an executed measurement (the shared dev browser in this formation had a concurrent writer, so a live key count would not have been attributable). The omission is unambiguous: Vue invokes function refs with `null` on unmount and the guard drops that call.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix: make feedback DATA. Lift `{ key, message, variant }` into the pane and pass it down as a prop (`:feedback="feedback?.key === palette.slug ? feedback : null"`). `defineExpose`, both cardRefs maps, both `(el: any)` casts and the leak all disappear together, and the component stops needing an imperative handle at all.

defects.defect: The inline rename row ships two nameless 18×18px icon buttons and an input whose only accessible name is its placeholder, and drops focus to `<body>` when it closes. This is PaletteCard's real contribution to the audit's nameless-button and small-tap-target counters — a contribution the visual REPORT records as zero because both palette routes were captured with no cards mounted.

defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with a seeded local palette, click the card title to open rename, then enumerate `card.querySelectorAll('button')` → 2 entries with empty accessible name at 18x18. Focus the input and dispatch `keydown{key:'Escape'}` → `document.activeElement === document.body`.
defects.proposedCure: Add `aria-label="Save name"` / `aria-label="Cancel rename"` and raise the hit area to the 24px floor via padding (the visual icon stays 14px); label the input with `aria-label="Palette name"`. Restore focus in the parent: capture the trigger element before entering rename mode and refocus it in the `submit`/`cancel` handlers, which is where the mode transition already lives (PaletteCard.vue:285-288).

defects.defect: The swatch hover panel is marked `aria-hidden="true"` while containing two tabbable buttons — an explicit WAI-ARIA MUST NOT. The comment claims the reka-ui Popover is "the accessible route", but that branch only mounts when `canHover === false`, so on any fine pointer there is no accessible route at all.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37-51 (`aria-hidden="true"` on the Teleport panel; the accessible branch is `v-if="!canHover"` at :9) · live measurement: {"panelAriaHidden":"true","tabbableInPanel":2,"panelButtons":[{"name":"Edit color oklch(63.94…deg)","w":28,"h":28,"tab":0},{"name":"Copy color oklch(63.94…deg)","w":28,"h":28,"tab":0}]} · WAI-ARIA 1.2 §aria-hidden: "Authors MUST NOT use aria-hidden=\"true\" on … an element that contains focusable elements."
defects.mechanism: two parallel implementations of one popover split by pointer capability, where the accessibility story was assigned wholly to the branch that does not mount on desktop, and the other branch was papered over with aria-hidden rather than fixed
defects.reproduction: Expand a card on a fine-pointer device, hover a swatch wrapper, then read `document.querySelector('.floating-panel')` — aria-hidden="true" with two tabIndex-0 buttons inside.
defects.proposedCure: Same single cure as C-2: one reka-ui `Popover` for both pointer classes, `:open` driven by `useHoverPopover` on fine pointers. reka-ui manages aria-hidden, focus scope and dismissal correctly by construction, and the duplicated branch (and its drift risk) disappears.

defects.defect: The decomposition is not along real seams. `PaletteCardSwatches.vue` is a 96-line wrapper with ZERO state and ZERO logic that declares 8 props and 8 emits, every one of which is a pass-through between `useHoverPopover()` and its consumer one component away — precisely the earns-nothing wrapper feedback_kiss_no_contrivance forbids. `PaletteCardMeta.vue` is a 64-line multi-root fragment extracted to reduce a line count. Meanwhile the centre did not move: PaletteCard still declares 17 emit variants and an 18-branch string-keyed dispatch table whose child contract is an untyped `action: [action: string]`, with `if (!fn) return;` silently swallowing any unknown string.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:75-95 (8 props, 8 emits, no `ref`/`computed`/`watch` anywhere in the file) — every prop sourced from PaletteCard.vue:246-255's `useHoverPopover()` destructure, every emit routed back to that same destructure at PaletteCard.vue:149-156 · the composable's only parent-side use is the one line PaletteCard.vue:277 `onBeforeCollapse: () => { openPopoverIndex.value = null; }` · PaletteCard.vue:200-218 (17 emits) and :290-319 (18-entry table, `if (!fn) return;` at :315-316) · PaletteCardMenu.vue:225 `action: [action: string]` · file sizes: PaletteCard 364 / Menu 228 / Swatches 96 / Meta 64 / Rename 66 / Feedback 58 lines; PaletteCard's `<script setup>` is 172 lines
defects.mechanism: markup was moved out while state stayed centralized, so the split produced conduits rather than components; the seam was drawn above the state that is actually local to the swatch row, and the parent's outward surface (17 emits, stringly-typed dispatch) was never touched
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural judgment, evidenced by the file contents and the prop/emit census above rather than by an execution.
defects.proposedCure: Move `useHoverPopover()` INTO PaletteCardSwatches (its state is entirely local to the swatch row; the parent's single need is covered by an `@collapse` emit or a `watch(() => expanded)` in the child). That collapses 8 props to 4 (`colors`, `isLocal`, `displaySlug`, `swatchClass`) and 8 emits to 3, making it a real component. Type the menu contract as a `MenuAction` union so `if (!fn) return;` becomes unreachable and deletable, and the 17-emit surface becomes checkable. Keep PaletteCardMenu, PaletteRenameInput and ActionFeedback — those three splits are along genuine seams. Fold PaletteCardMeta back into the title row (it is a fragment, not a component).

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: there is no test anywhere that would fail if PaletteCard were broken — and it IS broken. Zero unit tests mount any of the six files or exercise any of the four composables, and no e2e test ever expands a card, which is exactly why every defect in the expanded region (C-1, C-2, C-6, C-9) has shipped unnoticed since March 2026.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "PaletteCard" test/ demo/test/` → no matches; `grep -rln "useHoverPopover|useHeightTransition|useLeaveTimer" test/ demo/test/` → no matches (vitest.config.ts includes `test/**/*.ts` + `demo/test/**/*.ts`) · e2e coverage is only e2e/smoke/flows/palette-delete.spec.ts (clicks "Palette menu" then Delete) and e2e/smoke/flows/vote-toggle.spec.ts (clicks the heart); e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:183 asserts only `[role="article"].bg-well` resolves to `--well-bg` (a material census) · `grep -rn "expand" e2e/` returns dock/band tests only · REPORT.json records both palette routes captured with zero cards (browse consoleWarning "Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError…"; palettes.png shows "No saved palettes yet.")
defects.mechanism: the gates assert MATERIAL identity (tokens, tiers, backgrounds) and two isolated network flows, never BEHAVIOUR of the component's principal interaction, so an entire rendering region has no observer
defects.reproduction: Green-keeping mutations, each verified reachable by inspection: (1) delete `@click="$emit('click')"` at PaletteCard.vue:26 — expansion dies entirely; (2) change PaletteCard.vue:226 to `colors[1]?.css` — every card's certified ink is wrong; (3) replace PaletteCardSwatches.vue's template with `<template />` — the expanded card renders empty; (4) set ActionFeedback.vue:30 `autoDismissMs` default to 0 — feedback never dismisses; (5) delete `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` at PaletteCard.vue:244 — four BrowsePane async paths throw at runtime. All five keep the full suite green.
defects.proposedCure: Two files, no new infrastructure. (a) A vitest mount test that expands the card and asserts the swatch row renders NAMED, FOCUSABLE controls — it fails today on C-1. (b) One e2e that expands a card and clicks a swatch — it fails today on C-1 and C-2. Seed through `localStorage['color-palettes']` before boot; the store is a plain `useStorage` singleton (demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:6), so no API is required, as this audit demonstrated.

defects.defect: `@click.stop` on the palette title is unconditional, so on the browse wall (where `editableName` is unset) clicking the palette NAME — the most obvious target on the card — stops propagation and does nothing: no rename (correctly gated) and no expand (incorrectly suppressed).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:53-59 `@click.stop="editableName && startRenaming()"` — Vue compiles `.stop` to a stopPropagation() call that runs before the expression · BrowsePane.vue:92-117 does not pass `editable-name` (only PalettesPane.vue:89 does)
defects.mechanism: an event modifier used as if it were conditional on the handler's own guard; modifiers are unconditional by compilation
defects.reproduction: NONE executed live (the browse wall needs a reachable API and the shared dev server is CORS-blocked). Vue template-compiler semantics make the outcome deterministic from PaletteCard.vue:58 + BrowsePane.vue:92-117.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of C-4: split the editable title into its own `<button>` under `v-if="editableName"`, leaving the non-editable title a plain span with no handler and no modifier. No conditional-stop contrivance needed.

defects.defect: The `if (action !== "rename") menuOpen.value = false;` guard in `handleMenuAction` is provably dead, and the comment above it describes an intent the code contradicts: `startRenaming()` closes the menu itself, so both branches close it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:291-292 comment ("keep the menu open visually until the input takes focus"), :317 `if (action !== "rename") menuOpen.value = false;`, :318 `fn();`, and :280-283 `function startRenaming() { menuOpen.value = false; renaming.value = true; }`
defects.mechanism: a guard and the function it guards against both perform the same mutation — dead branch preserved by a comment that documents an intent never implemented
defects.reproduction: NONE — provable by reading PaletteCard.vue:280-283 against :317-318; every path sets menuOpen=false.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the guard and the comment; set `menuOpen.value = false` unconditionally before dispatch. (If keeping the menu open through rename is genuinely wanted, remove the assignment from `startRenaming` instead — but pick one, and let the code state it.)

defects.defect: `scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" })` on card expand is ungated by prefers-reduced-motion. The global PRM guard sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important`, but CSSOM-View consults that property only when `behavior` is `"auto"` — an author-supplied `"smooth"` overrides it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:48 `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "nearest" });` in `onAfterEnter` · demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 PRM guard sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important` (CSS property only) · in-repo counter-precedent: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:40 "Never `scrollIntoView`: even with…"
defects.mechanism: a JS scroll option that outranks the CSS property the global reduced-motion guard neutralises, so the app-wide PRM fence has a hole exactly where JS supplies an explicit behavior
defects.reproduction: NONE executed (would require flipping the emulated media feature); the CSSOM-View precedence rule and the two cited lines make it deterministic. `block: "nearest"` limits but does not remove the effect.
defects.proposedCure: Read the media query once (glass-ui already exports `useReducedMotion`) and pass `behavior: prefersReduced ? "auto" : "smooth"` — or follow the EasingSpecimenStrip precedent and drop the scroll entirely, since `block:"nearest"` means it only ever fires when the card is already partly off-screen.

defects.defect: `ActionFeedback` has no `role="status"`, no `aria-live` and no `aria-atomic`. It is the sole surface reporting the outcome of four async operations (save, delete, visibility flip, fork error) and it is silent to screen readers.
defects.evidence:
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:4-15 (bare `
` with a class list, an icon and a `{{ message }}`; no role, no aria-live) · BrowsePane.vue:226-265 drives it from onSave, onDeleteOwned, onSetVisibility and onForkError
defects.mechanism: an async-result surface built as pure decoration, so the outcome of a network mutation is conveyed by colour and glyph only
defects.reproduction: NONE — absence is direct from ActionFeedback.vue:4-15.
defects.proposedCure: Add `role="status"` (implicit `aria-live="polite"`) to the chip root. One attribute at the root of the component that owns the concern — no wrapper, no per-instance override.

defects.defect: `PaletteCardMenu` mixes two reka-ui activation idioms for one behaviour: eleven items use `@click`, five use `@select`, and the sub-trigger is worked around with `@click.prevent`. `@select` is the primitive's semantic event (it also fires for keyboard activation and typeahead); `@click` is the DOM leak-through, so the two groups of items are not keyboard-equivalent.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue — `@click` at lines 18, 31, 52, 66, 76, 86, 96, 136, 146, 158, 165; `@select` at lines 113, 116, 119, 123, 126; `@click.prevent` workaround at line 108
defects.mechanism: drift between a primitive's own event contract and raw DOM events within a single file, producing two activation semantics for one menu
defects.reproduction: NONE — the divergence is direct from the cited line numbers.
defects.proposedCure: Use `@select` uniformly — it is reka-ui's contract for menu-item activation and covers pointer, Enter/Space and typeahead identically. The `@click.prevent` on the sub-trigger then also becomes unnecessary.

defects.defect: `PaletteCard.vue` is the only file in its own folder that does not use Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure (standing edict 7), and its prop declarations restate `| undefined` that `?` already implies.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:182-198 `withDefaults(defineProps<{ expanded?: boolean | undefined; … }>(), …)` followed by eleven `props.palette` reads · siblings all use destructure: PaletteCardMenu.vue:206, PaletteCardMeta.vue:61, PaletteRenameInput.vue:39
defects.mechanism: idiom drift inside one component folder — the file that was refactored last kept the pre-3.5 form while the extracted children adopted the current one
defects.reproduction: NONE — direct from the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: Convert to `const { palette, expanded, layout = "default", swatchClass = "w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10", … } = defineProps<…>()` — Vue 3.5 compiles destructured props to reactive accessors, so `withDefaults` disappears with it. Drop the redundant `| undefined` on every optional prop.
