defects.defect: `.floating-panel` — the class that is supposed to make the swatch hover popover a floating surface — is defined by NO module: not in demo/styles/, not anywhere in the repo's CSS, not in @mkbabb/glass-ui 7.0.0. The teleported popover therefore computes to position:static with no background, shadow or z-index, so its inline top/left are inert and it lands in normal flow at the end of <body>.
defects.evidence: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37-51 applies `class="floating-panel"` + inline :style. `grep -rn "floating-panel" --include='*.css' . --exclude-dir=node_modules` → one hit, and it is a COMMENT (demo/styles/animations.css:2). `grep -rln "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/` → no output. Live probe (synthetic element + full document.styleSheets scan): {"computed":{"position":"static","transform":"none","background":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","zIndex":"auto","border":"0px","boxShadow":"none"},"rules":[],"ruleCount":0}. Measured rendered geometry: rect {x:-720, y:900, w:1440, h:40}, parentIsBody:true. Spec: CSS Positioned Layout L3, `static` — "the box's top, right, bottom, and left properties have no effect."
defects.mechanism: Ownership vacuum / dangling design-system reference. Glass 7.0.0 was 'adopted whole' at W44; `.floating-panel` was a glass-ui recipe the demo never owned and glass-ui 7 does not ship. No toolchain can see it — a CSS class is a string.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with ≥1 saved palette in localStorage key `color-palettes` → click a card to expand → hover any swatch. Popover renders as a transparent full-viewport-width strip at the bottom of the document instead of a panel over the swatch.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled hover branch entirely. glass-ui 7 ships ./popover and SwatchHoverMenu ALREADY uses it on the touch branch (line 61). Fold the swatch + its popover into ONE glass-ui `Swatch` component that owns its own surface; `.floating-panel` ceases to exist rather than being redefined in demo/.

defects.defect: useHoverPopover reads `e.currentTarget` inside a nextTick callback — i.e. after event dispatch has completed, when the DOM spec guarantees it is null. Every swatch hover throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')` and the popover's position is never applied. The `as Element` cast is the masking assertion that hid it from vue-tsc.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:30 — `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element));`. Live capture with an unhandledrejection listener: {"captured":["REJ:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')"],"inline":"top: 0px; left: 0px; transform: translateX(-50%);"} — the inline top/left are still the reactive initial 0px, proving positionPanel never completed. Spec: DOM Standard §2.2 — "The currentTarget attribute … When an event is dispatched, this is set to the object whose listener is being invoked, and reset to null afterwards."
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolled floating positioning inside a demo composable, duplicating @mkbabb/glass-ui/popover which the same component already imports and uses on its other branch. A dual path (edict 2) reimplementing a design-system primitive (edict 4); the `as Element` cast (edict 2 — masking fallback) let the null flow through typecheck.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, seed one palette, expand the card, dispatch/perform pointerenter on a swatch wrapper with `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', …)` installed. The rejection fires on every hover, on every desktop browser (canHover = matchMedia('(hover: hover)')).
defects.proposedCure: Capture the element at dispatch time (`const el = e.currentTarget as Element` BEFORE nextTick) is the patch; the transposition is to delete the branch — let the design-system Popover anchor to its own trigger so no coordinate is ever computed in demo/ at all.

defects.defect: The swatches pass `tag="button"` and `:aria-label` to glass-ui 7's WatercolorDot, which declares neither. Both are silently dropped: every colour swatch renders as `<span aria-hidden="true">`. The only focusable element in an expanded PaletteCard is the 'Palette menu' button — the card's primary content is keyboard-unreachable and invisible to assistive technology.
defects.evidence: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20 and :29-36 pass tag="button" + :aria-label; CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:62,64,95-105 the same. glass-ui 7.0.0 contract (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts): `type __VLS_Props = { color: string; variant?: "solid"|"ghost"; animate?: boolean; cycleDuration?: number; range?: [number,number]; seed?: string; }` — no `tag`, no name plumbing. Live DOM: {"tag":"SPAN","attrs":{"aria-hidden":"true","data-testid":"watercolor-swatch","data-variant":"solid", …no aria-label, no tabindex},"focusablesInCard":["BUTTON:Palette menu"]}.
defects.mechanism: Stale design-system prop contract surviving the Glass-7 adoption. vue-tsc cannot catch it: unknown attributes on a component are legal fallthrough attrs, not prop errors — so a green typecheck is not evidence the contract is current.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, seed a palette, expand the card, then query the swatch element's attributes and the card's focusable set: `[...card.querySelectorAll('a[href],button,input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])')]` returns exactly one entry, the menu button.
defects.proposedCure: The Swatch belongs in glass-ui as a first-class component that renders a real <button> with an accessible name — not a WatercolorDot the consumer tries to retag from outside. Interim: stop passing props the DS does not declare and wrap the dot in a real button in SwatchHoverMenu.

defects.defect: Palette export has two live homes: the file demo/palettes/export.ts (132 L — the ONLY path the card's five export menu items reach) and the directory demo/palettes/export/ (914 L across 13 files, the byte-exact W51 serializer set) whose sole consumer is one test. Two implementations of json/css/tailwind/svg/png, one explicitly labelled legacy in-source and still the only one a user can reach.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:113-128 → PaletteCard.vue:308-312 → usePaletteExport.ts:15-19 imports "./export" which resolves to the FILE export.ts. `wc -l demo/palettes/export/*.ts` → 914 total. `grep -rn "palettes/export/" --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' demo/ test/ src/` → exactly one hit: demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23. The collision is admitted at demo/palettes/export/serializers.ts:5-9: "the sibling legacy `../export.ts` (the pre-contract routed seat that W50 will replace) still resolves `./export`". Compounding: usePaletteExport.ts:21 swallows all failures into console.warn while the card owns a user-visible feedback rail used by save/delete/visibility.
defects.mechanism: A migration that shipped the replacement but never retired the incumbent, then documented the collision instead of resolving it. Edict 2 (no dual paths) named and deferred.
defects.reproduction: Static and deterministic: node module resolution prefers ./export.ts over ./export/ (which has no index.ts); the byte-exact set is import-dead outside the test. Verified by the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: One home: demo/palettes/export/ with serializers.ts as its barrel. Delete export.ts, route usePaletteExport through the byte-exact serializers, and surface failures on the card's existing feedback rail instead of console.warn.

defects.defect: 18 of the 19 demo/ui/* one-line shim barrels re-export from the glass-ui ROOT barrel rather than the per-component subpath glass-ui 7 publishes, so importing `{ Badge }` drags the whole design system into the module graph.
defects.evidence: All 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts are single re-export lines (e.g. `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`); only demo/ui/input targets a subpath. glass-ui 7 publishes 70 subpaths incl. ./button ./badge ./card ./popover ./dropdown-menu. The root barrel dist/glass-ui.js statically imports 42 chunk files totalling 167,733 bytes. Live on /#/palettes: {"name":"@mkbabb_glass-ui.js?v=3094e483","decodedBodySize":234309}. The three chunks PaletteCard needs total 8,123 B (badge 2,011 + button 2,960 + DropdownMenuTrigger 3,152). Repo census of the three doors in demo/: 90 shim sites, 37 direct-root, 82 direct-subpath — and PaletteCard.vue:165,166,170,171 uses all three in seven lines.
defects.mechanism: The shadcn-vue → glass-ui migration left a rename table in place of a boundary; nobody revisited which door it opens. docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md §1 forbids "one-line glass-ui forwarding directory" verbatim.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes and read `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` for `@mkbabb_glass-ui.js` — 234,309 B decoded. NOTE (honest scope): this is a DEV-graph number; the gh-pages Rollup build tree-shakes the root barrel and 37 sites import the root directly regardless, so no production payload regression is claimed — I did not measure one.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ (19 directories). Every consumer imports `@mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>` directly — one door, per-component chunks, and the architecture doc's own prohibition satisfied by construction.

defects.defect: The glass-ui icon-button atom is used ONCE in PaletteCard.vue, and the same recipe is hand-rolled 10 more times inside the palettes card cluster (15 repo-wide). Measured, the hand-rolled twins are 18×18 CSS px with aria-label null, against the atom's 36×36 named — below the WCAG 2.5.8 AA 24×24 floor, in the same card, twenty lines apart.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:96-104 uses `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` under a comment (93-95) claiming the recipe 'dies onto the glass-ui atom' and 'cures the ~24px touch target'. Counts: PaletteCardSwatches.vue 4, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue 3, PaletteRenameInput.vue 2, PaletteCardMeta.vue 1; `grep -rn "rounded-sm hover:bg-accent" --include='*.vue' demo/ | wc -l` → 15. Live measurement, rename state on /#/palettes: [{"type":"submit","w":18,"h":18,"aria":null},{"type":"button","w":18,"h":18,"aria":null}] with rootFont 16px; the atom in the same card: {"name":"Palette menu","w":36,"h":36,"cls":"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash "}.
defects.mechanism: A cure applied at one site and not propagated; the design-system atom that owns min-size, focus ring and accessible naming is imported into the file and then not used. Edicts 4 and 5.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a saved palette → click the palette title (PalettesPane passes editable-name) to enter rename → measure the two form buttons: 18×18, no aria-label. PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13-19 (p-0.5 + w-3 h-3) computes to 16px by the same arithmetic.
defects.proposedCure: Every icon button in the cluster becomes `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` (add an `xs` size producer-side if 36px is too large for the rename row). Zero hand-rolled recipes; min-size, ring and naming are inherited, not re-typed.

defects.defect: useHeightTransition's onAfterEnter calls scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}), which by spec bypasses the app's global prefers-reduced-motion guard: every card expansion smooth-scrolls the page for a user who asked for reduced motion.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:48 — `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "nearest" });`. The guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important` on `*`. CSSOM-View defers to the CSS scroll-behavior property only when the `behavior` option is "auto"; an explicit "smooth" forces a smooth scroll regardless. (The same composable's inline `style.transition` writes ARE caught, by the !important duration override — so the guard works everywhere except where JS overrides it explicitly.)
defects.mechanism: A height-morph composable that also performs document navigation — two unrelated responsibilities in one seam, and the second one escapes the CSS-level motion policy.
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from the spec + source: enable prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, expand a palette card whose body is off-screen; the page scrolls smoothly. No probe run.
defects.proposedCure: Scroll-into-view is the pane's decision, not the transition's — hoist it out of the composable. If it stays, read the motion preference and pass behavior: prm ? "auto" : "smooth".

defects.defect: useHoverPopover computes `left = rect.left + rect.width/2` — a CENTRE coordinate — but leaves the required translateX(-50%) to its consumers, and only one of the two supplies it.
defects.evidence: useHoverPopover.ts:20-24 (positionPanel). SwatchHoverMenu.vue:44 applies floatingStyle verbatim and adds no transform. PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 → `:floating-style="{ ...floatingStyle, transform: 'translateX(-50%)' }"`. CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 → `:floating-style="currentFloatingStyle"` — no transform.
defects.mechanism: Split ownership: the correction that makes the composable's output mean what it computes is not owned by the composable (nor by SwatchHoverMenu, the single component that consumes floatingStyle).
defects.reproduction: NONE — currently unobservable because L-15/L-16 destroy the position entirely. This is a LATENT defect that becomes live the moment those two are cured.
defects.proposedCure: Either return a left-edge coordinate, or fold the -50% into the composable's returned style object. Better: the design-system Popover anchors itself and no centering arithmetic exists anywhere.

defects.defect: `cssColor` is a public prop on the card that five host call sites are obliged to pass, and it reaches exactly one style binding — the slug chip's colour — only when `showSlug` is also passed AND the palette has zero colours.
defects.evidence: Declared PaletteCard.vue:186; its only use is PaletteCard.vue:226 `props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? props.cssColor ?? EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH`. Chain: firstColor → safeFirstColor (230) → :safe-first-color (144) → PaletteCardSwatches.vue:10, the slug chip's color/borderColor. `show-slug` is passed by only 2 of 5 hosts (BrowsePane.vue:101, AdminUsersPanel.vue:147). Passed by BrowsePane.vue:98, PalettesPane.vue:88, ExtractWorkbench.vue:149, AdminUsersPanel.vue:145, MixSourceSelector.vue:266 — the last as `""`, which `??` does not catch.
defects.mechanism: Derived state computed at the wrong level: the value is needed by one leaf for one binding, so the leaf should compute it (useSafeAccentFn is already a composable). Instead a five-link chain and a public prop exist to carry it down.
defects.reproduction: Static: grep shows two uses of cssColor in the component and one consumer of safeFirstColor. The empty-string path (MixSourceSelector.vue:266) would send "" into safeCss(), i.e. into the pass-1 L-1 throw path, for a zero-colour palette.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop from the card's surface. PaletteCardSwatches calls useSafeAccentFn("well") itself for the one chip that needs it.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's `paths` map has drifted from package.json#exports in both directions: three dangling entries (two of them retired subpaths) and two published subpaths with no entry.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (no "." root). tsconfig.demo.json paths, checked against the filesystem: `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts MISSING; `/parsing` → ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts MISSING; `/units` → ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts MISSING; color/math/easing/transform/quantize EXIST. Missing entries: `/value`, `/css` — and `/css` is imported at 10 demo sites. vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES the runtime alias set from exports precisely so it 'can never drift'; its TS twin is hand-maintained.
defects.mechanism: Two authorities for one published surface, one generated and one hand-written. `/parsing` and `/units` are retired subpaths — migration residue (edict 2).
defects.reproduction: node script comparing Object.keys(package.json.exports) against the tsconfig.demo.json paths entries and fs.existsSync on each target; output pasted in the report §L-24. Inert today (a missing paths target falls back to node resolution, which also fails), so dead config rather than an exploitable false public surface.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig `paths` map from package.json#exports the same way vite.config.ts already generates the alias set, so the two authorities cannot disagree.

result.strongestDefect: L-15 + L-16 together: the swatch hover popover — the card's entire expanded interaction surface — is built on a CSS class no module defines (`.floating-panel`, measured ruleCount 0, computing to position:static) positioned by a composable that reads `e.currentTarget` after event dispatch and therefore throws `TypeError: … null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')` on every hover (captured live). The result renders at {x:-720, y:900, w:1440, h:40} — a transparent full-viewport-width strip at the bottom of the document — while eight lines above, the same file already imports and correctly uses @mkbabb/glass-ui/popover on its touch branch. Two implementations of one concept in one file; the broken one is the desktop path.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as verified negatives so the next pass need not re-derive them: (1) Published-surface hygiene HOLDS — no file in the card's dependency cone imports @mkbabb/value.js at all, the whole demo/palettes/ feature touches it exactly twice and both are correct published subpaths (mix.ts:14 and export/png.ts:11 → @mkbabb/value.js/color); `grep -rn 'from \"@mkbabb/value.js\"' demo/` returns ZERO bare-root imports, which matters because package.json#exports has no \".\" key, so a bare-root specifier would be one a real consumer could not write; no @src/*, no dist/*, no path alias anywhere in the six files. The T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone is intact. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8) is CLEAN across all six files — PaletteCard.vue:168-169, PaletteCardMenu.vue:177-178, PaletteCardSwatches.vue:72, PaletteCardMeta.vue:59 all use `import type` or an inline `type` specifier. (3) No global keyframe is forked into a component — both scoped <style> blocks (PaletteCard.vue:337-364, ActionFeedback.vue:50-58) contain only geometry custom properties for the shared vj-morph / vj-celebrate families; the retired golden-text-shimmer fork is genuinely gone (edict 6 respected). (4) card/index.ts is a NAMED re-export barrel, not a star re-export — correct for SFCs whose scoped style makes the import side-effecting (PI-6). (5) useTemplateRef is used correctly at PaletteRenameInput.vue:48. (6) PaletteColorStrip.vue (72 L) carries no colour maths and no glass-ui edge — vue + own types only. (7) useHoverPopover.close() is bypassed at four sites in PaletteCard.vue (277, 322, 327, 332) which null openPopoverIndex without cancelling the leave timer; I traced every re-open path (onHover, onSwatchClick) and each calls cancelLeave() first, so the divergence is currently BENIGN — recorded as an unowned invariant, deliberately NOT filed as a defect.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the prune confirmation misstates the scope of an irreversible bulk deletion: under an active search the dialog reads "Prune 1 empty users? … permanently delete 1 user", the call is the unscoped server-wide POST /admin/users/prune-empty, and the result reads "Pruned 3 users". Promised 1, executed 3, reproduced in one probe run with a frame.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded negatives that did survive scrutiny, so they are not re-litigated: import type correct at :199; Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure with default at :205-220; the target===currentTarget keydown guard at :345 is load-bearing and correct; the shift-click confirm bypass really is excised (:311-314); resting destructive ink really is quieted — measured rgb(91,70,51) light / rgb(213,208,200) dark; the loading state really is row-shaped skeletons not a centered spinner (:46-48); motion is tokenized in demo/styles/animations.css:142-165 and reduced-motion-guarded at :184-192; no horizontal overflow at 390 (scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth 390); the WebKit/Chromium keyboard delta is macOS Full Keyboard Access per MT-F022 and is NOT counted as a defect.)

defects.defect: The confirmation dialog for the irreversible "Prune empty" bulk deletion states a count derived from the search-FILTERED client list, while the action it guards is an unscoped server-wide mutation. It promises fewer deletions than it performs.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 (emptyCount over the `users` prop) + demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:28 (users = pm.filteredAdminUsers) + demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:29-48 (filtered+sorted) vs demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:190 (pruneEmptyUsers(token) — no scope arg). Probe output: D-filtered {"headerBadge":"6","toolbar":["6 users","· 1 empty"],"renderedRows":1}; D-dialog "Prune 1 empty users?\n\nThis will permanently delete 1 user with 0 palettes and their sessions. This cannot be undone."; D-after POST /admin/users/prune-empty → toolbarAfter ["Pruned 3 users"]. Frame docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/frames-D2/D-confirm-prune-filtered-dark.png. Aggravated by demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:59 listUsers(token, 50) — even unfiltered the number is a 50-row page count. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 ("dangerous confirmation … Actor, scope, provenance and effect remain visible"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:55 PR-11.
defects.mechanism: Truth derived at the wrong altitude: the leaf computes scope from whatever array it was handed instead of receiving the server's scope.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2.mjs (section D). Manually: #/admin/users with an admin token and ≥2 empty users, type a query matching exactly ONE empty user, click "Prune empty", read the dialog, confirm, read the result line.
defects.proposedCure: Confirm against the server's scope, not a client-derived count: the prune affordance resolves the candidate set (GET the empty users), the dialog NAMES the candidates, and the confirmed call carries those identities — the two-phase review anatomy PR-11 already prescribes. Reading the unfiltered array instead only swaps a wrong number for a differently wrong one, because that array is a 50-row page.

defects.defect: A failed destructive mutation renders as a benign, self-contradicting success message. A 500 on the prune endpoint produces "No empty users to prune" while the same toolbar simultaneously reads "· 2 empty". No error surface at all.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:195-198 (catch → return 0) meeting demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-309 (count > 0 ? "Pruned N" : "No empty users to prune"). Probe output with the endpoint fulfilled 500 application/problem+json: {"message":"No empty users to prune","toolbar":["3 users","· 2 empty"],"rowsStillRendered":3,"anyErrorRole":false}. Frame frames-D2/G-prune-FAILED-desktop-light.png. The component already ratified the opposite principle for the LOAD path at AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50 ("error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster") and :51-62 (EmptyState variant="error").
defects.mechanism: The result channel's type cannot express failure: onPruneDone(count: number) collapses {refused} and {nothing to do} into the same integer, so no downstream design can distinguish them.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2d-prune-failure.mjs — intercepts POST **/prune-empty with a 500 and reads the rendered result span.
defects.proposedCure: Widen the result to the three outcomes the action actually has (pruned N / nothing to prune / failed + machine reason) and render failure in the error register already ratified at :51-62. The signature, not the string, is the defect.

defects.defect: The unauthenticated state was never designed. With no admin token the panel renders the TRUE-EMPTY plate — "· roster clear · / No users found." — a positive factual claim about a corpus the app has never queried; and the Refresh button is enabled, named, styled and completely inert.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:55-56 (getAdminToken() null → return before any request) falling through to AdminUsersPanel.vue:63. Probe E: {"token":null,"adminReqsBefore":10,"adminReqsAfterRefreshClick":10,"emptyStateSays":"· ROSTER CLEAR · |  | No users found.","refreshDisabled":false,"pruneDisabled":true} — zero new requests after the click. This is the state in ALL 60 mega-tranche captures: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:128,143,158,173 (text 273/273/122/122, dock reads "Login"). Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 §5.5, :71 §5.6, :52 PR-08.
defects.mechanism: A third state species (signed-out) was folded into an existing one (empty) instead of being designed or subtracted.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users with no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage; click Refresh; observe zero network activity and an unchanged "No users found." Also visible in every shipped audit screenshot at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/*/admin-users.png.
defects.proposedCure: Signed-out is a route-guard species, not a roster species. The admin route should not mount a roster it cannot populate, and the panel should not own a third empty-shaped state. Subtract the state rather than annotate it.

defects.defect: RTL fabricates identifiers. The hand-rolled two-span tail-priority slug split has no bidi isolation, so `empty-ghost-account-aaaa-33` renders on screen as `aaa-33empty-ghost-account-a` — a string that does not exist. The row and its own delete confirmation then display two different identities for the same account.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:97-101 (two sibling spans) + :246-252 (slugHead/slugTail). Probe C under dir=rtl: {"headText":"an-extremely-long-…-2","headL":1010.5,"headR":1194,"tailText":"f9a-33","tailL":950,"tailR":1010.5,"tailRenderedLeftOfHead":true}. Frame frames-D2/C-populated-rtl-desktop.png shows `aaa-33empty-ghost-account-a`, `aaa-77empty-ghost-account-a`, `bbb-11empty-three-b`. The dialog quotes the raw unsplit slug at :169. The count line likewise renders "empty 3 · users 6" (from :8-13). Law verbatim, VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:133 — slug/ID must keep "identical domain meaning inside an LTR-isolated value … no custom bidi reinterpretation"; :154 — "slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose".
defects.mechanism: An identifier composed by string concatenation across two DOM nodes instead of rendered as one typed, direction-isolated value.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2.mjs (section C), or set document.documentElement.dir='rtl' on a populated #/admin/users. Also visible without data in the shipped capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/adminusers.png ("users 0").
defects.proposedCure: Delete the split entirely. Head-elision with a protected tail is one CSS declaration on one LTR-isolated text node (`direction: rtl; text-overflow: ellipsis` inside a `<bdi>`), not two spans and two string functions. That single transposition also removes the viewport-dependent ellipsis gap artefact (390: `empty-ghost-acco…  aaa-33` with a visible inter-token gap; 1440: no gap).

defects.defect: The same number, from the same expression, is rendered twice ~60 px apart: the pane header Badge and the toolbar count line.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:5 (<Badge>{{ adminCount }}</Badge>) with adminCount = pm.adminUsers.value.length at AdminPane.vue:117-122, against AdminUsersPanel.vue:8-10 ({{ totalUsers }} user…) with totalUsers bound to pm.adminUsers.value.length at AdminPane.vue:33. Measured: headerBadgeText "6" / toolbarText "6 users", both fontSize 16.4px. Visible as `Users ⓪` above `0 users` in all four Safari matrices and as `Users ⑥` above `6 users` in frames-D2/A,B,D,F. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:57 PR-13 (total 2→1); :71 §5.6.
defects.mechanism: Duplicated element species — one quantity given two owners.
defects.reproduction: Open any admin/users capture: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png shows both simultaneously.
defects.proposedCure: The count is the header Badge's job. Delete the toolbar count span; the toolbar keeps only the actionable "N empty" scope, which is what the Prune button needs.

defects.defect: Two different denominators are joined by a "·" and read as one sentence: `totalUsers` is unfiltered while `emptyCount` is computed over the filtered list.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:8-13 renders `{{ totalUsers }} users` then `· {{ emptyCount }} empty`; totalUsers ← pm.adminUsers (AdminPane.vue:33), emptyCount ← the filtered `users` prop (AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 + AdminPane.vue:28). Measured under an active search: toolbar ["6 users","· 1 empty"] with renderedRows 1 — neither number describes what is on screen.
defects.mechanism: Same as D-1: scope derived from two different arrays inside one sentence.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2.mjs (section D) — the D-filtered block; or type a query into "Search users…" on a populated roster.
defects.proposedCure: Both quantities must come from the same population, and the population must be the one being displayed. Falls out of the D-1 cure (scope received from the port, not derived in the leaf).

defects.defect: The roster has no columns. The palette-count Badge — the one quantity the surface exists to convey — sits at five distinct x-positions across six rows, and the action cluster starts at two.
defects.evidence: Measured at 1440, identical in light and dark: badge left edges [313.5, 507, 535.5, 293.3, 454.8] (5 distinct x, spread 242.2 px); action-cluster left edges [549.1, 645] (96 px hole opens/closes where the `Palettes` button appears per AdminUsersPanel.vue:112 v-if="user.paletteCount"). Cause: the identity pill is shrink-to-content with max-w-full (:98) and the badge follows it inline (:102-104). Frames frames-D2/A-populated-desktop-light.png and B-populated-mobile-light.png. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:5 (relational proportion) and :73 §5.8 ("Real rendered relation wins over token intent").
defects.mechanism: Row composed as an inline flow rather than a column grammar.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2b-geometry.mjs — prints badgeXs and actsXs per scheme.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the area's review-row anatomy (AdminListItem) and give the quantity a fixed track. The count is scanned vertically; it must live in a column, not after a variable-width chip.

defects.defect: The disclosure has no affordance at rest and none when open. Expandable and inert rows are visually identical, and an opened row's header paint is unchanged.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-90 — role/tabindex/aria-expanded applied only when user.paletteCount, with the only visual signals being cursor:pointer, hover:bg-accent/50 and focus-visible. Measured: interactiveRows 3, inertRows 3 on a 6-row roster. Compare frames-D2/A-populated-desktop-light.png (all closed) with frames-D2/D-expanded-desktop-dark.png (row 1 open) — the header row is treated identically. No chevron, no rotation, no persistent open marker. Aggravated by :236 (expandedUserSlug is a single ref) so opening a second row silently closes the first. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 PR-07 ("Hover-only/unlabeled controls … → ADD-AFFORDANCE"), :70 §5.5.
defects.mechanism: State expressed only in ARIA and in transient pointer states; never painted.
defects.reproduction: Open a populated #/admin/users, screenshot the list, expand a row, screenshot again, diff the header row region — no change. Frames A vs D in frames-D2/ are that pair.
defects.proposedCure: A disclosure needs a persistent mark. Put a native named button on the identity region (see D-9) carrying a rotating chevron, and let expandable-vs-inert be legible at rest.

defects.defect: The row is a `role="button"` div with operable controls nested inside it, so its accessible name becomes the concatenation of the two destructive actions it contains.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-90 (div with role=button/tabindex/aria-expanded) wrapping :112-130 (two <Button>). Two-engine ariaSnapshot, byte-identical in WebKit and Chromium: `- button "mbabb 12 Palettes Delete user mbabb": - text: mbabb 12 - button "Palettes" - button "Delete user mbabb"`. Chromium full tab order (Full Keyboard Access on): … → DIV(role=button "mbabb12 Palettes") → BUTTON "Palettes" → BUTTON "Delete user mbabb" → … . Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 — "One native <button type=\"button\"> spans its specimen/identity region"; the card body owns no expand path.
defects.mechanism: Container-as-widget: the interactive role was placed on the row instead of on the identity region, so the widget's name absorbs its children's labels.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2c-a11y-two-engine.mjs — runs both engines and prints the ariaSnapshot plus the tab order.
defects.proposedCure: Move the disclosure to a native <button type="button"> spanning pill + count only, leaving the action cluster as its sibling. That fixes the name, removes the need for the manual keydown handler at :344-350, and removes the tabindex/role pair from the div.

defects.defect: Two irreversible actions of different scope share the same Trash2 glyph six pixels apart; the only differentiator names the object ("Palettes") rather than the verb (nothing says delete).
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:106-131 — `gap-1.5` (6 px) between a `🗑 Palettes` button (:112-121, deletes ALL the user's palettes) and a bare `🗑` (:122-130, deletes the user). Measured at 390: 82×36 and 28×36, cluster 116 px = 36% of a 324 px row against 133 px for identity. Frame frames-D2/B-populated-mobile-light.png. The W5-12/F-8 comment at :107-111 claims this family was cured; it cured the COLOUR (measured resting ink rgb(91,70,51) light / rgb(213,208,200) dark — correctly quiet) but not the COUNT: frame A shows six resting trash glyphs plus three inside the Palettes buttons on a six-row roster. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 PR-06.
defects.mechanism: Two action species of different scope given identical material and adjacency instead of one owner with a scope choice.
defects.reproduction: Load a populated #/admin/users at 390 (probe-D2.mjs section B) and read the action cluster; the button rects are printed in the probe log.
defects.proposedCure: One destructive owner per row. Scope ("this user's palettes" vs "this user") is chosen inside that one control's confirmation, not by aiming a thumb at one of two identical 28 px glyphs.

defects.defect: The prune result beat is a flex sibling of the two toolbar buttons inside a wrapping row, so its entry displaces both live controls by 105 px downward — the destructive button the user just released moves under the pointer as the acknowledgement of the action.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:16-20 (<Transition name="vj-celebrate"> span) inside the `flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap` toolbar at :4. Measured at 390 before/after one successful prune: Prune empty y 274.1 → 379.1; Refresh y 318.1 → 423.1 (both +105.0 px). Frame frames-D2/F-prune-result-mobile.png. Same measurement shows the toolbar is already ragged BEFORE any animation — Prune right-aligned on line 1 (x 249.1), Refresh orphaned at the left margin of line 2 (x 33) — the product of `<div class="flex-1" />` at :14 plus flex-wrap. Motion-law status, stated precisely: the transition IS tokenized (demo/styles/animations.css:142-165) and IS neutralised under prefers-reduced-motion (animations.css:184-192); the 105 px reflow is not a transition, so the guard does not reach it. Register defect on the same line: the celebration (:17 text-mono-small text-muted-foreground italic) and the persistent count (:8 text-mono-small text-muted-foreground) speak in one voice separated only by italics.
defects.mechanism: An ephemeral result message given layout participation in the same flex line as the persistent controls.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2.mjs (section F) — prints button x/y before and after one confirmed prune at 390.
defects.proposedCure: The result beat must not participate in the toolbar's layout. Either overlay it (absolute/grid-stacked in a reserved slot) or move it to the panel's designated status region. glass-ui 7.0.0 already exports ./toast; a hand-rolled 3-second self-clearing span inside a wrapping flex row is a toast that forgot it was one.

defects.defect: The area's ratified review-row primitive is bypassed and the cure it carries was not copied: the hand-rolled row's grid item has min-width:auto — the exact condition AdminListItem exists to prevent — masked by overflow:hidden.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue is the row anatomy, consumed by AdminNamesPanel.vue:44,94; AdminListSkeleton.vue:4 states the skeleton is "shaped as the AdminListItem row grammar" — so AdminUsersPanel's loading state (:46-48) is shaped like a row it never renders. AdminListItem.vue:6-11 documents the S.W5-12/F-1 cure: "min-w-0 on the ROW ITSELF … blowing the track to ~850px at 390". Measured on the live hand-rolled row: wrapperComputedMinWidth "auto", wrapperOverflow "hidden" (AdminUsersPanel.vue:68), rowComputedMinWidth "0px". No overflow today (scrollW 390 = clientW 390) only because line 68 clips. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 ("one review-row anatomy").
defects.mechanism: Copy-paste divergence from a shared primitive: the fix landed on the primitive and never reached the copy.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2b-geometry.mjs (prints wrapperComputedMinWidth/wrapperOverflow), and diff AdminUsersPanel.vue:64-90 against AdminListItem.vue:12-22.
defects.proposedCure: Consume AdminListItem for the header row (swatch/content/actions slots already match this row's three zones). That single move also lands D-7's column grammar and removes the divergence permanently.

defects.defect: The destructive confirmation is rendered on the most transparent material in the app — the pane behind reads through the copy — and the only container-shaped affordance in the modal is the irreversible action, because Cancel is emphasis="text" and the close X is suppressed.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:159 (DialogContent surface="glass" :show-close="false"), :174 (Button emphasis="text" Cancel), :175-178 (tone="destructive" solid red Prune). Frame frames-D2/D-confirm-prune-filtered-dark.png: the search field's "aaaa-33", the "Start a new palette" card and the row being deleted are all legible through the confirmation text. Title grammar bug in the same frame: "Prune 1 empty users?" (:290 has no plural guard, :291 does). Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 ("dangerous confirmation"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 §5.6.
defects.mechanism: Weight order inverted — the recoverable path is given the least visual availability, on the least legible surface.
defects.reproduction: Trigger any confirm on a populated #/admin/users (probe-D2.mjs section D) and read the frame.
defects.proposedCure: A confirmation for an irreversible action is not a glass surface. Use the opaque dialog material and give Cancel a real container; the destructive action earns its colour, not its monopoly on being button-shaped.

defects.defect: The sort menu offers a key the row refuses to display: sorting by "newest" (createdAt) reorders six rows that show only slug and count, so the resulting order has no visible cause.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:36-46 sorts by slug | newest (createdAt) | palettes; UserSortMenu is mounted at AdminPane.vue:17-21. The row renders slug + count only (AdminUsersPanel.vue:91-105). createdAt and status are on the User model and are consumed by the sort; neither reaches the row. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 — "Actor, scope, provenance and effect remain visible."
defects.mechanism: An ordering control whose key has no rendered column.
defects.reproduction: On a populated #/admin/users, open the sort menu in the search bar and switch between "newest" and "slug"; the row order changes with nothing on screen accounting for it.
defects.proposedCure: Either render the provenance the sort acts on (createdAt in the row's provenance rung) or drop the key. A sort with no visible column is an unfalsifiable ordering.

defects.defect: The row's identity chip is painted in the live picked accent — a variable carrying zero information about the row — and wears operable-chrome material, so the one element in the row that looks interactive is the only one that is not.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:99 and :168 — :style="{ color: safeAccent, borderColor: safeAccent }" with safeAccent injected from SAFE_ACCENT_KEY (the live picked colour). Measured across two boots of the identical roster: oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2) (gold) in one, crimson in frames captured minutes earlier. Material: measured pill = Fira Code / 16.4px / weight 700 / accent fill + accent border + pill radius; the real operable controls beside it are neutral glass at rgb(0,0,0) light / rgb(255,255,255) dark. demo/styles/foundation.css:746 groups .slug-pill with [role="tab"] and .glass-resting for the operable-chrome border-weight bump. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 §5.5, :74 §5.9, :78 §5.13 (slug = provenance = text-mono-small).
defects.mechanism: Decoration keyed to an unrelated variable, wearing the design system's interactive material.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2b-geometry.mjs prints the pill's computed color/border/weight per scheme; compare frames-D2/A (crimson pills) with the probe-D2b measurement (gold) on the identical roster.
defects.proposedCure: A slug is provenance. Render it in the provenance rung with the provenance material (mono-small, neutral ink, no border, no accent) and let the accent stay where it means something. That also frees the interactive material for the disclosure that currently has none (D-8).

defects.defect: Physical-direction margin inside a bidi-bearing row: `mr-1` on the Trash icon puts the gap on the wrong side under RTL while the surrounding layout is logical.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:119 — <Trash2 class="w-3 h-3 mr-1" />. Frame frames-D2/C-populated-rtl-desktop.png shows the icon trailing the word "Palettes" with the gap mirrored wrongly.
defects.mechanism: One physical property in an otherwise logical layout.
defects.reproduction: Set dir=rtl on a populated #/admin/users (probe-D2.mjs section C) and inspect the Palettes button.
defects.proposedCure: Use the logical `me-1`, or better, let the Button's own icon gap own the spacing — a per-instance margin on an icon inside a design-system Button is a per-instance override of a root that already handles it.

defects.defect: Nested housing: three boundary levels around one palette — pane Card → per-row bordered box → PaletteCard — and the route still renders the 50% "My Palettes" companion the constitution ordered removed.
defects.evidence: Measured resting border chain outward from a row: DIV.rounded-md.border.border-card-edge (AdminUsersPanel.vue:68) → DIV.glass-resting.card.rounded-card. Expanding adds border-t (:134) and seats full PaletteCards inside (:140-151). Frame frames-D2/D-expanded-desktop-dark.png. Companion visible in every capture and every probe frame. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:48 PR-04 ("Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE"; "Admin companion 50%→0"), :66 §5.1; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 ("Each Admin route uses the full main width").
defects.mechanism: A padding group promoted to a Card, repeated per row, inside another Card.
defects.reproduction: probe-D2.mjs section A prints borderChain; frames A and D show it.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the per-row border and let interval plus the row's own material express grouping (PROPORTION §5.4: a divider survives only when grouping would otherwise be ambiguous). The companion removal is AdminPane/route-level and is PR-04's owner W18, but this row anatomy is currently designing for 640 px it should not have.

defects.defect: Encapsulation inverted: the leaf owns the expanded-palettes list and the port reaches in through three imperative mutators plus a completion callback; and the leaf hand-rolls an imperative modal driver plus a toast that the design system already ships.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 defineExpose({ removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes }) over state owned at :237; consumers at demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:95,117,132,146 and demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:121-123. Six confirm refs plus a callback-in-a-ref at :255-261. glass-ui 7.0.0 exports ./data-table and ./toast (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json, version 7.0.0); neither is consumed anywhere in demo/. Owner edicts 1 and 4.
defects.mechanism: State parked below its owner, forcing an imperative back-channel; and design-system primitives reimplemented locally.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'adminUsersPanelRef.value?' demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts (4 call sites); python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json'));print(d['version']);print([k for k in d['exports'] if 'table' in k or 'toast' in k])".
defects.proposedCure: Move userPalettes to the port that already owns every other list on this route and render props; the three mutators and the ref plumbing disappear. Consume glass-ui's data-table/toast rather than reimplementing them in a leaf.

defects.defect: Two hygiene items: an uncleared 3-second timeout on the result message, and the only file in demo/ that imports the built-in Transition component.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:308 — setTimeout(() => { pruneResult.value = null; }, 3000) with no handle and no cleanup: two prunes inside 3 s truncate the first message, and an unmount inside 3 s writes to a dead ref. AdminUsersPanel.vue:186 imports Transition from "vue"; measured `grep -rl "<Transition" demo | wc -l` → 19 and `grep -rl 'Transition[ ,}].*from "vue"' demo | wc -l` → 1. Owner edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance).
defects.mechanism: Local bookkeeping that the framework/compiler already owns.
defects.reproduction: Run the two greps above; for the timer, click Prune twice within 3 s on a populated roster and watch the first message vanish early.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the Transition import (the compiler resolves built-ins). The timer disappears entirely with the D-2/D-11 cure, since the result stops being a self-clearing span in the toolbar.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue (races, unguarded async, error paths, cleanup, reactivity, a11y-as-implementation, boundary values, test truth)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]`, observed as declared at spawn, not inherited or undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 `toggleUserExpand` awaits a per-user palette fetch with NO request-generation guard, so a slow response for user A lands in the OPEN disclosure of user B. Reproduced in chromium AND webkit (probe-impl-c3.json: RACE_REPRODUCED true both engines; beta's row `aria-expanded=true` renders "ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA"). Because :150 binds the card's admin delete to the ROW's slug (`emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)`), the follow-on click destroys the wrong owner's data: probe-impl-c3b.json captures `DELETE /admin/palettes/alpha-p-1` issued from beta-drifter-0002's row, beta's badge 2→1 and alpha's stuck at 4 while alpha actually has 3.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as measured negatives so the next seat does not re-spend budget: (1) This component contributes ZERO to the visual REPORT's tap-target and nameless-button counts — probe-impl.json C7_mobile at 390x844, both engines: `under24: []` across 10 visible buttons, zero nameless, docScrollW 390 == innerW 390 (no horizontal overflow); the 4 smallTapTargets REPORT.json charges to /#/admin/users (results[9]) are all dock controls (Switch to slug 22x22, Generate new slug 22x22, Cancel 22x22, a 160x23 input). (2) Every named local hazard is absent: grep over the file gives defineModel 0, ValueUnit 0, parseCssColor 0, requestAnimationFrame 0, addEventListener 0, Observer 0, setInterval 0, WebGL 0 — the PRM-RAF epidemic has no site here. (3) No unbounded growth or leaked handles: `userPalettes` is replaced wholesale at :361/:368/:375, never appended; `confirmAction` is overwritten per showConfirm; the file's only scheduled work is the single setTimeout at :308. (4) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — :199 `import type { Palette, User }` is the only type-only import and is correctly marked. (5) The keydown guard at :344-350 (`e.target !== e.currentTarget`) is genuinely load-bearing and correct. (6) My own hypothesis C-14 (prune receipt swallowed by the `?.` handle on sub-view change) was REFUTED by measurement, with a control proving the navigation was real.

defects.defect: Concurrent-expand race: `toggleUserExpand` writes `userPalettes` from an awaited fetch with no request-generation guard, so a late response for user A renders inside user B's open disclosure — and the admin delete then destroys A's palette while decrementing B's count.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 (`userPalettes.value = await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)`; `finally` clears loading first-to-settle) and :150 (`@admin-delete="emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)"`). probe-impl-c3.json, BOTH engines identical: `t_betaSettled: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "BETA-PALETTE-BBB 2 0"}` then `t_alphaLanded: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA 2 0"}`, `RACE_REPRODUCED: true`. probe-impl-c3b.json: `deleteRequests: ["http://localhost:9077/admin/palettes/alpha-p-1"]`, `VERDICT: {betaBadgeBefore:"2", betaBadgeAfter:"1", alphaBadgeBefore:"4", alphaBadgeAfter:"4"}`. useAdminUsers.ts:118-121 decrements the owner passed by the row. Frames: frames-impl/C3b-{chromium,webkit}-beta-shows-alpha.png.
defects.mechanism: Value not bound to its key — `expandedUserSlug` and `userPalettes` are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order; nothing records which request a resolved value belongs to.
defects.reproduction: VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9077 npx vite --port 9077 ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c3.mjs (race, 2 engines) ; node .../probe-impl-c3b.mjs (the destroying DELETE + badge deltas). Serve alpha's /admin/users/*/palettes with 1500ms delay and beta's with 40ms; click alpha, wait 300ms, click beta.
defects.proposedCure: Do not add a sequence counter to the current shape — the shape is the defect. Express the disclosure as the keyed resource it is: a colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` driven by `watch(slugRef, …)` with an AbortController cancelled on key change, returning `{ palettes, loading, error }` bound to the key they were fetched for. A response for a stale key then has nowhere to land — the race becomes unrepresentable rather than policed. Side effects: supplies C-4's missing `error` cell, and removes userPalettes/removeUserPalette/updatePaletteTier/clearUserPalettes from the :389 defineExpose (the adjudicated L-1/L-2 inversion) as a consequence rather than as separate work.

defects.defect: The prune confirmation quotes a SEARCH-FILTERED count while `POST /admin/users/prune-empty` destroys every empty user in the corpus; the Prune button's enablement is wrong in both directions from the same source.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter((u) => !(u.paletteCount ?? 0)).length)` over the FILTERED prop (AdminPane.vue:28 `:users="pm.filteredAdminUsers.value"`, filter at useAdminUsers.ts:30-34); :288-299 composes the copy from `emptyCount.value`; demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69 `pruneEmptyUsers(token)` takes no filter/body/slug-list. probe-impl.json, BOTH engines: fixture has 3 empty users, search "gamma" → `C2_pruneDialog: "Prune 1 empty users? This will permanently delete 1 user with 0 palettes and their sessions. This cannot be undone."`. Inverse, search "alpha": `C2_filteredNoEmpty.toolbar = [{Prune empty, disabled: true}, …]` while 3 empty users exist. probe-impl-c8.json at scale: 137-user roster → dialog promises 10.
defects.mechanism: A destructive action's stated scope and its gate are derived from a client-side view filter while its effect is global — the describing authority and the executing authority are different.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl.mjs (cells C2_unfiltered / C2_filtered / C2_pruneDialog / C2_filteredNoEmpty). Frames: frames-impl/C2-{chromium,webkit}-prune-dialog-filtered.png.
defects.proposedCure: A destructive action's stated scope must come from the authority that executes it: either the server answers a preview (`GET /admin/users/prune-empty` → `{count}`) that the dialog quotes and the button gates on, or the client sends the explicit slug list it just described. Renaming the computed or passing the unfiltered array does not fix the split; the description and the effect must be the same query. (Riders visible in the same pasted string: the title never pluralises — "Prune 1 empty users?" — while the description does.)

defects.defect: The roster prints a total it never measured and offers no second page: `res.total` is discarded, `listUsers(token, 50)` is the only request ever issued, and `data.length` is labelled "N users".
defects.evidence: useAdminUsers.ts:59-60 (`const res = await listUsers(token, 50); adminUsers.value = res.data;` — `res.total` unread); AdminPane.vue:31 `:total-users="pm.adminUsers.value.length"`; panel :8-10. probe-impl-c8.json with server `{data: 50 rows, total: 137}`: `listRequests: ["…/admin/users?limit=50&offset=0"]`, `read.countLine: "50 users"`, `read.headerBadge: "50"`, `read.paginationControls: []`, `VERDICT.unreachableUsers: 87`. Sibling contrast: useAdminAudit.ts:62 and useAdminFlagged.ts:70 both consume `res.total`; AdminAuditPanel.vue:83 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126 both mount PaginationBar; PaginationBar.vue sits UNUSED in this component's own directory.
defects.mechanism: A page size presented as a population — the count is sourced from the returned array while the label claims the corpus.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c8.mjs — serves total:137 / data:50 and reads the console's claim. Frame: frames-impl/C8-pagination-and-prune.png.
defects.proposedCure: Consume `res.total`, thread limit/offset through the existing composable, and mount the `PaginationBar.vue` that already exists two files away — matching the two sibling admin panels exactly. No new component, no new directory (KISS).

defects.defect: A failed disclosure fetch costumes as an empty palette set: `loadUserPalettes` returns `[]` on any error and the panel has no error branch for the expanded region — in the same file whose comment forbids exactly this for the roster.
defects.evidence: useAdminUsers.ts:154-161 (`catch (e: any) { console.warn(…); return []; }`); AdminUsersPanel.vue:135-138 has only loading→empty (the roster's own error path exists at :51-62); the file's stated invariant at :49-50 — "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster." probe-impl.json C4, BOTH engines, disclosure endpoint 500: `{disclosureText: "· NONE PINNED · No palettes.", saysNoPalettes: true, saysUnreachableOrError: false, hasRetryButton: false}` with `consoleErrors: ["Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 …"]`.
defects.mechanism: Failure and emptiness collapse to the same value (`[]`) at the composable boundary, so the view cannot distinguish them.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl.mjs (cell C4_failedDisclosure). Frames: frames-impl/C4-{chromium,webkit}-failed-disclosure.png. Note the row's badge still reads the true count two lines above the "No palettes." plate.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of C-1's cure at zero extra cost: the keyed-resource composable returns `{ palettes, loading, error }`, and the disclosure renders the identical `EmptyState variant="error"` + Retry pair already present at :51-62. Model the three states as a discriminated union so "empty" cannot be written in the error state.

defects.defect: "0 users" is printed above "The roster is unreachable." — the file's own A-3 invariant is guarded on `loading` only, so the self-contradiction it names is reintroduced verbatim in the error state, in two files.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:5-10 — the comment says the count "speaks only once the roster resolves" but the guard is `v-if="!loading"`; AdminPane.vue:118-121 guards `adminCount` on `pm.loadingUsers` alone. probe-impl.json C1, users endpoint 500, BOTH engines byte-identical: `mainText: "Users 0 Manage accounts and permissions. 0 users Prune empty Refresh The roster is unreachable. Internal Server Error Retry …"`, `countLine: "0 users"`, `hasUnreachable: true`, `rowsRendered: 0`, `toolbar: [{Prune empty, disabled:true},{Refresh, disabled:false}]`. Independently corroborated by the sibling seat's own probe-populated.json `.error.text`.
defects.mechanism: Four roster states (unresolved/loading/error/resolved) modelled as three independent booleans plus a nullable string, which permits the count to exist inside the error state.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl.mjs (cell C1_errorState). Frames: frames-impl/C1-{chromium,webkit}-error-toolbar.png.
defects.proposedCure: Not `&& !loadError` bolted onto two v-ifs. Return a discriminated union from the composable so `count` is a member of the RESOLVED variant only; both consumers (panel toolbar and pane header badge) then become incapable of printing a count they do not have, and the invariant is enforced by construction rather than by two comments.

defects.defect: Every user row is a `role="button"` containing two focusable descendants (nested-interactive, WCAG 4.1.2), carries no `aria-controls` for the region it discloses, and computes its accessible name from contents so it absorbs the destructive button's label.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-89 (role/tabindex/aria-expanded on the row div) with the action cluster at :106-131 INSIDE it. probe-impl.json C5_a11y, BOTH engines identical: every row `{"focusableDescendants": 2, "descendantLabels": ["Palettes", "Delete user beta-drifter-0002"], "ariaControls": null, "accName": "beta-drifte r-0002 2 Palettes"}`. Structural DOM fact, reproduced in chromium and webkit, independent of macOS Full Keyboard Access (MT-F022 does not absorb it).
defects.mechanism: The disclosure affordance was implemented as the whole row (per the :70-77 premise "there is NO other keyboard path") rather than as a dedicated control, forcing interactive content to nest inside a button role.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl.mjs (cell C5_a11y.rows). Also directly checkable with axe's `nested-interactive` rule against #/admin/users with a populated roster.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the disclosure onto a real sibling `<button>` (a chevron carrying its own accessible name plus `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at an id'd region), leaving the row a plain container. This is exactly the `interactive` prop the adjudicated MT-AU1 scope already moves into AdminListItem.vue — it must carry the CORRECTED shape, not the current one, or the wave hardens the defect into the shared atom.

defects.defect: The only receipt for the app's most destructive bulk action is announced to no one, and a second action's message is truncated by the first's uncancelled timer.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:16-20 (bare `<span>`, no role/aria-live) and :303-309 (`setTimeout(…, 3000)` with no handle, never cleared; `grep -c onUnmounted` on the file = 0). probe-impl.json BOTH engines: `C5_beatLiveRegion: []` (zero live regions contain the beat text) and `C5_a11y.liveRegions` within <main> = 1, belonging to the OTHER pane. Double-beat timing, chromium: beat1 at ≈t0+900ms, beat2 set at t0+2332ms, message present at t0+3350 and NULL at t0+4300 — beat2 died ≈1000ms before its own 3000ms window (t0+5332); webkit identical shape (beat2 at t0+2045). Sibling contrast in the same directory: PaginationBar.vue:17 `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, AdminTagsPanel.vue:54 `role="status"`, AdminListSkeleton.vue:10 `role="status"` rendered v-for="i in 3" at :47 — loading is announced three times over while the destruction result is announced zero times.
defects.mechanism: An action-result beat rebuilt inline without its announcement or its cancellation, while the correct atom already exists elsewhere in the tree.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl.mjs (cells C5_doubleBeat and C5_beatLiveRegion), prune stubbed to {pruned: 0} so the button stays enabled for a second beat inside the first's dismissal window.
defects.proposedCure: Move the existing ActionFeedback.vue atom (which already does clearTimeout-before-re-arm correctly) to demo/shared/ui/ and give it the `onUnmounted` teardown it lacks (`grep -c onUnmounted demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue` = 0) plus `role="status"`, then consume it here. Never re-author the beat inline; twelve consumers otherwise inherit the same hole.

defects.defect: One malformed row denies the entire admin console: `slugHead`/`slugTail` call `.length`/`.slice` unguarded inside the v-for, so a single non-string slug throws and the ErrorBoundary replaces the whole panel with a raw, engine-divergent JS error string.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:247-252 (`function slugHead(slug: string) { return slug.length > SLUG_TAIL ? … }`). probe-impl-c10.json, one row with `slug: null`, BOTH engines: chromium `{alert: true, rows: 0, bodyLen: 125, mainText: "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length') Try again", deleteLabels: []}`; webkit `{alert: true, rows: 0, bodyLen: 118, "null is not an object (evaluating 'slug.length')"}`. The repo already documents this crash class at e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:100-135; the boundary (demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue) catches it, which is exactly the problem — roster, Prune, Refresh and every delete disappear together.
defects.mechanism: Zero row-level tolerance: the component has no non-string arm, so the whole-panel boundary IS its error handling.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c10.mjs (case nullSlug). Frames: frames-impl/C10-{chromium,webkit}-nullSlug.png.
defects.proposedCure: The crash belongs to the component, not the boundary. Validate at the transport/composable seam: a row whose slug is not a string is a row the panel does not render (or renders as a flagged, non-actionable row), so a single bad record degrades one row instead of the console. The ErrorBoundary stays as last resort, not as the design — and it must never leak a raw engine string to an operator.

defects.defect: An empty slug produces a destructive control whose accessible name is literally "Delete user " and a confirmation dialog whose identifying pill renders empty.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:126 `:aria-label="`Delete user ${user.slug}`"`, :97-101 (slug pill; slugHead("")→"", slugTail("")→""), :165-169 (the same pill in the confirm dialog). probe-impl-c10.json, case emptySlug, BOTH engines: `deleteLabels: ["Sort users", "Delete user "]`, `rows: 1`, `interactiveRows: 1`, `alert: false` — it renders and is fully operable. Not caught by the e2e a11y battery's accessible-name leg, which tests for emptiness of the name, not for identifying content within it.
defects.mechanism: Template interpolation of an unvalidated field directly into a destructive control's accessible name and into the confirmation's only identifier.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c10.mjs (case emptySlug).
defects.proposedCure: Same seam as C-8 — validate the row at the composable boundary so an unidentifiable user never reaches a destructive affordance. A confirmation that cannot name its target must not be offerable.

defects.defect: Raw `paletteCount` truthiness leaks domain-boundary values into interaction and layout: -1 makes the row a live disclosure and offers "delete all palettes" for a user with none; MAX_SAFE_INTEGER renders unformatted into a two-digit Badge.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:81/:87/:112 branch on raw `user.paletteCount`; :103 prints `user.paletteCount ?? 0`; :241 counts `!(u.paletteCount ?? 0)`. probe-impl-c10.json, BOTH engines: negativeCount → badge "-1", `interactiveRows: 1`, delete-palettes offered, NOT counted as empty; hugeCount → badge "9007199254740991", row interactive.
defects.mechanism: JS truthiness used as a domain predicate — every non-zero value, including negatives and absurd magnitudes, reads as "has palettes".
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c10.mjs (cases negativeCount, hugeCount).
defects.proposedCure: Express the predicate once, at the boundary, as `paletteCount > 0` on a validated non-negative integer, and let the row shape follow from that single derived flag rather than from three independent truthiness reads.

defects.defect: Duplicate slugs collide in the `v-for` key and in the expansion state: two rows key on the same value, both carry the identical destructive label, and expanding either opens both disclosures over one fetch.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:67 `:key="user.slug"` and :134 `v-if="expandedUserSlug === user.slug"`. probe-impl-c10.json, case duplicateSlugs, BOTH engines: `rows: 2`, `interactiveRows: 2`, `deleteLabels: ["Sort users", "Delete user dupe-0001", "Delete user dupe-0001"]`.
defects.mechanism: A server-side uniqueness invariant used as a client-side identity without verification; the same string serves as render key and as expansion state.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c10.mjs (case duplicateSlugs). The both-open consequence is certain by inspection of :134 rather than separately measured — labelled as such.
defects.proposedCure: Same boundary validation as C-8/C-9. Listed because :67 has a naturally unique alternative at hand and because C-8 establishes that this component's current answer to a contract violation is to die.

defects.defect: Test truth: the vitest tier cannot mount ANY component in this repo, and the three e2e specs that touch this panel would stay green through nearly every defect above.
defects.evidence: `grep -c 'plugin-vue\|plugins' vitest.config.ts` → 0 (no plugins key at all, so .vue is untransformable under `npm test`); `grep -rn 'from ".*\.vue"' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` → 0 across `find test demo/test -name '*.ts' | wc -l` → 25 files; `grep -rln '@vue/test-utils' test/ demo/test/ e2e/` → no output (devDependency ^2.4.10 with zero importers, alongside jsdom ^26.1.0); `grep -rln 'AdminUsers\|prune' test/ demo/test/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: Vacuous gate — the assertions that exist are orthogonal to the behaviour that matters, and the tier that could assert it is structurally disabled.
defects.reproduction: Named mutation that keeps every gate GREEN: replace AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter((u) => !(u.paletteCount ?? 0)).length);` with `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.length);` — the panel then offers "Prune 5 empty users?" for a five-user roster and prunes globally, while e2e/smoke/admin/flows/user-status.spec.ts (asserts only that DELETE /admin/users/<slug> fires), both a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts battery tests (assert nameless==[] and undersized==[], both already true — see negative proof), the BR-9 keyboard test and the U-F58 boundary test all pass. The same immunity covers C-1, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6 and C-7. Note also `expect(report.controlsChecked).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — the spec's own guard against an empty-scope false green — is satisfied by the toolbar's Prune/Refresh/Sort buttons with ZERO user rows present.
defects.proposedCure: Give vitest a vue plugin (`plugins: [vue()]` in vitest.config.ts) so the already-installed @vue/test-utils + jsdom can mount SFCs, then gate the behaviours no browser cheaply reaches: (i) a prune whose transport throws must not render success-family copy; (ii) a second action-result survives its own full dismissal window; (iii) a late palette response for a stale key does not render; (iv) a failed disclosure renders the error plate, not the empty one; (v) no count is rendered while loadError is set. Structure first where possible (C-1/C-4/C-5's discriminated union make three of these unrepresentable); tests only for what structure cannot forbid.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the byte-exact export contract (`demo/palettes/export/`, 12 modules, V.W51, PALETTE-CONTRACT Appendix W51) ships to nobody: its ONLY consumer is `demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23`. BrowsePane's live export (`BrowsePane.vue:324` → `usePaletteExport.ts:9` → `demo/palettes/export.ts`) is the pre-contract implementation, which the new barrel names as legacy in its own header (`export/serializers.ts:6-9`). Two implementations of one concept, deliberately kept from colliding by filename; the tested path is dead and the shipping path is untested. The dead path is also the only one that dogfoods value.js (`export/png.ts:11` imports `@mkbabb/value.js/color`; the live path touches the library not at all).
result.negativeProof: The axis the brief guessed at is CLEAN and I prove it: the demo does NOT deep-import `src/`. Every value.js specifier in BrowsePane's 82-module runtime graph is a published `package.json#exports` subpath — `@mkbabb/value.js/color` (color-utils.ts:1, generate-color.ts:33, ink.ts:7, picker-color.ts:27, mix.ts:14, export/png.ts:11) and `@mkbabb/value.js/css` (generate-color.ts:34, ink.ts:11, picker-color.ts:34). `grep -rn '"@src/|\.\./\.\./src/|value\.js/dist' demo` returns 0. Two structural mechanisms make the violation unauthorable rather than merely absent: `vite.config.ts:37-50` GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` as anchored `^…$` regexes (so an alias cannot drift from the export map, and the bare `.` entry cannot prefix-swallow a subpath — the R-era boot break), and `tsconfig.demo.json` carries no `@src/*` path. That mechanism should survive any restructure verbatim.

defects.defect: The V.W51 byte-exact export contract (demo/palettes/export/, 12 modules) is dead in production — only a test consumes it — while BrowsePane's live export routes through the pre-contract demo/palettes/export.ts. Dual path where the tested implementation ships nothing and the shipping implementation has no byte test.
defects.evidence: $ grep -rn "export/serializers" demo src test → demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23 (ONLY hit). $ grep -rn 'from "./export"' demo → demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:9 (ONLY hit). BrowsePane.vue:198,324 imports/calls usePaletteExport. demo/palettes/export/serializers.ts:6-9 names its rival: "the sibling legacy `../export.ts` (the pre-contract routed seat that W50 will replace) still resolves `./export`". export/png.ts:11 imports @mkbabb/value.js/color; export.ts:85-119 uses SVG→Image→canvas and imports no value.js.
defects.mechanism: dual-path / ownership-duplication: one concept (palette export) with two live homes, kept from colliding by filename rather than by deletion; the contract-backed home has zero production consumers so its test is a false proof.
defects.reproduction:
grep -rn "export/serializers" demo src test  # → 1 hit, a test file
grep -rn 'from "./export"' demo             # → 1 hit, usePaletteExport.ts:9
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/palettes/export.ts and demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts. onExport becomes: build an ExportSnapshot from the Palette, then serializeJson|Css|Tailwind|Svg|Png + filenameFor/mimeFor from export/canonical.ts. The download side-effect moves to export/download.ts. One home, and the existing byte test then guards shipping code.

defects.defect: Three slugifiers for one concept, with measured behavioural divergence on every non-ASCII input — and the W51 contract explicitly states no slugifier should exist at that layer.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/utils.ts:3-12 (NFKD normalize + combining-mark strip); demo/palettes/export.ts:9-11 (no normalize); demo/palettes/export/canonical.ts:51-58 identifierPrefix — comment line 51: "The prefix already satisfies the token grammar; no slugifier exists." Measured (both fns extracted verbatim and run in node): "Ångström Blues" → utils "angstrom-blues" vs export.ts "ngstr-m-blues"; "Café Noir" → "cafe-noir" vs "caf-noir"; "Müller-Röhm 2" → "muller-rohm-2" vs "m-ller-r-hm-2"; "naïve  palette" → "naive-palette" vs "na-ve-palette"; "日本 sunset" → "-sunset" vs "sunset"; "A—B" → "ab" vs "a-b". 6 of 6 disagree.
defects.mechanism: ownership-duplication: identifier derivation has no unique home, so the stored slug and the exported filename are derived by different rules and diverge.
defects.reproduction: node -e 'const a=s=>s.normalize("NFKD").replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g,"").trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9 -]/g,"").replace(/\s+/g,"-").replace(/-+/g,"-"); const b=s=>s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,"-").replace(/(^-|-$)/g,""); for(const c of ["Café Noir","Ångström Blues","Müller-Röhm 2"]) console.log(c, a(c), b(c));'

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a pure alias layer — 19 directories, each one file, each a single re-export of @mkbabb/glass-ui — and BrowsePane reaches the design system through BOTH the shim and the real specifier inside one 20-line import block.

defects.defect: The published package has no root export — `import … from "@mkbabb/value.js"` throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED — yet a live source comment and a shipped doc both assert/document that root barrel.

defects.defect: The BROWSE_PORT_KEY injection Symbol lives inside the PROVIDER module, so a leaf pane importing one Symbol drags 20 unrelated modules — the entire admin composable set, slug migration, and the whole platform/auth stack — into its runtime graph. The correct leaf-keys pattern already exists one directory over and BrowsePane uses it on the very next line.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:182 `import { BROWSE_PORT_KEY } from "./usePalettePorts"` (runtime edge) vs BrowsePane.vue:183 `import { CSS_COLOR_KEY } from "../color-session/keys"` (a leaf module with type-only imports). usePalettePorts.ts:4-19 imports 15 composables. Measured with a type-edge-erasing import tracer: full graph from BrowsePane.vue = 82 modules; with the usePalettePorts edge cut = 62; dropped = 20 (useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useAdminUsers, useColorNameQueue, useSlugMigration, usePaletteStore, usePaletteActions, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit, useBrowsePalettes, useFilteredList, usePalettePorts, platform/auth/{useAdminAuth,useSession,useUserAuth,sessions,sessionToken}, platform/storage/useSafeStorage, platform/transport/api-problem). demo/palettes has no keys.ts.
defects.mechanism: wrong direction of dependency: consumer → provider. Keys and port types belong in a leaf that both consumer and provider import; instead the consumer imports the assembly.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/trace3.mjs   # prints 82 / 62 / the 20-module drop list
defects.proposedCure: Create demo/palettes/keys.ts holding the five InjectionKeys plus the five port TYPES (type-only imports from the composables — type edges compile away). usePalettePorts imports keys.ts to provide(); every consumer imports keys + types only. Direction restored: consumers → keys ← provider, mirroring demo/color-session/keys.ts exactly.

defects.defect: The five-port refactor renamed the god facade instead of dissolving it: three port members are whole sub-composable objects, one of which hands the unauthenticated public Browse pane the 16-member ADMIN moderation surface so it can call one user-facing verb.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:22-31 states the thesis ("FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports… no consumer injects a member outside the port it named"). usePalettePorts.ts:189-191 exposes `versions`, `tagEdit`, `flagged` — the raw returns of useVersionHistory (8 members), useTagEdit (5), useAdminFlagged (16). useAdminFlagged.ts:22-43 declares dismiss/deletePalette/loadFlagged/nextPage/prevPage etc., all gated on getToken() from useAdminAuth; only `report` (:118, "User-facing flag/report — no admin token required") is public. BrowsePane consumes exactly: pm.flagged.report (:298), pm.tagEdit.allTags (:218), pm.tagEdit.loadAllTags (:223), pm.versions.revert (:279).
defects.mechanism: god-module survival by nesting: the aggregate blob was split into five names, but three slots still pass an entire composable through, so the port boundary constrains nothing and an admin surface leaks onto a public pane.
