grep -n 'pm\.\(flagged\|tagEdit\|versions\)\.' demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue   # → 4 sites, 4 verbs
defects.proposedCure: Split useAdminFlagged at the authority line: useFlagReport() (the one anonymous verb, owned by demo/palettes) and useAdminFlagQueue() (token-gated, owned by demo/palettes/admin). Ports list flat members only — reportFlag, revertVersion, availableTags, loadTags — never a composable object.

defects.defect: OKLab perceptual distance is hand-rolled twice (client + server) with a magic 0.15 radius in both, the typed client seam to the server implementation is dead code with zero callers, and the metric has no home in the colour library this repo publishes. The pane-local filter is invisible to the port, so paging, hasMore and the empty-state copy all describe the unfiltered query.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:339-349 — `const radius = 0.15; … Math.hypot(c.L-L, c.a-a, c.b-b) <= radius`, with a gratuitous `(p: any)` cast at :344 and an `as` widen at :345 even though demo/palettes/types.ts:32 already declares `oklabColors?: {L,a,b}[]`. api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-180 — same predicate, `query.colorRadius ?? 0.15`, Math.sqrt form. demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-30 declares colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius and :50-53 wires them into URLSearchParams; `grep -rn colorL demo | grep -v '^demo/palettes/api/'` → 1 hit, BrowsePane.vue:354, a COMMENT saying the server supports it. src/subpaths/color.ts exports 24 symbols, none a distance metric, while src/quantize.ts:116 and src/color/anchors.ts:203 each hand-roll their own Math.hypot.
defects.mechanism: missing library ownership: the concept most native to a colour library has four private copies and no public home, so the demo and the api independently reimplement it, and the demo's copy sits downstream of the port and is invisible to it.
defects.reproduction:

# consequence: with a colour search active, BrowsePane.vue:133 hasMore and :136-143 "More from the commons" page the UNFILTERED cursor, and :85 renders "No published palettes here yet." for a colour-filtered empty result
defects.proposedCure: Publish oklabDistance (or deltaEOk) on @mkbabb/value.js/color; src/quantize.ts and src/color/anchors.ts consume it; the api service imports it. The pane stops filtering client-side and passes colorL/A/B/Radius through the seam demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-30 already provides, so paging, hasMore and the empty copy all describe one query. Delete the (p: any) and the `as` — the field is already typed.

defects.defect: remotePalettes — the browse wall's row collection — has no owning module: it is handed out as a mutable Ref through the port and mutated by hand-rolled slug-index lookups from six different modules, nine sites.
defects.evidence: $ grep -rn "findIndex((p) => p.slug" demo → 9 hits: BrowsePane.vue:281, BrowsePane.vue:314, useBrowsePalettes.ts:130 (onVote), :166 (onRename), :197 (onSetVisibility), useAdminUsers.ts:87, browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:372, useDialogBrowseActions.ts:60, :80. Each repeats the same `idx >= 0 && existing` guard dance; BrowsePane.vue:314-318 reads remotePalettes.value[idx] before testing idx >= 0 (harmless today only because undefined short-circuits the &&).
defects.mechanism: no unique semantic ownership of a mutable collection: the port exposes the raw Ref, so every consumer re-derives "find the row for this slug and replace it".
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "findIndex((p) => p.slug" demo | wc -l   # → 9
defects.proposedCure: useBrowsePalettes owns the collection and exposes patchRow(slug, patch) / prependRow(p) / removeRow(slug); the port hands out a readonly computed. Keying rows by slug in a Map makes all nine sites O(1) and one line each.

defects.defect: The transport layer's typed error vocabulary is flattened to one hardcoded string at the composable boundary, so BrowsePane paints the exact mislabel that demo/platform/transport/availability.ts was written to prevent — while the dock, in the same viewport, reports the truth.
defects.evidence: availability.ts:167-169 comment: "A designed misconfig is NOT an unreachable backend — never mislabel it." :112-129 builds a loud actionable DevMisconfigError message naming origin, base URL and the fix. useBrowsePalettes.ts:77-82 catch block: `browseError.value = "Failed to load palettes"` — one string for DevMisconfigError, ApiUnavailableError, ApiProblem and any HTTP status. BrowsePane.vue:61-78 then renders message="The commons is unreachable." with that string as :detail. Screenshot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the plate reading "The commons is unreachable. / Failed to load palettes". Live DOM read against http://localhost:9000/#/browse returned the dock lamp text "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`" on element class="dock-status-lamp fira-code" with [data-variant="misconfigured"].
defects.mechanism: type erasure at a layer boundary: a typed error hierarchy exists in platform/ and has zero consumers on the browse path, so the pane re-invents a diagnosis the platform layer already made correctly.
defects.reproduction:

sed -n '61,78p' demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue          # the message it paints
# and: open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png — plate says "The commons is unreachable.", dock says nothing of the kind
defects.proposedCure: browseError becomes Ref<Error | null>; EmptyState selects its copy from the error's name (DevMisconfigError → the loud dev copy, ApiUnavailableError → "the commons is unreachable", ApiProblem → its title). The hierarchy already exists; the pane just has to stop flattening it. Side note: every #/browse row in the visual REPORT (lines 121,136,151,166) was measured on this error state — the wall itself has never been captured.

defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:209 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`, :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`, dispatch at :228-230, :237-239, :249, :264. defects.mechanism: ownership-duplication plus a lifecycle bug in both copies: Vue invokes a function-ref with null on unmount and the && short-circuits, so cardRefs retains torn-down proxies for every slug ever rendered.
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS for the growth measurement. The mechanism is exact from Vue's function-ref contract plus the two source lines (BrowsePane.vue:94, PalettesPane.vue:84), but I did not measure Object.keys(cardRefs).length growing live: the shared dev browser at localhost:9000 was under concurrent use by other seats mid-session and my probes were contaminated (the page navigated itself from #/browse to #/extract to #/admin/audit between reads). The duplication half of the finding is fully confirmed by grep.
defects.proposedCure: Better than deduplicating: delete the imperative rail. PaletteCard takes a `feedback?: {message,variant}` prop and renders it declaratively — the port already returns {success, message} from onDeleteOwned/onSetVisibility, so the data is in hand. If the imperative form must stay, one usePaletteCardFeedback() in browser/card/composables/ whose bind() deletes on the null call, consumed by both panes.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — a single click on BrowsePane's own Retry button permanently destroys the pane body. `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (BrowsePane.vue:40) couples DOM presence to a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine it animates settles synchronously (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws before any fetch, availability.ts:188-195). The leave completes; the enter never mounts. Measured live: state-container children 1→0 at t=251ms, still 0 at t=6000ms; wrapper height 224.5px→12px; typing in the search field does not recover it. This is the "full-slab remount hole" VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 forbids by name, and it occurs in exactly the state all 60 audit captures were taken in.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negative proofs (attacked and could not break, so no later seat re-litigates): (1) `duration-fast` is NOT a dead utility despite DESIGN.md:250 — live probe injecting `class="transition-opacity duration-fast"` yields transitionDuration "0.2s", transitionProperty "opacity"; --duration-fast=0.2s, --duration-normal=0.3s on :root. (2) vj-morph's max-height leg does NOT animate layout here — --vj-morph-collapse is unset so it resolves none→none and is inert. (3) No fourth motion family and no deleted animations — vj-morph is one of the three sanctioned families (animations.css:56-79). (4) prefers-reduced-motion IS handled — global guard animations.css:184-193. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax honored — BrowsePane.vue:197 `import type { Palette, Tag }`. (6) overflowX=0 in all four Safari matrices plus RTL desktop and RTL mobile. (7) Keyboard 7/12 NOT born-RED per MT-F022 — the gap is roving tabindex, which is correct. (8) The 4 small tap targets on /#/browse are companion-owned slug controls per REPORT.json (`Switch to slug`/`Generate new slug`/`Cancel` 22x22 + one 160x23 input), not BrowsePane's; BrowsePane's own ⋮ trigger is 32x32, above WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24x24.

defects.defect: One Retry click permanently blanks the pane body. Transition mode="out-in" on the three-state container makes DOM presence a function of a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine settles synchronously; the pending enter never mounts and the pane is left as a void under the search field with no error, no empty plate, no skeleton and no recovery.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`); demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:188-195 (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws synchronously, unconditional for `misconfigured`). Live Playwright/WebKit 1440x900, sampled every 25ms from the click: t=0 n=1 h=224.5 "The commons is unreachable.Failed to load palettes"; t=28 n=1 vj-morph-leave-from|vj-morph-leave-active; t=227 n=1 vj-morph-leave-active|vj-morph-leave-to; t=251 n=0 h=12.0 ""; t=1202 n=0 h=12.0 "". Second clean-page run, 6s tail: {wrapChildren:0, wrapH:12, paneText:"BrowseDiscover palettes from the community."}; after typing into the search field: {wrapChildren:0, same paneText}. Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/evidence/D-browse-before-retry.png vs D-browse-after-retry-6s.png.
defects.mechanism: Animation clock owns DOM presence — branch identity is animated with mode="out-in" across an async boundary that can settle faster than the leave duration.
defects.reproduction: 1) `http://localhost:9000/#/browse` at 1440x900 (dev server without VITE_API_URL, so the misconfigured latch is armed — the state all 60 audit captures show). 2) Wait ~3.5s for the error plate. 3) Click Retry once. 4) The state container's element children go 1→0 at ~251ms and stay 0 indefinitely; wrapper height 224.5px→12px. Typing in the search box does not restore it.
defects.proposedCure: Stop animating branch identity. Keep one persistent state region whose CONTENT cross-fades (default simultaneous mode), or drop the Transition on the state container entirely and let the individual plates own their entrance. A v-if guard inside mode="out-in" only narrows the window; it does not close the class.

defects.defect: The Browse composition is the equal-card matrix the constitution rules cannot satisfy any member, and the field wears the Card shell the same row forbids.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 Browse row: field at 64%…66.6666667%, inspector at 33.3333333%…36%, "browse workspace chassis; every rendered bounded palette entity slip has exactly one Card shell, and the field/empty/inspector have none"; same §: "`Card` … is never the default page primitive" and "Resizing the old equal-card matrix cannot satisfy any member." Measured live at 1440x900: Browse pane x199→711 = 512px; My Palettes companion x731→1240 = 509px; stage 199→1240 = 1041px → 49.2% / 48.9%. Delta vs the mandated floor: −14.8 to −17.5 percentage points. BrowsePane.vue:2 `<Card tier="resting" class="pane-scroll-fade w-full mx-auto overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden min-w-0 h-full">`. Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png and shots/safari-desktop-dark/browse.png.
defects.mechanism: The composition row was never built — Card used as the default page primitive, protagonist ratio unowned, companion is another route's pane rather than the mandated inspector.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse at 1440x900 and measure the two card rects: 512px and 509px inside a 1041px stage.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose to the browse workspace chassis the row names: field 64–66.667%, selected-public-palette inspector 33.333–36%, field/empty/inspector unhoused, Card tuple retained only on entity slips.

defects.defect: No selected-palette inspector exists anywhere in the pane, so every action the constitution assigns to the inspector is crammed onto the card as a seventeen-handler omnibus with an expand-in-place selection model.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: "A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable role=article, listbox/option composite, or seven-mode omnibus. … The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path. Full detail, rename/lifecycle/export actions and durable operation state live in the selected inspector." BrowsePane.vue:92-117 binds :expanded, @click=toggleExpand, @save, @delete, @vote, @rename, @edit-color, @add-color, @feature, @admin-delete, @set-visibility, @fork, @versions, @flag, @export, @edit-tags — 17 bindings. No inspector region appears in the 360-line file. §3.1 mobile order for Browse is "search, results, selected inspector"; the third term is absent. Live a11y snapshot renders the entity as `article "Palette: Featured One" [cursor=pointer]` — the clickable role=article the sentence forbids.
defects.mechanism: The composition row was never built — the missing inspector region forces every inspector-owned job onto the card body.
defects.reproduction: Read BrowsePane.vue:92-117 and grep the file for any inspector/detail region: none exists. Confirm on /#/browse that selection is expressed as card expansion (pm.expandedId) with no companion detail surface.
defects.proposedCure: Build the inspector the composition row specifies, move the fourteen action handlers into it, and reduce the card to identity + specimen + one native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` seat.

defects.defect: The error plate asserts one hard-coded cause for every failure — "The commons is unreachable." — and the record shows it is measurably the wrong diagnosis, while a correct one renders simultaneously in the Dock.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:62-66 (fixed message + :detail=pm.browseError); useBrowsePalettes.ts:79 sets the single literal "Failed to load palettes" for every catch. REPORT.json /#/browse, both desktop matrices: consoleWarnings ['Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.'] with failedRequests:[] and pageErrors:[] — a CLIENT parse bug, nothing unreachable. Live: the true cause is DevMisconfigError and the Dock renders `alert: "dev misconfigured — run \`npm run dev\`"` in the same viewport at the same instant. Consumer census `grep -rn "apiAvailability|DevMisconfigError" demo/ | grep -v transport/availability.ts` → DockStatusLamp.vue, status-lamp.ts, useApiClient.ts. BrowsePane is not on the list despite availability.ts:49 exporting the reactive cell and useApiClient.ts:41 re-exposing it.
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — a four-arm state union collapsed to one string.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse on the dev server without VITE_API_URL: the Dock says "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`" while BrowsePane says "The commons is unreachable." Separately, REPORT.json records a SyntaxError under the same UI copy.
defects.proposedCure: Branch the error plate on the closed `ApiAvailability` union (unknown | available | unavailable | misconfigured) plus the caught error class, one true sentence and one correct affordance per arm. Not a longer string — a state discrimination.

defects.defect: Retry is a dead affordance in exactly the state it is offered: while the transport latch is `misconfigured` it can never issue a request, and clicking it destroys the pane (D-01).
defects.evidence: availability.ts:188-191 — `if (apiAvailability.value === "misconfigured") throw new DevMisconfigError();` unconditional, no cooldown arm (RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS applies only to `unavailable`). Live probe counting every request whose URL contains /palettes: networkReqsBeforeRetry: 8, networkReqsAfterRetry: 8 — all eight are Vite module URLs (`/@fs/.../BrowsePane.vue?t=…`). Zero API requests before or after the click.
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — an action offered in a state where it provably cannot succeed.
defects.reproduction: On /#/browse with the misconfigured latch armed, attach a request listener filtered to '/palettes', click Retry, count requests: unchanged at 8, all Vite module fetches.
defects.proposedCure: Gate the recovery action on the availability arm: under `misconfigured` the plate names the configuration fault and offers no retry; under `unavailable` it offers retry with the cooldown surfaced.

defects.defect: The empty plate states a false fact about the world when the wall is merely filtered: four independent narrowing dimensions, one hard-coded "No published palettes here yet.", no filter badge for the text dimension, and no clear-filters action on the plate.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:83-86 (`:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` with fixed empty-text/empty-hint); displayedBrowse at :339-349 derives from pm.filteredBrowse (client text filter, useBrowsePalettes.ts:43) further narrowed by the pane-local colour filter; tier and tags narrow it server-side. SearchFilterBar.vue:186-192 — activeFilterCount counts tier + selectedTags + colorSearchActive but NOT the search text, so a text-filtered-empty wall shows no badge. PaletteCardGrid.vue:27-29 exposes an #emptyAction slot that BrowsePane leaves unused, so the empty plate carries no action while the error plate does. Same mechanism at PalettesPane.vue:77-80.
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — filtered-empty was never separated from true-empty, the third species EmptyState.vue's own header argument implies.
defects.reproduction: Mechanism reproduces live today on the sibling site: /#/palettes with 1 saved palette, type `zzz` into "Search your palettes…" → the plate reads "No saved palettes yet." The Browse instance needs a reachable API to demonstrate; the branch conditions above are the proof of shape.
defects.proposedCure: Three species, not two: a `no-results-for-this-filter` plate that names the active filters and carries a clear-filters action, distinct from `true-empty`. Count the search text in activeFilterCount.

defects.defect: The load-more failure state does not exist: the catch is a console.warn, so the skeletons appear, silently vanish, and the button returns with nothing said.
defects.evidence: useBrowsePalettes.ts:109-111 — `} catch (e) { console.warn("Failed to load more palettes:", e); }` — no browseError, no flag, no surface. BrowsePane.vue:125-144 renders the two skeleton plates and the button off pm.loadingMore / pm.hasMore only. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08: "Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient → ADD-AFFORDANCE. Persistent entity status/recovery."
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false.
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-proven; the runtime arm requires a reachable API whose continuation request then fails. Labelled a hypothesis on the runtime arm; the catch block is the confirmed shape.
defects.proposedCure: Route the continuation failure into the same durable status region the fresh-load failure uses, with the page-turn identity attached.

defects.defect: A failed sort silently ships a stale wall under the new sort's label: sortMode is set before the request, the catch does not clear remotePalettes, and the error branch requires an empty wall so it is skipped.
defects.evidence: useBrowsePalettes.ts:117-121 sets sortMode.value before awaiting loadRemotePalettes(true); :78-82 catch sets browseError but leaves remotePalettes populated; BrowsePane.vue:62 `v-else-if="pm.browseError.value && displayedBrowse.length === 0"` — with a populated wall the error branch is skipped and the v-else wall renders. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — the error surface is conditioned on emptiness rather than on the error.
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-proven hypothesis on the runtime arm; requires a reachable API that then fails a sort request. Branch conditions cited above are the confirmed shape.
defects.proposedCure: Decouple the error surface from wall emptiness: a durable per-request status that can coexist with rendered content, and revert the sort control to the order actually in effect.

defects.defect: The sort-pending state is opacity-only and the dimmed wall stays fully interactive — no aria-busy, no live region, no pointer-events guard.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:87-90 — `:grid-class="'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')"` is the entire pending design. Measured on the live page: `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-busy]').length` = 0; `[aria-live]` regions = [] (whole document). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: states are never colour-only.
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — a visual dim substituted for a state.
defects.reproduction: On /#/browse, evaluate `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-busy]').length` → 0 and `[...document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]')]` → [] while the pane owns four async states.
defects.proposedCure: One durable status region owning aria-busy + a polite result-count announcement, and an inert/pointer-events guard on the wall while a replacement request is in flight.

defects.defect: Both loading states carry an aria-label on a bare div (role=generic), where ARIA prohibits naming — so the developing wall and the load-more page are silent.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:44-48 `<div v-if="pm.browsing.value" key="developing" class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3" aria-label="Loading palettes">` and :125-131 `aria-label="Loading more palettes"`. ARIA 1.2 §5.2.8.4 places role=generic in the name-prohibited set. Corroborated by the measured aria-busy: 0 / aria-live: [] on the live page. Contrast the shared atom EmptyState.vue, which correctly gives the error plate role="alert" and the empty plate role="status" — only the two states authored inline in BrowsePane got no role.
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false; plus a god-module boundary drawn wrong — two of four states live in a correctly-roled shared atom, two live as raw divs in the pane.
defects.reproduction: Inspect the two divs; neither carries a role, so the aria-label is dropped by AT. Live check: no [aria-busy] and no [aria-live] anywhere on the route.
defects.proposedCure: Move the loading plates into the same shared state atom that already owns empty/error, with role="status" and aria-busy, so all four states share one roled surface.

defects.defect: The search placeholder is hard-clipped mid-token on mobile in both directions, with no ellipsis: the slotted ⋮ filter trigger overlays the field without reserving inline padding.

Rendered: shots/safari-mobile-light/browse.png and shots/safari-mobile-dark/browse.png → "Search the common" (tail lost); shots/rtl-mobile/browse.png → "earch the commons" (head letter lost, because the trigger flips to inline-start). The twin "Search your palettes..." in the same viewport uses no slot and renders whole — proving the clip is caused by the slotted trigger, not string length.

defects.defect: Authored English prose is not direction-isolated, so RTL relocates terminal punctuation to the visual left.

defects.defect: The empty/error plate top-aligns inside an h-full Card, leaving over half the card height as unowned void — the opposite of the content-hug the composition row mandates.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 Browse row: "primary empty invitation content-hugs"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04: "Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE … Collapse absent support." BrowsePane.vue:2 Card is h-full; :4 inner column is `flex flex-col gap-3 min-h-0` with no grow on the state region. Measured live at 1440x900: pane rect top 114.99 bottom 865.09 (height 750.10); error rect top 268.67 bottom 481.22 (height 212.55); dead space below = 865.09 − 481.22 = 383.87px = 51.2% of the card height. Visible in all four Safari matrices.
defects.mechanism: The composition row was never built — a fixed-height Card housing a content-hug state.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse at 1440x900 in the error/empty state and measure getBoundingClientRect on the pane Card and the [role=alert] plate: 383.87px of empty card below the plate.
defects.proposedCure: Unhouse the empty/inspector per the composition row so the invitation hugs its own content; the field, not a fixed Card, owns the remaining stage.

defects.defect: `.search-seated` is a per-instance override of a glass-ui root component, deliberately unlayered to beat the producer's cascade layer, and replicated across three consumers — a producer variant that was never raised.
defects.evidence: Owner edicts 4 and 5. BrowsePane.vue:12 applies class="search-seated" to SearchBar from @mkbabb/glass-ui/search. demo/styles/utils.css:132-155 overrides background, backdrop-filter, border, box-shadow, max-width and the descendant `.input-bar-field` font-family; its own comment: "INTERIM DEMO SEAT — a consumer opt-in on the producer recipe (unlayered, so it wins over the @layer components recipe by layer order) … BOOKED SWAP … dies onto glass-ui's P3 seated field-chrome rung — ASK-D (variant=\"seated\")". Site census: BrowsePane.vue:12, PalettesPane.vue:35, admin/AdminPane.vue:14.
defects.mechanism: Producer boundary crossed — three consumers of one hand-rolled chrome, using cascade-layer ordering as the override mechanism edict 5 exists to forbid.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "search-seated" demo/ → three .vue consumers plus the utils.css definition; read utils.css:132-155 for the override surface.
defects.proposedCure: Land `variant="seated"` in glass-ui SearchBar (ASK-D, already filed) and delete the three-site override plus the utils.css block. Booked is not shipped.

defects.defect: "Find by Color" is a silent partial search over the loaded page while the server API supports the query, with an untokenised magic radius and a silent data-dependent exclusion.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:336-355 — `const radius = 0.15;` then a client-side filter over pm.filteredBrowse with `if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;` and the comment "API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant". demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:49-52 genuinely sends colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE is 50, and BrowsePane.vue:133 keys load-more on pm.hasMore, so paging fetches the next UNFILTERED page and then colour-filters it. `oklabColors` is optional on the type (types.ts:32) and is a migration field server-side (api/src/platform/migrations/check.ts:46). The `(p: any)` cast at :344 is unnecessary since oklabColors is declared on Palette.
defects.mechanism: Search semantics unowned — a masking client-side fallback chosen over a working server path (owner edict 2), plus an unparameterised distance threshold.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the runtime arm (needs a populated reachable commons). Code-proven: the server params exist and are unused; the radius is a bare literal; the missing-oklabColors branch returns false.
defects.proposedCure: Use the server colour params so the search covers the commons; token the radius and expose it or justify it against a measured OKLab ΔE; render palettes lacking oklabColors as an explicit excluded count rather than dropping them into a false empty.

defects.defect: cardRefs is a deep-reactive map of component public instances whose entries are never released, because the ref callback's `el &&` guard skips the unmount null.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({});` and :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`. Vue invokes the function ref with null on unmount; the guard skips that call, so no key is ever deleted. `reactive` (not shallowReactive/markRaw) means each read returns a reactive proxy wrapping a component public instance, so property access is tracked inside the component's own instance graph. `grep -rn "shallowReactive|markRaw" demo/palettes/` → zero hits.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene — imperative child-instance coupling stored in the wrong reactivity primitive with no teardown.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the accumulation arm — requires a reachable API to populate and page the wall past the 50-cap. Labelled a hypothesis on runtime consequence; the code shape (no delete path, deep reactive) is confirmed.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the ref map entirely — the feedback it drives belongs in the inspector D-03 is missing (see D-17). If a collection must survive, use a plain Map with an explicit null-branch delete.

defects.defect: Transient per-card feedback is the ONLY truth for save, delete, visibility and fork outcomes, and it is silently swallowed if the card unmounted between request and verdict.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:226-250 and :262-265 route every verdict through cardRefs[slug].showFeedback(...) (PaletteCard.vue:238,244 defineExpose). :249 uses optional chaining, so a verdict for an unmounted card is discarded with no surface. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: "Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace. A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth."
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — same PR-08 family as D-07/D-08.
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-proven; the swallow path requires a reachable API plus a filter/sort/page change between request and response.
defects.proposedCure: Durable per-entity operation state in the selected inspector (the region D-03 identifies as missing); the flourish may remain, but only as celebration over a persisted truth.

defects.defect: The route has no H1; the pane identity announces as h3 with no h2 or h1 above it, while being styled at the display-1 rung the type matrix reserves for the route H1.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json /#/browse, all four matrices: "h1": 0, "main": 1. Live accessibility snapshot: `heading "Browse" [level=3]`. demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue emits `<h3 class="pane-header-title font-display">` and styles it `.pane-header-title { font-size: var(--type-display-1) }`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "Each route has one H1 and exactly one stable main landmark, owned by the shell"; §4 maps route H1 to text-display/Fraunces.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene / shared-atom family — PaneHeader has 9 consumers; the cure belongs at the shell plus that atom, BrowsePane is a site.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse and evaluate `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length` → 0; the visually-largest text on the pane is an h3.
defects.proposedCure: The shell owns the route H1 per §4.1; PaneHeader emits the correct level beneath it, or the pane identity becomes the H1 when the pane is the route protagonist.

defects.defect: Two hard-coded skeleton counts (4 and 2) for one grammar, neither related to the 50-row page size, so the skeleton is decoration rather than a request-shaped preview.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:207 `const SKELETON_COUNT = 4;` and :130 `<PaletteCardSkeleton v-for="i in 2" ...>` — the second is a bare literal with no name. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE is 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts currentFilterOpts). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7: "Request-bound skeletons exist only while real work is in flight."
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene — two magic numbers for one designed grammar.
defects.reproduction: Read BrowsePane.vue:130 and :207.
defects.proposedCure: One named count derived from the page size (or a deliberate, documented cap) shared by both arms; the constitution's grammar is one species, so it should read from one source.

defects.defect: The forced-colors capture proves nothing (WebKit does not honour the emulation) and the pane ships no forced-colors treatment, so the selection/focus deltas §4.1 and §4.2 require are undemonstrated.
defects.evidence: shots/forced-colors-desktop/browse.png is visually indistinguishable from shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png apart from a slightly muted ambient field — glass cards still translucent, the pastel `Palettes` gradient text still renders, cartoon shadows still paint. Repo-wide `grep -rn forced-colors demo/ src/` → 9 hits, all in demo/styles/foundation.css, demo/styles/focus-ring.css and one gradient editor; ZERO under demo/palettes/. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: focus distinct from selection "in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency"; §4.2 requires a nonzero selected-state delta in forced colors.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene / evidence gap — an unverified matrix cited as coverage.
defects.reproduction: Compare the two PNGs side by side; then grep demo/palettes/ for forced-colors → no hits.
defects.proposedCure: Capture forced-colors on an engine that honours it (Chromium/Edge WHCM) before citing the matrix; then prove a nonzero selected-state and focus delta for the pane's selection model — which per D-03 is currently geometry-only card expansion.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1/L-12 — every `WatercolorDot tag="button"` mount in the demo is a dead control. glass-ui 7.0.0 deleted the `tag` prop, the polymorphic host and the `<slot/>`, and sets `inheritAttrs:false` with no `$attrs` spread, so `@click`, `aria-label` and the slotted `<Plus>` are all discarded. The subject's primary CTA ("Add current color") renders as `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events:none`, `tabIndex:-1`, no accessible name and no icon — measured live at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes. The blast radius is 6 mounts / 4 components / 3 routes and 6 red e2e role-queries; on touch, `SwatchHoverMenu`'s `<PopoverTrigger as-child>` path means the swatch menu cannot open at all. Root cause is a missing module: nothing in the lattice owns "an interactive color swatch", so six call sites hand-assembled one out of a decoration primitive and a string prop.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND. (Proven negatives are recorded in the report's "What is SOUND" + pass-2 stamp: zero deep-`src/` reach from demo — `grep -rEn 'from "(@mkbabb/value.js…|../src/…|@/src…)"' demo` returns 44 hits, all real `package.json#exports` keys (`/color 25, /css 10, /math 6, /easing 5, /quantize 4`), zero bare-root, zero internals, so a real consumer could write every demo import verbatim; the subject imports the library not at all, correctly, being a pure UI leaf. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean across the closure. No god module: 312/116/93/67/17 lines across the five files. `useHoverPopover` has exactly two consumers and one home — no dual path. Vue 3.5 idiom is correct: reactive props destructure paired with `toRef(() => …)` at the composable seam. `inv-K-1` (library → producer ban) is live enforcement, unlike the demo-side rules.)

defects.defect: The component's primary CTA is dead: `<WatercolorDot tag="button" @click="addCurrentColor" :aria-label=…><Plus/></WatercolorDot>` at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 binds four contracts (tag prop, fallthrough aria-label, click listener, default slot) that glass-ui 7.0.0 honours none of.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts declares exactly 6 props (color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed) — no `tag`. dist/watercolor-dot.js: `grep -o 'inheritAttrs:[^,]*'` → `inheritAttrs: !1`; `grep -c 'renderSlot'` → `0`; attrs-handling census → `1 useAttrs` only, no mergeProps, no $attrs spread. Live Playwright probe on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: {"tagName":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"pointerEvents":"none","tabIndex":-1,"matchesButton":false,"hasPlusSvg":false,"childTags":["svg.watercolor-filter-host","SPAN.watercolor-ghost-stroke"]}. Visual: shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png shows the dashed ghost with no `+` glyph.
defects.mechanism: missing-module / paint-primitive-promoted-to-control: no seam owns "interactive color swatch", so consumers assemble one from a decoration primitive plus a `tag` prop, and the producer legitimately withdrew the prop (a component hard-coding aria-hidden + pointer-events:none on its own root is declaring itself paint).
defects.reproduction: npm run dev (server already live) → open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → the "Start a new palette" well shows a dashed silhouette with no + glyph; clicking it does nothing; Tab never reaches it. Programmatic: document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost') → SPAN, aria-hidden=true, pointer-events:none, tabIndex -1. e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:35 getByRole("button",{name:/Add current color .* to palette/}) cannot match.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui grows `./swatch` — a real <button> hosting a WatercolorDot, owning the accessible name, focus register, press/hover legs and popover attachment. WatercolorDot stays pure paint, consumed only by ./swatch. SwatchHoverMenu.vue is absorbed. Six call sites become <Swatch>/<SwatchMenu> mounts and the class of defect ends: a paint primitive can no longer be promoted to a control by passing it a string.

defects.defect: The dead-`tag="button"` defect is a 6-mount, 4-component, 3-route epidemic, not a local 2-mount bug; on touch the SwatchHoverMenu popover cannot open at all because `<PopoverTrigger as-child>` merges its props as attrs into a component with inheritAttrs:false.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'tag="button"' demo` → 6 hits: MixSourceSelector.vue:168,215 · GenerateControls.vue:203 · CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:98 · SwatchHoverMenu.vue:17,32 — all WatercolorDot. Playwright pass over three routes: /#/mix .add-slot-ghost count 1 → SPAN/aria-hidden/pe:none/tabIndex -1/ariaLabel null; /#/generate .generate-swatch count 5 → same; /#/palettes .watercolor-swatch count 7 → same. Red role-queries: e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:40, e2e/smoke/safari/mix-flow.spec.ts:30, e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:353 and :412, e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:53, e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:35.
defects.mechanism: missing-module / paint-primitive-promoted-to-control (same mechanism as L-1, at population scale) — one absent seam became six simultaneous silent breakages on a single producer change.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe2.mjs against the live dev server; or open /#/mix and try to add the current color (impossible), /#/generate and click any swatch to copy (no-op), /#/palettes on a coarse-pointer emulation and tap a saved swatch (menu never opens).
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as L-1, applied once at the producer: glass-ui `./swatch`. Six consumers converge on one component; the demo stops hand-assembling controls out of paint.

defects.defect: The `.d.ts` trust boundary the demo tsconfig argues for is a false proof: vue-tsc is green while L-1 is fully live, because Vue's generated component types accept arbitrary extra attributes as fallthrough attrs, making `tag="button"` on a propless component legal TypeScript.
defects.evidence: `timeout 420 npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0, 0 diagnostic lines, at HEAD 041ca263 with L-1 live. The proof stack at the glass-ui seam: vue-tsc green-and-blind (measured); eslint absent (`npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue` → `no-restricted-imports = undefined`); unit tests 0 hits; e2e red and unread.
defects.mechanism: structural-typing at a component seam — a boundary that cannot express "unknown prop" is not a boundary.
defects.reproduction: npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit → exit 0, zero output, while the CTA is provably dead.
defects.proposedCure: Make the seam nominal, not structural: glass-ui exports a `WatercolorDotProps` type the demo spreads as a checked object (unknown key → excess-property error, which TS does report), and ships a producer-side contract test for WatercolorDot on the pattern of its existing labeled-field.contract.test.ts.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a 19-module pure-alias layer over glass-ui with zero logic, and 18 of 19 barrels route through the root barrel rather than the granular subpath glass-ui 7 ships — producing four different design-system import idioms inside this one component's tree.
defects.evidence: All 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts dumped: each is a single `export … from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` (only input reaches `/forms`). CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:174-181 imports Input/Button/Tooltip through the aliases while :191 imports WatercolorDot directly from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot`, and useSwatchActions.ts:5 imports writeClipboard from the root barrel for a function that lives at ./dom. Reachable ESM graph: glass-ui.js root barrel = 66 modules / 218.9 KB vs button.js = 11 / 16.8 KB. demo/ui/alert/index.ts carries the tombstone of its own conversion ("previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation … B.W2 converted it to a re-export").
defects.mechanism: alias/shim layer retained after its content was proved empty — the wrapper survived the thing it wrapped.
defects.reproduction: for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do cat $f; done → 19 single-line re-exports, no logic.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely (19 files, 0 lines of logic) and rewrite the ~200 consumer imports to the granular glass-ui subpath. Mechanical codemod; removes a directory from the demo lattice and makes the design-system dependency legible at every call site.

defects.defect: `btn-interactive` is a phantom class. The component's own comment says the hover/press scale legs were "retired onto the producer's btn-interactive atom"; that atom does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0, so the animation was deleted, not moved — a direct edict-6 violation.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "btn-interactive" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → no output (0 files in the whole 7.0.0 package). Live document.styleSheets walk → {"n":0,"samples":[]} — zero CSS rules mention it. The class is applied at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:75,78,100 (and ColorInput.vue:69,78). Live computed transition on .add-slot-ghost is "transform, border-radius, filter, box-shadow / 0.2s, 0.6s, 0.2s, 0.2s" — all from glass-ui's own .watercolor-swatch; no scale leg in either register. Corroborating history: docs/precepts/instructions/LESSONS-LEARNED.md:603 records `.btn-interactive` being retired at the substrate under a false zero-site verdict.
defects.mechanism: cross-repo token deletion under a false zero-site verdict; the consumer kept the class name as documentation of an atom that no longer ships.
defects.reproduction: In the live page console: [...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return[]}}).filter(r=>(r.cssText||'').includes('btn-interactive')).length → 0.
defects.proposedCure: Mint the atom where its comment already claims it lives — glass-ui `@utility btn-interactive`, riding --transition-liquid-spatial @ --spring-smooth-duration with the house focus register — and let ./swatch compose it, so the six swatch sites inherit the press/hover legs instead of naming a class that resolves to nothing.

defects.defect: The G-DEMO-1 / G-DEMO-3a / G-DEMO-3b architectural boundary rules are dead config: their file globs target `demo/@/**`, a directory that no longer exists, and their banned specifier prefix `@components/**` has zero usages. The "standing, eslint-enforced" barrel-seam law does not apply to the subject at all.
defects.evidence: `npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue` → `no-restricted-imports = undefined`. `ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory. `grep -rn '"@components' demo | wc -l` → 0. eslint.config.js:232-239 globs demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/**; :274-277 globs demo/@/composables/**; the restricted group at :247 and :295 is `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`. Meanwhile browser/index.ts:6 asserts "the G-DEMO-3b boundary (eslint.config.js) enforces it standing", and CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:193 is the live violation it would have caught (`import ApiOfflineChip from "../status/ApiOfflineChip.vue"` — a raw cross-cluster .vue reach).
defects.mechanism: config keyed on a path shape the W43/RF-15 restructure deleted; the guard silently degraded to a no-op while its prose kept asserting enforcement.
defects.reproduction: npx eslint --no-warn-ignored --print-config demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue | jq '.rules["no-restricted-imports"]' → null.
defects.proposedCure: Re-key the three rules onto the live tree (demo/palettes/**, demo/picker/**, demo/shell/**, demo/workbenches/**, demo/scenes/**) with relative-path groups (`**/browser/*/*.vue`), and add a CI assertion that each no-restricted-imports group matches ≥1 real import today — a boundary rule that can never fire is indistinguishable from an absent one.

defects.defect: Wrong direction of dependency: 4 props + 8 emits re-declare state the app already provides by injection; 6 of 8 emits are 1:1 relays onto ports built for exactly this, and useSwatchActions hand-retypes the colorTargetPort surface.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:196-213 (4 props / 8 emits). PalettesPane.vue:163 `inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY)!` then re-drills it as a prop at :43, while the child injects SAFE_ACCENT_KEY from the same keys module at :215 and its composable injects EDIT_TARGET_KEY at useSwatchActions.ts:4 — three facets of one colour session, two transport idioms. PalettesPane.vue:46-53 relays @apply/@add-color/@start-edit/@saved/@updated/@clear-current straight onto colorTarget.* and pm.*; usePalettePorts.ts:137-155 (libraryPort) and :234-240 (colorTargetPort: emitApply, emitAddColor, emitStartEdit, emitSetCurrentColor, commitColorEdit) already expose every one. useSwatchActions.ts:12-17 re-declares that port's call signatures by hand.
defects.mechanism: prop-drill/inject dual transport for one concept, plus a second structural declaration of an already-typed port.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural (verified by reading the port definitions against the relay list).
defects.proposedCure: Inject, don't drill. useSwatchActions takes inject(COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY) directly (it already injects EDIT_TARGET_KEY two lines up); the component injects CSS_COLOR_KEY and LIBRARY_PORT_KEY. The 4-prop/8-emit surface collapses to zero props and two emits, and PalettesPane.vue:41-54 (14 lines of relay) becomes a single self-closing tag.

defects.defect: The edit-commit control pair (FROM→TO WatercolorDot diff + Check/Undo2) is implemented twice — here and in the dock — and the `commitEdit` command it sends has two wirings that have already drifted apart.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:56-84 vs Dock.vue:136-144: same arrow span, same Check aria-label="Save edit" with the identical per-instance `:style="{ color: safeAccent }"`, same Undo2 aria-label="Cancel edit"; differing only in dot size (w-11/sm:w-12 vs w-7), seeds (edit-from-i/edit-to-i vs edit-original/edit-new) and host (bare <button class="btn-interactive"> vs <DockControl>). Divergent command wiring: demo/color-picker/App.vue:41 `@commit-edit="colorPickerRef?.commitEdit(); viewManager.mobilePaneIndex.value = 1"` vs demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:156 `"onCommit-edit": () => deps.colorPickerRef()?.commitEdit()` — same verb, same target ref, one extra side effect on one path only.
defects.mechanism: responsive routing implemented as a fork — two homes for one concept with nothing holding them in agreement, plus a command with two call sites and no single owner.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the drift's user-visible consequence (structural); the duplication itself is verified by the two file:line pairs above.
defects.proposedCure: One EditCommitBar owning the FROM→TO diff and the two verbs, living in demo/color-session/ (which already owns EDIT_TARGET_KEY and the EditTarget type), rendered by whichever host is on screen and styled through the host's slot. The command moves onto COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY (usePalettePorts.ts:239 already exposes commitColorEdit), so both hosts call one port method and the pane-index reset lives inside it once — deleting the commitEdit/cancelEdit emit pair from this component, from PalettesPane, and from usePaneRouter's rightProps special case.

defects.defect: The palette-name collision rule has two homes that disagree, and hosting it here costs a full `savedPalettes: Palette[]` prop drilled into a swatch editor to run one `.find()`.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:253-256 `savedPalettes.find(p => p.name.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase())`. demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:66-74 `store.value.palettes.find(p => p.isLocal && p.name.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase() && colorsMatch(p.colors, colors))`. Three divergences: isLocal filter present/absent, colorsMatch present/absent, resolution move-to-front-and-reuse vs prompt-to-Update. `Palette` (demo/palettes/types.ts:14-64) is a 23-field type; this component reads only .name and .id.
defects.mechanism: domain rule duplicated in a presentation component; the duplicate drifted and dragged a heavyweight prop with it.
defects.reproduction: NONE — divergence is structural. Failure shape: a name that collides on the component's rule but not the store's yields an Update confirm for a palette the store would have created fresh.
defects.proposedCure: The store owns identity. usePaletteStore grows findByName(name) (or createPalette returns a discriminated {ok} | {collision: Palette}); the component asks the port and the savedPalettes prop dies with the duplicated predicate.

defects.defect: Palette export has two live implementations and the tested one is not the shipped one: `demo/palettes/export.ts` (132 lines) and `demo/palettes/export/` (12 modules, 1073 lines) both exist, and the directory has no index.ts, so `from "./export"` resolves to the file.
defects.evidence: `ls demo/palettes/export/` → bytes, canonical, css, digest, json, png, reload, rfc8785, serializers, svg, tailwind, types — no index.ts. `wc -l` → export.ts 132, export/ 1073. usePaletteExport.ts:9 imports exportAsJSON/exportAsCSSCustomProperties/exportAsTailwindConfig/exportAsSVG/exportAsPNG/downloadExport `from "./export"`; Node/Vite extension resolution picks the sibling file over the extensionless directory, so the 12-module implementation is unreachable through that specifier.
defects.mechanism: dual implementation disambiguated only by module-resolution order — the most fragile possible arbiter.
defects.reproduction: node -e "console.log(require.resolve('./demo/palettes/export'))" (or read usePaletteExport.ts:9 against `ls demo/palettes/export/`): the directory has no index, so the file wins.
defects.proposedCure: Delete export.ts. `export/serializers.ts` + the 11 byte-exact modules become the only implementation, reached through an explicit `export/index.ts` barrel, and the one slugify moves to demo/palettes/utils.ts.

defects.defect: SAFE_ACCENT_KEY is injected from app-root boot into a leaf card to power one per-instance inline style whose value is already on :root as var(--primary) by construction; and two keys from the same module use opposite inject contracts (crash-on-missing vs silent masking default).
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:173,215 import + `inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!`; sole use is :76 `<Check :style="{ color: safeAccent }">`. Provider is demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:91 `provide(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY, safeAccentCss)`; :96 mirrors the same ref onto --accent-live; demo/styles/foundation.css:250-251 `--accent-view: var(--accent-live); --primary: var(--accent-view);`. Contract asymmetry: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:215 `inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!` vs useSwatchActions.ts:23 `inject(EDIT_TARGET_KEY, ref(null) as ShallowRef<EditTarget|null>)`.
defects.mechanism: one value, two transports (injection channel duplicating a CSS custom property) — the injection is the sole reason a leaf card is coupled to app-root boot; plus a masking fallback (edict 2) sitting beside a crash-on-missing inject for the same class of dependency.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural; the identity safeAccent === var(--primary) follows from useAtmosphereBoot.ts:91 vs :96 and foundation.css:250-251.

It is the pass-2 finding that changes what the mega-tranche must DO rather than merely what it must delete. Strongest across both passes remains pass-1 L-1 (the byte-exact export contract ships to nobody while its test stays green), with L-4/N-2 next — the dead guard that let everything else accumulate: `npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue` → no-restricted-imports = undefined.
result.negativeProof: The brief's headline charge does NOT hold: BrowsePane's graph contains no demo import a real consumer could not write, and the mechanism that closes it is structural rather than disciplinary. Measured: `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/ | wc -l` → 0 (no bare-root import, which matters because package.json#exports has NO "." key — such an import would be unresolvable); `grep -rn '@src/\|\.\./\.\./src/' demo/ | grep -v '\.md'` → no output (zero deep reaches into src/ from demo); and all 49 value.js specifiers in demo/ are keys that exist in the export map — `grep -rho 'from "@mkbabb/value.js/[a-z]*"' demo/ | sort | uniq -c` → color 24, css 10, math 6, easing 5, quantize 4, each a published subpath. BrowsePane itself imports zero value.js. The enforcement: vite.config.ts:38-49 GENERATES the self-alias set by reading package.json#exports at config time and emitting one anchored-regex (^…$) alias per subpath, so an alias cannot drift from the export map nor prefix-match into a subpath (the comment at :30-36 records the R-era boot break that anchoring cured); tsconfig.demo.json:33 carries no @src/* path (the @src alias survives only for the exempt assets/docs/*.md source-embed pages). A non-published specifier is therefore not merely absent from this tree — it is unauthorable by accident. Secondary negatives verified: no live raw-.vue reach past the palette-browser barrel seam (`grep -rn 'from "[^"]*browser/[^"]*\.vue"' demo/` → empty, though N-2 proves nothing enforces this); BrowsePane's type-only import is correctly `import type { Palette, Tag }` at :197, so verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied; and browse renders with overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0 in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:121,136,151,166). Derive the collision: `const duplicate = computed(() => savedColorStrings.length ? savedPalettes.find(p => p.name.toLowerCase() === effectiveName.value.toLowerCase()) : undefined)` and gate the confirm on `duplicate.value` at commit time. defects.defect: TransitionGroup keys are position-derived, so every swatch after a mutation point is destroyed and remounted: the .vj-enter-move FLIP never runs and N-1 SVG turbulence filter graphs are re-created per removal. The key registry also lives inside an impure computed.

Measured DOM identity across a removal: before [wrap0,wrap1,wrap2,wrap3] → after [<NEW NODE>,<NEW NODE>,wrap3] — both survivors recreated; only the literal-keyed add slot (:87 key="__add__") persisted. Filter census: {"inEditor":4,"pageWide":10} five-octave feTurbulence graphs for 3 colours, each id minted by useId() so a remount mints a new filter element. The producer docblock names the hazard: "forces the filter graph to RE-RASTERIZE every frame, which flashes Safari". demo/styles/animations.css:99 defines .vj-enter-move, which can never apply.
defects.mechanism: M3 — identity derived from position; plus a computed with side effects (mutates a Map and increments a counter during evaluation).
defects.reproduction: node .../cpe-challenge-c-probe2.mjs → `keyChurn`.
defects.proposedCure: Key from identity, not position. Mint a stable id where the buffer actually lives (model.savedColors, useColorPipeline.ts:166) and carry it through; failing that, `${color}#${occurrenceIndex}` is position-free and survives shifts. Either way the Map, the counter, the prune watcher and the `?? i` fallback all delete.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: no unit test exists, the only e2e that exercises the component is RED on HEAD, CI never runs Playwright, and vue-tsc is green despite four dead bindings. A one-line deletion of the primary action keeps every gate green.

defects.defect: addCurrentColor no-ops silently at a domain boundary (current colour already the sole entry) with no feedback; and because C-1 makes the control unactivatable, its reorder branch has never executed in the shipped app.

defects.defect: Five hand-rolled <button> elements with per-instance utility styling where the design system provides Button, including a 130-character class string triplicated verbatim.

defects.defect: The route-level visual audit structurally cannot see this component's a11y defects: it captured /#/palettes in the EMPTY state, where the save button, the name input and the duplicate banner do not render.
defects.evidence: REPORT.md:97 reports namelessButtons: 1 for /#/palettes; the captured screenshots (shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png, shots/safari-mobile-dark/palettes.png) show "Start a new palette" / "No saved palettes yet." The save row is v-if'd on savedColorStrings.length > 0 at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:118, so this component contributed zero to the audit's counts — while in the populated state it adds one nameless button (C-6), one unlabeled input (C-7) and three tabbable controls inside aria-hidden (C-4).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue` (area palettes, route #/browse)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the browse wall is DEAD in all four Safari matrices and the pane reports the wrong cause. `request()` ends with a bare `return res.json()` (client.ts:118) with no content-type guard; `loadRemotePalettes` then DISCARDS the caught error and substitutes the constant "Failed to load palettes" (useBrowsePalettes.ts:79), which BrowsePane.vue:62-67 renders under "The commons is unreachable." REPORT.json records `SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.` on /#/browse in 4/4 matrices; my WebKit probe proves that string IS WebKit's `Response.json()` parse failure; and `curl` proves the dev origin answers `/palettes?...` with HTTP 200 + text/html. So the server ANSWERED and the client blew up parsing it — and the user is told the server is unreachable. Four distinct typed failures (DevMisconfigError / ApiUnavailableError / ApiProblem / raw SyntaxError) collapse into one 24-character string.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded as finding C-18: the one axis that IS sound is a11y geometry. BrowsePane contributes ZERO small tap targets and ZERO nameless buttons — measured on a fully-loaded 50-card wall: `smallTapTargets: []`, `namelessButtons: 0`, `operableControls: 103`, `overflowX: 0`. The REPORT's 4 small targets at /#/browse are the dock slug widget, identical on all 15 routes. Also genuinely absent: ValueUnit wrapping, defineModel, rAF loops, WebGL, observers, timers, listeners; `verbatimModuleSyntax` is honoured. Per MT-F022 keyboard reachability was NOT touched — it needs a two-engine proof this seat did not run.)

defects.defect: The browse wall is non-functional in every Safari matrix, and the pane surfaces a false diagnosis: a client-side JSON-parse failure is rendered as "The commons is unreachable." `request()` returns `res.json()` unguarded (no content-type check) and `loadRemotePalettes` discards the typed error, replacing it with one constant string for all four distinguishable failure classes.
defects.evidence: audit/visual/REPORT.json — /#/browse, 4/4 matrices: consoleWarnings ['Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.'], bodyTextLength 280/124; shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png renders the error plate, zero cards. probe-C-webkit-json.mjs: `== WebKit ==  /good PARSED OK · /empty|/html|/trailing SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.` `curl -D - http://localhost:9000/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest` → `HTTP/1.1 200 OK / Content-Type: text/html`. Sites: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:118, demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:79, demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:62-67.
defects.mechanism: Typed failure collapsed to a constant / swallowed — the transport mints ApiProblem/ApiUnavailableError/DevMisconfigError/raw SyntaxError and the caller throws all four away.
defects.reproduction: Point VITE_API_URL at any origin whose fallback answers 200 with non-JSON (the repo's own vite dev server does exactly this for /palettes), load /#/browse in Safari/WebKit. Confirmed: 4/4 captured matrices + the WebKit message-identification probe + the curl showing a 200 text/html body on the palette path.
defects.proposedCure: `request()` guards the parse (content-type check → throw a typed ApiProblem/ApiMalformedResponse carrying status + a body excerpt); `browseError` becomes `Ref<ApiProblem | Error | null>`; the EmptyState `detail` slot renders the real machine truth (the DevMisconfig message is already written to be actionable and currently dies in the console).

defects.defect: `loadingMore` is stranded TRUE for the session whenever any reload supersedes an in-flight cursor continuation. The load-more affordance dies permanently and two developing plates sit at the foot of the wall forever; palettes 51+ become unreachable.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:112 `finally { if (gen === loadGeneration) loadingMore.value = false; }` — the generation guard is correct for the append and wrong for the flag; :98 then rejects every future click and nothing else ever writes the flag false. Pane is KeepAlive'd (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:126). Unit: `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/probe-c.vitest.config.ts` → `Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 6 passed (6)`. Live: probe-C-live-r2.mjs → `"afterRace": { "cards": 50, "strandedSkeletonVisible": true, "loadMoreButtonCount": 0 }`; frame r2-stranded-loadmore.png.
defects.mechanism: Lifecycle state guarded by the wrong variable — a generational guard applied to an inflight flag that is not generational state.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse with a commons that reports hasMore. Click "More from the commons", then type one character in the search box while page 2 is in flight (the 400ms debounce at usePaletteWiring.ts:162 bumps loadGeneration). Release page 2. The button never returns for the rest of the session. Reproduced live and in 2 unit probes.
defects.proposedCure: `finally { loadingMore.value = false; }` unconditionally; keep the `gen` guard on the append only. Idiomatically: fold cursor + inflight + error into one `usePagedResource` state machine so "in flight" cannot outlive its request.

defects.defect: A keyset cursor minted under filter-set A is sent to the server together with filter-set B, so the "next page" is not the continuation of the current result set and rows are skipped silently.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:103 `listPalettes({ ...currentFilterOpts(), cursor })` re-derives filters at send time. Measured (probe-C-live-r3.mjs): `"G_debounceWindow": { "requests": ["?limit=50&cursor=page-2&sort=newest&q=ab", "?limit=50&sort=newest&q=ab"] }` — the cursor came from the UNFILTERED stream, the q is new. Server keyset windows on (createdAt,_id): api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:147-151.
defects.mechanism: Lifecycle state guarded by the wrong variable — cursor identity is not bound to the filter set that minted it.
defects.reproduction: Type 2+ characters in "Search the commons…" and click "More from the commons" within the 400ms debounce window. Measured request: `?limit=50&cursor=page-2&sort=newest&q=ab`.
defects.proposedCure: Store the cursor together with the opts that minted it (`nextCursor: { cursor, opts }`) and send the captured opts; invalidate the cursor whenever the filter set changes.

defects.defect: The error plate can never render when the wall is non-empty: a failed search/sort/tier reload leaves the stale wall on screen with no error at all, while the load-more button silently vanishes.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:62 `v-else-if="pm.browseError.value && displayedBrowse.length === 0"`; useBrowsePalettes.ts:77-82 never clears `remotePalettes` on failure; BrowsePane.vue:133 gates load-more on `!pm.browseError.value`. Probe C-3 (passing): `expect(b.browseError.value).toBe("Failed to load palettes"); expect(b.filteredBrowse.value.length).toBe(50);`
defects.mechanism: Typed failure swallowed — an error state whose only rendering path is gated on a condition the error itself cannot produce.
defects.reproduction: Load the wall (50 rows), then make the next reload fail (type a search while the backend 500s). Unit-reproduced in probe-C1-loadingMore-stuck.test.ts case C-3.
defects.proposedCure: Treat a failed RELOAD as distinct from an empty wall: render a non-blocking band with an inline retry over the retained wall; the full plate owns only the empty-and-failed case.

defects.defect: `cardRefs` is a write-only registry: Vue's null-on-unmount ref call is swallowed by the `el &&` short-circuit, so the map grows unboundedly for the session inside a KeepAlive'd pane and pins dead component instances. Feedback written to a stale entry is silently lost.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`, :209 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`. probe-C4-cardrefs-leak.test.ts (passing): `expect(Object.keys(cardRefs).length).toBe(154)` after 4 list changes; `expect(cardRefs.a.$.isUnmounted).toBe(true)`; `cardRefs.a.showFeedback("Saved!")` produces no DOM. Same idiom copy-pasted at PalettesPane.vue:84. Consumers: BrowsePane.vue:228, 237, 249, 264.
defects.mechanism: Lifecycle state never released — a parent-held imperative handle map with no release path.
defects.reproduction: Search, paginate, or change sort so the rendered slug set changes; the map retains every slug ever rendered. Unit-reproduced with the verbatim idiom (2 probes, including a passing control that shows the null branch releases correctly).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the registry. Card feedback is card-local state driven by a prop/event, not by reaching through a parent-held instance handle. (Minimal patch: `if (el) cardRefs[slug] = el; else delete cardRefs[slug]`.)

defects.defect: "Find by Color" is a second, line-for-line copy of the server's OKLab matcher that runs against only the ≤50 loaded rows and issues zero network requests — the commons is not searched.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:339-355 (radius 0.15 hard-coded; `(p: any)`; comment at :353-354 admits the API supports it server-side) vs api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-181 `colorMatcherFor` (`query.colorRadius ?? 0.15`). The client already types the params: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:47-50. Measured (probe-C-live-r3.mjs): `"requestsIssuedByColorSearch": 3` — unchanged from before the search, i.e. zero requests issued.
defects.mechanism: App-scoped/data-shape cousin — a duplicated predicate and duplicated constant with no shared source, running on the wrong side of the wire.
defects.reproduction: Open Filters → Find by Color → pick #00ff00 → Search on a 50-row wall of red palettes: wall goes to 0, network tab shows no request.
defects.proposedCure: Thread colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius into `currentFilterOpts()` and delete `displayedBrowse` + `colorSearchParams` outright, so the colour filter composes with the cursor, sort and tag/tier set instead of fighting them.

defects.defect: A zero-RESULT search renders the TRUE-EMPTY invitation ("No published palettes here yet. / Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall.") on a commons with 50 published palettes — and "More from the commons" is still offered directly underneath it.
defects.evidence: Measured twice: probe-C-live-r2 `"zeroResultSearch": { "cards": 0, "eyebrow": true, "copy": true, "hint": true }`; probe-C-live-r3 `"H_colorSearchNoMatch": { "wallCards": 0, "trueEmptyInvitation": true, "hint": true, "loadMoreStillOffered": 1 }`. The load-more block at BrowsePane.vue:132-144 lives OUTSIDE PaletteCardGrid, so `empty` never suppresses it. Frames r2-zero-result-search.png, r3-color-search-empty.png.
defects.mechanism: App-scoped/data-shape cousin — three distinct states (empty commons / no results for this query / error) collapsed into two plates.
defects.reproduction: On a loaded wall, type `zzzzqqq` in "Search the commons…" (or run a colour search that matches nothing). Both measured live.
defects.proposedCure: Three states, three plates: empty commons / no results for THIS query (with a clear-filters action) / error. Gate the load-more block on `displayedBrowse.length > 0`.

defects.defect: One `searchQuery` ref drives both simultaneously-visible panes: typing in "Search the commons…" filters My Palettes in the right pane and overwrites its own search box.

defects.defect: The pane has no live region at all, and both loading blocks put `aria-label` on a role-less `div` (role=generic), where ARIA in HTML prohibits naming — so the loading states are nameless and silent, and no async result is ever announced.

defects.defect: The colour search field silently searches a DIFFERENT colour than the one typed: anything that is not exactly 6 hex digits — including its own placeholder's `hsl(...)`, plus `red`, `#f00`, `oklch(...)` — is discarded and replaced by the swatch's current hex, with no error and no hint.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, running as declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1/D-2/D-3 are one mechanism: the component is written as an instrument on top of a producer primitive that glass-ui 7 deliberately reduced to a decoration. `WatercolorDot` is now `inheritAttrs:false`, renders one hard `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">` with no `<slot/>`, and exposes only `{color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}` — so the add-current-color CTA's `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click` and `<Plus>` glyph are ALL dropped (measured: `tag:"span"`, `ariaHidden:"true"`, `pointerEvents:"none"`, `tabIndex:-1`, `childSvgNonFilter:0`). The empty state's only affordance is an unmarked, inert, unnamed dashed blob. Compounding it, the desktop swatch action menu (`.floating-panel`, a phantom class defined nowhere) computes `position:static` and lays out at `{x:0,y:900,w:1440,h:40}` — one full viewport below the fold, transparent, `aria-hidden` — so Edit/Copy/Remove are unreachable by every modality. Net: a populated 5-colour draft exposes to keyboard/AT exactly two things: a text field and a button with accessible name "".
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative evidence recorded in the report's "What is genuinely right" section: motion is fully tokenized on the house `vj-enter` family with a global `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` guard and measured-identical reduced-motion geometry; zero horizontal overflow / zero page errors / one `<main>` across all 11 scenarios including 24 colours at 390px; forced-colors preserves the specimen faces via producer `forced-color-adjust:none`; dark scheme passes contrast at 10.85:1; `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean; Vue 3.5 idioms correct — reactive props destructure + `toRef(() => …)` across the composable boundary.)
