result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: R2.1 — With a healthy commons and ten palettes on the wall, a keyboard user cannot open a single one, in either engine. The palette card root is a clickable `role="article"` div with `tabIndex:-1`, `cursor:pointer` and zero `aria-pressed` seats; 30 consecutive Tab presses in WebKit AND Chromium never land on a palette (cardFocusable 0/10, tabHitArticle 0/30, 22 tab stops all belonging to search/filters/vote/menu). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 forbids the exact construction by name: "not a clickable `role=article` … One native named `<button type=\"button\">` spans its specimen/identity region". This is also WCAG 2.1.1. It is invisible to every existing audit capture because all sixty of them are the error arm; it overturns Round 1's own negative-proof row that declined to born-RED the keyboard gap for want of a two-engine proof.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four hypotheses were killed by measurement and are recorded so no later seat re-litigates them. (1) SEED TINT REFUTED BY EXPERIMENT: I suspected §2's "Seed tint is forbidden outside the ambient field" from the maroon cast in the dark captures; loading #/browse in dark with a pink seed and with oklch(60% 0.18 195) yields byte-identical surfaces — pane oklab(0.395241 0.00968 0.016528/.7536), card oklab(0.345296 0.010372 0.017546) in BOTH. The warmth is a fixed neutral pole (OKLab C≈0.019, h≈59°) plus the ambient field through the pane alpha. Hypothesis withdrawn. (2) MOTION IS SOUND: vj-morph is fully tokenized (--duration-fast measured 0.2s) and globally PRM-guarded (animations.css:184,202); under reducedMotion:"reduce" both engines report ONLY the six scroll-scrubbed pane-header-* animations, which are position-mapped scrubs with the reasoning documented in PaneHeader.vue; the infinite metal-shimmer-sweep correctly disappears under PRM; no layout-forcing property animates (--vj-morph-collapse unset → max-height none→none, an inert leg). (3) NO HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW: overflowX 0 in all four populated matrices, matching the ten audit matrices incl. RTL desktop, RTL mobile and 200% zoom. (4) ONE MAIN LANDMARK: mains:1 in every matrix despite two panes co-mounted. Also sound: verbatimModuleSyntax is clean (BrowsePane.vue:197 `import type` is the file's only type-only import), and useBrowsePalettes.ts:64,72,77 uses a real loadGeneration counter to drop stale responses.

defects.defect: The palette seat is pointer-only: the card root is a clickable `role="article"` div with tabIndex:-1 and no aria-pressed seat, so the route's primary action (open a palette) is unreachable by keyboard in both shipping engines.
defects.evidence: shots/STATES-2ENGINE.json, identical WebKit + Chromium: {"cardCount":10,"cardFocusable":0,"cardRoles":["article"],"cardCursor":["pointer"],"ariaPressed":0,"tabStops":22,"tabHitArticle":0}. Source: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:5-26 (bare div, @click="$emit('click')", no keydown, no tabindex); consumer elects it at demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:97 and :102. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102.
defects.mechanism: Selection/activation modelled as a click handler on a non-focusable container instead of a named native button seat; the producer comment at PaletteCard.vue:2-4 encodes a false dichotomy ("button semantics omitted because inner interactive controls must be reachable") that the constitution already answers by putting the button INSIDE as a sibling of the nested controls.
defects.reproduction: Serve #/browse with a reachable commons; press Tab 30x; observe document.activeElement never has role="article". Reproduced in webkit and chromium via docs/.../BrowsePane/shots/STATES-2ENGINE.json (MT-F022 two-engine proof).
defects.proposedCure: One native named `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` spanning the specimen+identity region inside the article; pressed true iff that palette is the selected-inspector identity, at most one true. Delete expandedId/toggleExpand and move detail/actions into the selected inspector that §3.1 already specifies. Not a tabindex="0" patch on the div — that would manufacture a focusable non-button.

defects.defect: All ten Browse captures in the mega-tranche visual audit are the error arm, so REPORT.md's /#/browse row measures an error page, not a palette wall — the component's primary state has zero rendered evidence.
defects.evidence: REPORT.md:121/136/151/166 rows for /#/browse (text 280/124, smallTapTargets 4, namelessButtons 0) all correspond to "The commons is unreachable". Live console at localhost:9000: "DevMisconfigError: value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED: http://localhost:9000 has no VITE_API_URL and is targeting the cross-origin production API (https://api.color.babb.dev), whose CORS allow-list excludes localhost" at demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:138:9.
defects.mechanism: The capture harness ran against a web-only dev server whose transport guard short-circuits every palette request before fetch; nothing in the harness asserts that a data-bearing route actually bore data, so the matrix went green on a uniformly degraded page.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/*/browse.png — all ten render the error plate. Confirmed live: curl https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50 returns 10 rows, so the commons was healthy the whole time.
defects.proposedCure: The visual harness must fail a route whose primary content did not render, not screenshot the fallback. Add a per-route data precondition (e.g. expect >=1 [role=article] on /#/browse) and run the matrix against the local stack or an explicit VITE_API_URL. Re-capture all Browse/Library/Admin matrices before any of them is cited as a pass.

defects.defect: In dark mode the palette specimen — the route's protagonist — renders at 1.41:1 against its own card, versus 12.58:1 in light. There is no design for a dark specimen on a dark stage.
defects.evidence: Pixel-sampled from shots/populated-desktop-{dark,light}.png (DPR2, x=900): dark strip rgb(36,31,31) vs card body rgb(66,55,47) = 1.41:1; light same strip vs rgb(233,225,217) = 12.58:1. Strip geometry: h-10 = 40px of a 100px card, 458px full bleed. 4 of 10 live palettes carry the single color lab(12.23 2.53 0.5). WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1.
defects.mechanism: The specimen well follows the scheme instead of guaranteeing a contrast floor against the specimen it hosts; §2 assumes "the specimen supplies color" without an arm for a specimen darker than the stage.
defects.reproduction: Open shots/populated-desktop-dark.png — the top four cards read as empty dark rectangles. Sample any pixel in the strip band vs the card body below it.
defects.proposedCure: Make the specimen stage scheme-INVERTED rather than scheme-following: a constant light plate under the strip in both schemes, or a producer-owned specimen-well tier that guarantees >=3:1 against any member color. Not a per-card border patch — the stage is the wrong tier.

defects.defect: The entity card is a hand-styled div wearing three stacked zero-blur cartoon casters, against a ratified tuple that specifies shadow=false and a prohibition on "cartoon casters stacked within casters"; the pane adds a fourth caster.
defects.evidence: Live computed style of the card root: class="group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer", boxShadow = oklab(.28 .0168 .0249/.32) -3px 3px 0 0, oklab(...)/.26 -5px 5px 0 0, oklab(...)/.18 -7px 7px 0 0. Pane root: 8px 8px 0px 0px, alpha .8. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:54 (tuple, shadow=false) and :186 ("not cartoon casters stacked within casters"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-05.
defects.mechanism: The card was built as a bespoke div with a decoration atom (cartoon-surface) instead of the ratified glass-ui Card tuple, so the tuple's shadow=false clause has no enforcement point.
defects.reproduction: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[role=article]')).boxShadow on a populated #/browse. Forced-colors consequence: box-shadow is not WHCM-adjusted, so visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/browse.png shows the caster surviving as a solid black slab while every other surface flattens.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the bespoke div with the ratified Card tuple exactly ({size:sm, material:content, tier:quiet, surface:opaque, shadow:false, grain:false, specular:off}) and delete cartoon-surface from the entity site; retire the pane's own 8px caster under the same PR-05 row so the route paints zero caster layers.

defects.defect: The sort-pending state is `opacity-50` string-concatenated into a child's class prop, which drops palette identity text from 13.52:1 to 3.11:1 — below the AA floor — while leaving the grid fully interactive.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:87-90: `:grid-class="'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')"`. Measured live: ink rgb(28,25,23) on card rgb(233,225,217) = 13.52:1 at rest; composited at opacity .5 over pane fill rgba(238,231,222,.169) = 3.11:1. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 ("a token name is not evidence"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08.
defects.mechanism: A pending state expressed in the alpha channel of the whole subtree rather than as a designed status; compounded by building a child's root class list with string concatenation (owner edict 5, per-instance override).
defects.reproduction: Trigger a sort change on a populated #/browse; sample the palette-name ink against the card while pm.sortLoading is true.
defects.proposedCure: Sort-pending reports into the status region R2.5 creates; the field keeps full opacity. If a visual pending cue is wanted, it belongs to the producer's own pending register, not to a consumer-authored opacity utility.

defects.defect: There is no status region anywhere in the Browse pane: five independent filters and a pager change the result count and nothing is announced, and no visible result count exists at all.
defects.evidence: shots/STATES-2ENGINE.json: "liveRegions": 0 in both WebKit and Chromium, across skeleton/wall/empty/error. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:114 (§5.1), row "in-route filter, tab, selection, or pagination" — "announce changed result count/state through the owning status region".
defects.mechanism: Every state signal in the pane is a rendered plate (skeleton, empty, error) rather than an announced status, so filter transitions have no semantic channel; there is also no receptacle for the pending/failure truth PR-08 requires.
defects.reproduction: Populated #/browse: type a query that removes all results; query the DOM for [aria-live] inside the pane — zero nodes, and the result count never appears.
defects.proposedCure: One durable status region owned by the field, driven by a discriminated state union (idle/loading/loaded(n)/filtered(n of m)/error(cause)). Sort-pending (R2.4), filtered-empty (Round 1 D-06), load-more failure (D-07), stale sort (D-08) and operation verdicts (D-17) all report into it instead of into five ad-hoc surfaces.

defects.defect: The route's primary control — the commons search field, and the first tab stop in the pane — has no accessible name; a placeholder is not a name.
defects.evidence: shots/STATES-2ENGINE.json: "searchNamed": false in both engines; "nameless": ["INPUT.input-bar-field rect=373x24.87"]. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 ("Role, accessible name, state/value ... are explicit"). The audit missed it because REPORT.md:94's namelessButtons metric counts only <button>.
defects.mechanism: The glass-ui SearchBar is consumed with a placeholder only (BrowsePane.vue:10-14); no aria-label or associated <label> is supplied at the consumer site and none is defaulted by the producer.
defects.reproduction: Populated #/browse: document.querySelector('.pane-scroll-fade input') has no aria-label and no labels; Tab once into the pane to land on it unnamed.
defects.proposedCure: Name it at the producer (SearchBar takes a required accessible name) so all three consumer sites inherit, rather than adding an aria-label per instance.

defects.defect: Ten vote controls render at 38.63 x 23.59 CSS px on mobile — below the 24px target floor — immediately beside sibling menu buttons roughly twice their size; and data marks are visually indistinguishable from action marks in the same row.
defects.evidence: shots/TELEMETRY.json, iPhone 14, ten instances: BUTTON.flex 38.63x23.59 name="0 votes, click to vote". WCAG 2.5.8 minimum is 24x24. Row composition: `1  fork2  heart0  ...` mixes two data marks and two action marks at identical weight (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 law 5). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-12.
defects.mechanism: Target geometry follows the glyph rung instead of being an independent quantity, so a compact count+heart cluster inherits a sub-floor block size while its neighbour inherits a generous one.
defects.reproduction: Load #/browse at 390px with data and measure the vote buttons. Note this also means REPORT.md's smallTapTargets:4 for /#/browse understates the populated route by ten, because it was measured on the error page.
defects.proposedCure: Separate visible glyph size from operable seat geometry (PR-12's own wording) so both actions in the cluster meet the floor at the same optical rung, and give the two data marks a non-actionable register so the operable ones are identifiable.

defects.defect: `.pane-scroll-fade` implements no fade: maskImage is `none`, so the pane hard-clips the last card through its color strip — a class whose name asserts an affordance the CSS never delivers.
defects.evidence: getComputedStyle(pane).maskImage === "none" and -webkit-mask-image === "none" on the live pane. The rule at demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:44-47 sets only `contain: layout style paint` and `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll`. Visible at the bottom of both shots/populated-desktop-*.png: the sixth card is sliced mid-strip by a hard horizontal cut.
defects.mechanism: The class was renamed or repurposed away from its original masking job while nine consumers kept applying it for the fade it no longer performs; the same h-full scroll host also stretches the empty plate (Round 1 D-13).
defects.reproduction: Open shots/populated-desktop-light.png and look at the pane's bottom edge; then read the .pane-scroll-fade rule.
defects.proposedCure: Either restore the mask at the host or rename the class to what it does (`pane-scroll-host`). A hard cut through a color specimen reads as a rendering fault and must not be the designed boundary; the scroll host and the fade should be decided together with the empty-plate stretch.

defects.defect: Two import paths to the same design system inside one 360-line file: Card/Button via one-line `demo/ui/*` re-export barrels, SearchBar direct from @mkbabb/glass-ui.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:180 `import { Card } from "../ui/card"`, :181 `import { Button } from "../ui/button"`, :195 `import { SearchBar } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/search"`. demo/ui/card/index.ts and demo/ui/button/index.ts are each exactly one line re-exporting from @mkbabb/glass-ui. Census: 18 of 19 demo/ui/* barrels are pure one-line re-exports. Owner edicts 2 and 4.
defects.mechanism: A migration-era indirection layer was never deleted after the direct glass-ui imports landed, so both paths are live and this file demonstrates each.
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/card/index.ts; cat demo/ui/button/index.ts; then read BrowsePane.vue:180-195.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the 18 pure re-export barrels and rewrite consumers to import from @mkbabb/glass-ui directly (owner edict: migrate the consumer at the root, no compat shim). Repo-wide family; BrowsePane is a site, not the owner.

defects.defect: `availableTags` masks an API contract violation client-side instead of fixing the payload, and the comment admits it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:215-220 coerces `Tag[] | Record<string, Tag>` with Object.values; the comment states the declared type is `Tag[]` "but the `/colors/tags` read can resolve an object-shaped payload at runtime". Owner edict 2 bans masking fallbacks by name.
defects.mechanism: A prop-type warning was silenced at the consumer rather than at the endpoint, so the real defect (an endpoint returning two shapes) is hidden from every future reader and from the API's tests.
defects.reproduction: Read BrowsePane.vue:210-220; the comment is the reproduction — the coercion exists because the object-shaped branch is real.
defects.proposedCure: Fix /colors/tags to return one shape and delete the coercion; if the shape genuinely varies, that belongs in a typed transport boundary with a test, not in a pane's computed.

defects.defect: Round 1's D-01 (one Retry click permanently blanks the pane via mode="out-in") is structurally corroborated: the state container has no height reserve at exactly the moment it is empty.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:29 the state container is `<div class="grid gap-3 pb-3">` with no min-height; the only reserve, `min-h-[120px]`, lives ON PaletteCardGrid (demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue) which is unmounted during the leave of a mode="out-in" swap. Round 1 measured the blank window to 25ms twice with screenshots in ./evidence/.
defects.mechanism: DOM presence made a function of an animation clock, with the reserve attached to the branch rather than to the container that outlives both branches.
defects.reproduction: NONE re-run by Round 2 — I did not re-measure the blank window; Round 1's reproduction stands and this is the structural half of the same cure.
defects.proposedCure: Stop animating branch identity (cross-fade content in one persistent region), and put the reserve on the container that survives both branches rather than on a branch.

defects.defect: The `Featured` badge runs an infinite 5s shimmer with no pause control.
defects.evidence: Live getAnimations(): {n:"metal-shimmer-sweep", iterations:null, duration:5000, target:"badge-atom inline-flex items-c..."}. result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface (subject: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited. Model receipt is the first section of the report.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Four BLOCKERs, three MAJORs, one MINOR cluster and one INFO, all with reproductions.
result.strongestDefect: L-3 — the dead component holds the live application's ONLY login-error surface, so every login failure is silent on every breakpoint. `useSlugMigration.ts:83-87` routes all four error branches through `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; `slugBarRef` (declared at :30, typed to PaletteSlugBar) is never bound in any template (App.vue binds only showMigrateDialog/migrateMode/onMigrateRespond at :153-156), so `.value` is permanently null and all four calls are no-ops. The live twin SlugEditLayer.vue declares `slugError` at :13, writes it at :49,59-62, and never renders it (template :75-119 contains no reference) — and calls `pm.onSlugSwitch()` un-awaited at :54 so its own catch can never fire. Reproduced live at http://localhost:9000: submitted a nonexistent 4-segment slug through the dock Login flow; result `{destructive: 0, slugInputValue: "", matchingLines: [unrelated OKLCh docs prose]}` — no error node, no alert, and the input self-cleared (the SUCCESS affordance) while the login had failed. A user-facing BLOCKER whose cause is purely structural: no amount of correct code inside PaletteSlugBar.vue could have prevented it, because the shell has not mounted that component since the D.W3 restructure.

defects.defect: Login failure is silent in the live application on every breakpoint, because the only error surface is a defineExpose on the dead component reached through a template ref that is never bound. The S.W2·W2-6 typed-ApiProblem fix repaired already-unreachable code, and the live twin's own error ref is write-only.
defects.evidence: useSlugMigration.ts:30 `const slugBarRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteSlugBar>|null>(null)`; :83-87 all four failure branches call `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`. `grep -n migration demo/color-picker/App.vue` → only :153 showMigrateDialog, :155 migrateMode, :156 onMigrateRespond — slugBarRef never bound, and appears in no template repo-wide. SlugEditLayer.vue:13 declares slugError, writes it at :49,:59-62, template :75-119 never renders it; :54 calls pm.onSlugSwitch() un-awaited so its catch at :57-65 is unreachable. LIVE REPRO on http://localhost:9000 (dock Login → 'nonexistent-fake-bogus-slugword' → submit → 2.5s): {"slugEditLayerOpen":true,"destructive":0,"slugInputValue":"","matchingLines":["OKLCh is the polar form of OKLab…"],"ariaLive":[{role:alert,text:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"}]} — zero .text-destructive nodes, no login error in any alert/status region, and the input SELF-CLEARED (the success affordance).

defects.reproduction: npm run dev; http://localhost:9000; click the dock Login control; type any nonexistent 4-lowercase-segment slug; submit; observe zero error feedback and a cleared input. Statically: `grep -rn slugBarRef demo` shows it is declared and read but never bound to a template.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 directories, 19 files, 29 lines total — every one a pure alias re-export of a glass-ui primitive that glass-ui 7.0.0 already ships on its own subpath. This is precisely the alias/back-compat shim owner edict 2 forbids, and demo/ui/alert/index.ts self-documents the motive ("the two consumers import from this barrel unchanged"). PaletteSlugBar reaches glass-ui through THREE different idioms in one 14-line import block: subpath, demo alias, and the 43-chunk root barrel.
defects.evidence: `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → one line: `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. `find demo/ui -type f | wc -l` → 19; `find demo/ui -type f -exec wc -l {} + | tail -1` → 29 total. All 19 have a matching glass-ui subpath (verified against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json exports, v7.0.0). demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9 documents the shim rationale verbatim. Consumers: 92 import statements across 81 files (`grep -rn 'from "[^\"]*ui/(button|popover|dropdown-menu|...)"' demo | wc -l` → 92; `grep -rln 'from "[^\"]*ui/' demo | wc -l` → 81). PaletteSlugBar.vue:132-145 mixes @mkbabb/glass-ui/search (subpath), ../../../ui/button + ../../../ui/popover (alias), @mkbabb/glass-ui (root). Barrel fan-out measured: root glass-ui.js imports 43 distinct chunks vs search.js 7; sideEffects is ["*.css"] and `grep -cE 'import\s*\"[^\"]*\.css\"' glass-ui.js` → 0.
defects.mechanism: a compatibility alias layer retained as a structural fiction; it also breaks the demo's value as a dogfood, because the imports a real external consumer would write are not the imports the demo writes
defects.reproduction: `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts`; `find demo/ui -type f -exec wc -l {} + | tail -1`; the two grep counts above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entire and rewrite the 92 imports to glass-ui subpaths (@mkbabb/glass-ui/button, /popover, /dropdown-menu, …). Mechanical single pass; it removes 19 alias files and makes demo consumption byte-identical to an external consumer's. NOTE (labelled hypothesis, NOT measured): the bundle-size effect of the 43-chunk root reach is unproven — I did not run a comparative build. The consistency defect stands independently.

defects.defect: Direction of dependency is inverted: the app SHELL depends on the PALETTES feature for the application's identity surface. Five shell files value-import SESSION_PORT_KEY from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts, whose symbol is literally Symbol("palette.session"). A type back-edge runs the other way (palettes → shell) for a single `as` cast, making the two top-level areas mutually dependent. usePalettePorts.ts is also a god module: 275 lines, 5 injection ports, built from 15 composables.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'from "\.\./*.*palettes/' demo/shell/` → 5 files / 8 edges: DockViewSelect.vue, Dock.vue, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue, menus/ProfileSection.vue, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue — all importing ../palettes/usePalettePorts. usePalettePorts.ts:271 `export const SESSION_PORT_KEY: InjectionKey<SessionPort> = Symbol("palette.session")`. Reverse edge: usePalettePorts.ts:19 `import type { ViewId } from "../shell/useViewManager"`, used at :34, :35 and — load-bearingly — only for the cast at :88 `setActiveTab: (tab: string) => depsSwitchView(tab as ViewId)`. usePalettePorts.ts is 275 lines (wc -l), imports 15 composables (:4-18), provides 5 ports (:242-246); PORT 1·Session's inputs all come from demo/platform/auth/ (:5-7), so it is pure pass-through of another area's state under a third area's key.
defects.mechanism: the identity port was namespaced, owned and provided by whichever feature happened to need it first; the shell then injected it, inverting the chrome→feature direction
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'palettes/' demo/shell/ | grep -E 'import|from'` → 8 edges; `grep -n 'ViewId' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts` → :19,:34,:35,:88.
defects.proposedCure: Move identity below both areas: new demo/platform/auth/useIdentity.ts exporting IDENTITY_KEY = Symbol("identity") with { userSlug, isAdmin, lastError, login, logout, regenerate }; provided by App.vue. Move useSlugMigration.ts from demo/palettes/ to demo/platform/auth/. PORT 1·Session leaves usePalettePorts (5 ports → 4). Kill the ViewId edge by moving post-login view switching to App.vue (the composition root already owns the router), which removes both the cross-area type import and the `as` cast. Result: shell → platform/auth and palettes → platform/auth, both strictly downward; the shell↔palettes cycle dissolves.

defects.defect: The client re-derives the SERVER-owned slug format with a hand-written regex, duplicated in two files, with no shared constant and no contract test. Currently sound — no failing input exists at HEAD — so this is filed as a labelled hypothesis, not a live bug.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:185 === SlugEditLayer.vue:26: /^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/. Server authority api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts:84-90 generateSlug() = `${adj}-${verb}-${color}-${animal}`. I scanned every word literal in that file: total 515, failing /^[a-z]+$/ = ["node:crypto","findBySlug","Failed to generate unique slug after max retries"] — i.e. all 512 real words pass. No live bug.
defects.mechanism: a format contract owned by the server, re-implemented client-side without a shared definition or a test pinning the two together
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a hypothesis. No input at HEAD exhibits it. The failure would require a hyphenated or non-[a-z] word added to any of the four server word lists (e.g. "off-white"), after which a legitimate slug would classify as an ADMIN TOKEN and route to adminLogin instead of userLogin.
defects.proposedCure: Single-source the shape in demo/platform/auth/slugFormat.ts (SLUG_SEGMENTS + isSlug), and add a contract test that imports api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts and asserts generateSlug() satisfies isSlug() across N samples — which turns a latent format drift into a red test.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, area palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the tag-filter checkboxes are bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not have (its contract is `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). `update:selectedTags` never emits, so selecting a tag filters nothing; and because the control runs uncontrolled it visibly fills in AND flips `aria-checked` to "true", so it confirms an action it did not perform to sighted and AT users alike. Both `<Checkbox>` sites in the entire demo (SearchFilterBar.vue:51, TagEditPopover.vue:27) are miswired identically — the demo's Checkbox integration has a 0% working rate.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded anyway (§8 of the report), including two claims I formed and then DISPROVED: (a) the five `role="radio"` buttons DO get accessible names via implicit `<label>` wrapping — Chromium a11y tree reads `radio "Newest" [checked]`, `radio "Most Popular"`, `radio "Most Forked"`, `radio "All" [checked]`, `radio "Featured"` — retracted; (b) no radio hit-box overlap: live rects 44x44 at y 422-466, 479-523, 536-580, 13px clear — retracted. Also sound: every tap target >=24x24 (trigger 32x40, radios 44x44, swatch 28x28, input 148x36, Search 52.6x24), so this component contributes ZERO rows to the visual REPORT's 60 small-tap-targets (the 4 on /#/browse are PaletteSlugBar's); popover self-names correctly (`dialog "Filters"`, aria-haspopup/aria-expanded via reka); RadioGroup wiring is CORRECT (P7: `update:tier: [[""]]`) — the control proving C-1 is a real asymmetry not a harness artifact; verbatimModuleSyntax compliant (`import type { Tag }` line 144); Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure correct, no defineModel so no stale-read hazard; zero rAF/WebGL/ValueUnit/timers/listeners/observers — no cleanup owed, PRM-RAF clean; `.section-label` + `scrollbar-thin` are real glass-ui utilities (demo/styles/utils.css:13, glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/base.css); root-level styling, no shadcn-root override; edicts 1/3/4/5/6 clean; eslint clean.

defects.defect: Tag-filter checkboxes bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, which glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not expose (contract is `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). `:checked` degrades to a dead DOM attribute, `@update:checked` listens for an event never emitted, and the component runs uncontrolled — so it visibly toggles and flips aria-checked to "true" while `update:selectedTags` never fires and nothing filters. The prop-driven initial state is also ignored (a selected tag renders unchecked).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts (CheckboxProps has modelValue/defaultValue/disabled/value/id/class — no `checked`); compiled component node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js:451 `emits: ["update:modelValue"]`. Measured (vitest+@vue/test-utils mount of the real SFC): rendered HTML `<button data-slot="checkbox" checked="false" role="checkbox" aria-checked="false" data-state="unchecked">`; `emitted after click: ["click"]`, `update:selectedTags = undefined`; `before click data-state: unchecked aria-checked: false` -> `after click data-state: checked aria-checked: true` with `update:selectedTags emitted: undefined`; with props selectedTags=['a','b'], `checkbox aria-checked: [ 'false', 'false' ]`. Family: `grep -rn "<Checkbox" demo/` returns exactly 2 sites — SearchFilterBar.vue:51 and TagEditPopover.vue:27 — and `grep -rn "update:checked|:checked=" demo/` shows both miswired (SearchFilterBar.vue:52-53, TagEditPopover.vue:28-29).
defects.mechanism: prop/emit-name drift against a major design-system upgrade (glass-ui 7.0.0, W44 whole-major adoption) left unbound because vue-tsc runs with strictTemplates defaulted OFF, so unknown props/handlers fall through as attrs
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config <scratch>/probe.config.ts with a mount of demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (Popover/PopoverTrigger/PopoverContent stubbed open, availableTags=[{name:'warm'}]): click `[data-slot="checkbox"]` -> data-state flips unchecked->checked and aria-checked false->true, while w.emitted()['update:selectedTags'] is undefined. Latent in prod only because `curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` returns `[]` (HTTP 200), hiding the section via v-if at line 47; e2e/smoke/admin/flows/tag-create.spec.ts creates tags on every run.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the real contract: `:model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)"` (toggleTag already derives the next array from the prop, so the CheckedState payload is discardable); same repair at TagEditPopover.vue:28-29 where the payload IS used — `(checked) => onToggle(tag.name, checked === true)`. The gestalt cure is architectural, not per-site: set `"vueCompilerOptions": { "strictTemplates": true }` in tsconfig.base.json so the whole prop/emit-drift class becomes a compile error instead of silent runtime breakage.

defects.defect: The "Find by Color" text field is decorative. Everything outside `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i` — 3-digit hex, 8-digit hex, hsl()/oklch(), named colours, whitespace, outright garbage — is silently discarded and replaced by `pickerHex.value` (default `#4488cc`), after which the component sets colorSearchActive=true, increments the filter badge and emits, reporting success for a colour the user never asked for. The placeholder advertises the capability it drops (`placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"`).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (the ternary at line 218), placeholder line 92, pickerHex default line 170. Measured emissions, all bit-identical: `hsl(120 100% 50%)` -> [0.61358428709272,-0.04147814390571797,-0.11751090263911201]; `#f00` -> same; `not-a-color` -> same; `"   "` -> same; and `oklab(#4488cc) = [0.61358428709272,-0.04147814390571797,-0.11751090263911201]` — exact match. Control `#ff0000` -> [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585] (correct). The correct answers the guard threw away, measured through the SAME function: `oklab(hsl(120 100% 50%)) = [0.8664396175234368,-0.23388758093655815,0.1794984451609376]`, `oklab(#f00) = [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585]`. The parser is fully capable: SearchFilterBar.vue:206 -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:11 -> demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 (parseCssColor), which throws a typed PickerColorError on real failure (picker-color.ts:112) — the exact error signal the component discards.
defects.mechanism: masking fallback — a validity guard that substitutes a plausible wrong value for the error it should raise (owner edict 2: no masking fallbacks), gratuitously narrowing a stack that already parses full CSS L4
defects.reproduction: Mount SearchFilterBar (Popover stubbed open), `input[type=text].setValue('hsl(120 100% 50%)')` then `.trigger('keydown.enter')` -> emitted colorSearch payload is the OKLab of #4488cc, not of green. Repeat with '#f00', 'not-a-color', '   ' — identical payload each time; '#ff0000' is the only shape that works.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex and the fallback. Parse the trimmed text directly (rename hexToOklab -> cssToOklab, since it was never hex-only); on empty input or PickerColorError set a local `parseError` and DO NOT emit; render parseError into the polite aria-live region C-6 already requires. Net KISS deletion: one regex and one fallback out, one honest error branch in.

defects.defect: `applyColorSearch` is declared `async` but contains no `await`, so it runs to completion synchronously and `searching` goes true->false before Vue's scheduler ever runs. The Loader2 spinner, the `:disabled` state and the reentrancy guard are all unreachable dead code.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (async, no await), spinner line 102, `:disabled="searching"` line 98, guard line 214, Loader2 import line 142. Measured: `Search btn found: true  disabled attr: undefined`; `[sync after dispatch] spinner present: false`; `[after nextTick] spinner present: false`; `[after nextTick] Search label present: true`.
defects.mechanism: vestigial async ceremony around a synchronous computation — state that mutates and reverts within one tick can never be rendered
defects.reproduction: Mount SearchFilterBar, locate the button whose text is 'Search', trigger('click'), and inspect w.html() both synchronously after dispatch and after nextTick: 'animate-spin' is absent in both, and the button never carries a disabled attribute.
defects.proposedCure: The search IS synchronous — the OKLab distance filter is a `computed` in BrowsePane.vue:339-349. Delete `searching`, the `async`, the `finally`, the reentrancy guard, the `:disabled` and the Loader2 import. Reintroduce a real loading state only if the server-side colorL/colorA/colorB query noted at BrowsePane.vue:354 is adopted, i.e. only around a real await.

defects.defect: The "Clear all filters" button lives inside `v-if="activeFilterCount > 0"`; clicking it drives the count to zero, so the focused button unmounts itself and focus falls to <body> inside an open popover, breaking focus order and leaving the popover's focus scope with nothing to restore.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:110-120 (the v-if wrapper) and 227-232 (onClearAll); parent zeroing in demo/palettes/browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts onClearFilters. Measured with attachTo: document.body and real focus: `focus before: BUTTON "Clear all filters"` -> `Clear-all still in DOM: false` -> `focus after : BODY`. WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured).
defects.mechanism: a control whose own side effect destroys its mount condition — self-unmounting focused element with no focus transfer
defects.reproduction: Mount SearchFilterBar with tier='featured', focus the 'Clear all filters' button, trigger('click'), then setProps({tier:'', selectedTags:[]}) to mimic the parent response; document.activeElement is BODY.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the row mounted and disable it (`:disabled="activeFilterCount === 0"`) rather than v-if-ing it out — this also stops the popover from resizing under the pointer. Alternatively move focus explicitly to the popover content root before the state change.

defects.defect: Zero test coverage anywhere in the repo for this component, and the two automated gates that could have caught C-1 are structurally blind: vue-tsc runs with strictTemplates defaulted OFF (no vueCompilerOptions in any tsconfig), so unknown component props and unknown on* handlers are accepted as fallthrough attrs rather than errors; eslint reports nothing.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "SearchFilterBar|Find by Color|Search by CSS color|Clear all filters|aria-label=\"Filters\"" e2e/ test/ demo/test/` -> no output. `grep -rn "selectedTags|tierFilter|colorSearch|Most Forked|Featured" e2e/ test/` -> no output. `grep -rn "Filters|EllipsisVertical|filter-option|filter-section" e2e/ demo/test/ test/` -> no output (across 240 .spec.ts files + the whole vitest tree). `grep -n "vueCompilerOptions|strictTemplates" tsconfig.base.json tsconfig.demo.json tsconfig.lib.json` -> no output; typecheck script is package.json:65. `npx eslint demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue` -> clean, no output.
defects.mechanism: vacuous gate — coverage is zero rather than thin, and the type gate's one relevant switch is left at its permissive default, so a whole-major design-system swap could not surface prop/emit drift
defects.reproduction: The maximal vacuous mutation: delete the entire <PopoverContent> subtree (lines 16-122) and replace the whole <script setup> with `const emit = defineEmits<{}>()`. `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` both stay green, because no test references this component at all.
defects.proposedCure: Set `"vueCompilerOptions": { "strictTemplates": true }` in tsconfig.base.json — the single highest-leverage repair in this report, converting the entire prop/emit-drift class from silent runtime breakage into a compile error. Then add one e2e spec that opens the Filters popover and asserts: a tag checkbox click changes the wall, a non-hex CSS colour either searches that colour or refuses, and Clear-all does not drop focus to body.

defects.defect: Filter state is invisible to assistive technology: the trigger's aria-label="Filters" overrides the visible active-filter count badge, both role=radiogroup elements are unnamed (the "Sort"/"Tier" labels are unassociated divs), there is no aria-live for the async-feeling colour-search result, and the popover has no heading semantics.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:5 (aria-label) vs 7-12 (count span); section labels are plain divs at lines 20, 32, 48, 63. Measured in jsdom: `trigger aria-label: Filters` while `trigger text (badge): "3"`; `aria-live regions: 0`; `section-label elements are div (not heading): [ 'DIV','DIV','DIV','DIV' ]`. Measured live against http://localhost:9000/#/browse: `radiogroups: [{name: null}, {name: null}]`, `ariaLive: 0`, `headings: 0`; a11y tree shows `- generic: Sort` followed by an unnamed `radiogroup`, same for Tier.
defects.mechanism: accessible-name computation ignored — aria-label suppresses the subtree that carries the state, and visual adjacency substituted for programmatic association
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, click button[aria-label="Filters"], then evaluate over the [role=dialog]: querySelectorAll('[role=radiogroup]') both return null for aria-label/aria-labelledby; querySelectorAll('[aria-live]').length === 0. In jsdom, mount with tier='featured' selectedTags=['a','b'] and read the trigger's aria-label ('Filters') against its textContent ('3').
defects.proposedCure: `:aria-label="activeFilterCount > 0 ? `Filters, ${activeFilterCount} active` : 'Filters'"`; give each .section-label an id and point the matching RadioGroup at it with aria-labelledby (RadioGroupProps extends PrimitiveProps, so the attr falls through to the role=radiogroup root); add one polite aria-live region announcing the result count. All root-level, no per-instance overrides.

defects.defect: `hexToOklab` carries an unreachable defensive throw, and its name misrepresents what it does — it is a general CSS-colour-to-OKLab conversion, and discarding that generality is precisely defect C-2.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:205-211. Every reachable argument is either a regex-validated 6-digit hex (line 218) or pickerHex, and pickerHex can only ever be a 6-digit hex because MiniColorPicker.vue:85-105 computes currentHex from clamped HSV via `Math.round(c*255).toString(16).padStart(2,'0')`. No input can produce a "none" channel, so lines 207-209 are dead.
defects.mechanism: dead defensive code paired with a name that encodes the artificial narrowing rather than the real capability
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static reachability finding; the branch cannot be entered by any input the component accepts.
defects.proposedCure: Rename to cssToOklab, delete the "none"-channel throw, and let PickerColorError propagate to the user-facing error surface that C-2's cure introduces.

defects.defect: `colorSearchActive` is a private local ref that feeds the public activeFilterCount badge while duplicating state the parent already owns (BrowsePane's colorSearchParams), so the badge can report an active colour filter the parent cannot see or clear.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:171 (the ref), 193 (activeFilterCount reads it), against demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:336 `const colorSearchParams = ref<{L,a,b}|null>(null)` — the same fact, held twice. Measured: after a colour search the badge reads "1"; after a prop-side reset of tier/selectedTags the badge still reads "1".
defects.mechanism: unowned duplicated state — a derived public value computed partly from private state the owner of the other inputs cannot reach
defects.reproduction: Mount SearchFilterBar, run a colour search, read the trigger badge ('1'), then setProps({tier:'', selectedTags:[]}) and read it again ('1'). HYPOTHESIS on reachability in today's wiring: the only reset path currently routes through onClearAll, so no live user flow is known to hit the desync. The ownership defect itself is confirmed.
defects.proposedCure: Lift the colour filter to the parent as a prop (`colorFilter: {L,a,b} | null`) — BrowsePane already holds exactly that value. activeFilterCount then derives entirely from props, and C-9's double-emit collapses into one.

defects.defect: onClearAll emits both clearColorSearch and clearFilters, and BrowsePane's clearFilters handler clears colorSearchParams a second time — the colour filter is cleared twice per click.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:227-232 emits both; demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:329-332 `onClearFilters()` calls clearBrowseFilters() AND sets colorSearchParams.value = null. Measured: `emitted on clear: ["clearColorSearch","clearFilters","click"]`.
defects.mechanism: redundant event surface — two emits expressing one intent because the state is split across the boundary (see C-8)
defects.reproduction: Mount with tier='featured', click the 'Clear all filters' button, read Object.keys(w.emitted()).
defects.proposedCure: Collapse to a single `clearFilters` emit once C-8 lifts colorSearchActive into the parent; delete the clearColorSearch event from the emits declaration.

defects.defect: Repeated Search activations with unchanged input re-emit every time, each one re-running the full OKLab distance scan over every palette and every colour in the wall. No idempotence or debounce.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (no comparison against the last emitted value) driving demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:339-349 (`palettes.filter(... oklabColors.some(c => Math.hypot(...) <= radius))`). Measured: 5 identical clicks -> `colorSearch emissions for 5 identical clicks: 5`.
defects.mechanism: unguarded event emission driving an O(palettes x colours) recompute per activation
defects.reproduction: Mount SearchFilterBar, click the 'Search' button 5 times without touching the input, then read w.emitted()['colorSearch'].length -> 5.
defects.proposedCure: Compare against the last emitted OKLab triple and no-op when unchanged; small today, but it is the shape that does not survive a larger wall.

defects.defect: The filter popover can neither shrink nor scroll: max-height is none, overflow-y is visible, and there is no floating-ui `size` middleware — so once the tag list and the Clear-all row are present the content is projected to exceed a phone viewport with no way to reach the bottom.
defects.evidence: Measured live at 390x664 with the tag section absent: dialog height 441.5px; on the popover root `overflowY: "visible"`, `maxHeight: "none"`, `scrollHeight: 439` === `clientHeight: 439` (no inner scroll). Arithmetic: the tag block adds max-h-28 = 112px plus its section label and padding (~43px) and the Clear-all row adds ~44px -> ~640px against a 664px viewport.
defects.mechanism: popover sized by content with collision handling that can shift but not resize — no size middleware, no max-height, no inner scroll container on the content root
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. Not reproduced because the live tag catalog is empty (`curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` -> `[]`), so the tag block never renders. Separately I observed one transient 81.5px bottom overflow (dialog y=304, height 441.5, bottom 745.5 vs viewport 664) which floating-ui's collision shift then resolved to a fitting position — that transient is NOT reported as a defect.
defects.proposedCure: Give the popover content a `max-height: var(--reka-popover-content-available-height)` with `overflow-y: auto` on the content root (root-level, in the glass-ui PopoverContent variant rather than as a per-instance override), so the panel scrolls instead of clipping regardless of tag count.

defects.defect: An inert single-child flex wrapper and a dead Tailwind @reference directive.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:2 `<div class="flex items-center gap-1.5">` wraps exactly one child (the Popover), so gap-1.5 and items-center compute nothing. Line 236 `@reference "../../../styles/foundation.css"` opens a scoped block that uses no @apply and no theme() — only `var(--font-serif)`, `var(--type-small)`, `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--duration-fast)`, `var(--ease-standard)`, `color-mix(...)`.
defects.mechanism: vestigial scaffolding — layout and build directives retained past the structure that justified them
defects.reproduction: NONE — static reading of the template root and the scoped style block.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the wrapper div (the Popover can be the component root) and delete the @reference line.

defects.defect: Mixed emit idiom and a needless coercion: the template calls $emit(...) for sort and tier while the script holds a typed `emit` used everywhere else, and String(v) coerces a value the type system already guarantees is a string here.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:21 and :33 use `$emit`, against the typed `const emit = defineEmits<{...}>()` at line 154 used at lines 186, 202, 221, 230-231. `SelectionValue` is `string | number` per node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts, and every option value declared at lines 163-167 and 35/39 is a string literal.
defects.mechanism: idiom drift within a single file — two ways to say the same thing, plus a defensive coercion with no reachable non-string input
defects.reproduction: NONE — static reading.
defects.proposedCure: Use the typed `emit` uniformly and drop String(v); if the union genuinely needs narrowing later, narrow it at the handler signature rather than coercing at the call site.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (PaletteSlugBar.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context) — explicitly declared for this seat, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-2 — `@submit.prevent="onSlugSwitch"` is bound to glass-ui SearchBar, which sets `inheritAttrs: false` and re-spreads `$attrs` onto its inner `<input>`; a `submit` event never reaches an input, so the handler never fires and nothing calls preventDefault. Activating the login control performs a NATIVE GET form submission: measured URL `http://localhost:9000/#/extract` → `http://localhost:9000/?#/extract`, full SPA reload, `switchSlug` never emitted.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative results recorded in the report's hazard sweep: no rAF, no WebGL, no defineModel, no ValueUnit, no parseCssColor, no listeners/observers, no unbounded growth, verbatimModuleSyntax clean, animations preserved.)

defects.defect: The component renders on zero routes, and `useSlugMigration`'s `slugBarRef` is therefore never bound — making all four `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)` calls (the ONLY user-visible login-error copy in the app) permanent no-ops.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:1; `grep -rn "SlugBar\|slug-bar" --include=*.vue --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules` returns only the barrel export, the `import type` in useSlugMigration.ts:6, the ref decl at useSlugMigration.ts:30 and an e2e prose comment — no `<PaletteSlugBar>` tag anywhere. usePalettePorts.ts:126-135 does not re-export slugBarRef. Visual-audit negative proof over 60 Safari captures: `grep -c` in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json → "Account menu" 0, "Sign in with slug" 0, "Cancel slug edit" 0, "Copy slug" 0, while the live twin's "Switch to slug" = 60.
defects.mechanism: Orphaned surface left by the D.W3 Lane A restructure; the composable's error plumbing was never re-homed to the surviving dock surface (SlugEditLayer.vue, which writes slugError at lines 49/59-62 and never renders it).
defects.reproduction: grep the repo for a `<PaletteSlugBar` template usage — zero hits; then `grep -c "Account menu" docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json` → 0 across all 60 captures.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/palettes/browser/slug/ and its barrel line; move error RENDERING into SlugEditLayer.vue and change the session port's `onSlugSwitch` to return Promise<void> so the layer awaits and renders its own failure — retiring the reach-through-a-template-ref idiom entirely.

defects.defect: `@submit.prevent="onSlugSwitch"` binds to glass-ui SearchBar, which declares `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads non-class $attrs onto its inner `<input>`, not the `<form>` root. A submit event never reaches an input, so the handler never runs and nothing preventDefaults — activating the control performs a native browser GET form submission and reloads the SPA.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-15; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js:309 `inheritAttrs: !1` and :327-341 (root gets only class + data-surface; `o.value` = $attrs-minus-class is spread onto the `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef"...}, o.value, ...))`). Live measurement: URL before `http://localhost:9000/#/extract` → after clicking the type=submit button `http://localhost:9000/?#/extract` (Playwright: "Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation"); sessionStorage.PROBE_SWITCH === null. Navigation-safe rerun: formVei null, inputVei null, eventsAfterSubmit [].
defects.mechanism: A component's fallthrough contract was assumed rather than read; `tag="form"` makes SearchBar look like a form element while inheritAttrs:false re-routes every listener to the input.
defects.reproduction: Mount the unmodified SFC into the live dev page via Vite /@fs, click Login, type a slug, click the submit Button — the page navigates (a `?` is appended to the URL) and the switchSlug emit never fires.
defects.proposedCure: Own the `<form>` in the consumer (`<form @submit.prevent><SearchBar tag="div"/><Button type="submit"/></form>`, the idiom SlugEditLayer.vue:76-79 already uses), or add a first-class `@submit` emit to glass-ui SearchBar so `tag="form"` becomes honest.

defects.defect: The slug input is never focused: the focus call runs ~226 ms before the element is inserted, because `nextTick` inside a 50 ms setTimeout races a `<Transition mode="out-in">` whose leave runs for `--duration-fast: 0.2s`. `searchBarRef.value` is null and `?.` swallows the call; there is no retry.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:172-182 and :4; demo/styles/animations.css:111-116; measured on the live page: durFast "0.2s", insertedAtMs 276, and document.activeElement never becomes the input across samples at 0/62/82/155/305/606/1207 ms.
defects.mechanism: A time-based guess (setTimeout 50) layered on a lifecycle fact (Transition out-in completion) — two clocks, no handshake.
defects.reproduction: Mount the SFC live, click Login, rAF-poll for `host.querySelector('input')` and sample document.activeElement — input appears at 276 ms, focus never lands.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the setTimeout and focus from the transition's own `@after-enter` hook; restore focus to the trigger on cancel/escape; switch the string ref to `useTemplateRef` per edict 7.

defects.defect: `slugSwitching` is set true and reset in the same synchronous turn (the async `onSlugSwitch` contains no `await`, so `finally` runs before the stack unwinds), making the Loader2 spinner and the `:disabled` double-submit guard unrenderable.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225 (no await), :23 and :26. Live invocation of the real component's onSlugSwitch through the dev instance handle, 5 inputs × 6 rAF frames: slugSwitchingAfterSyncCall=false and spinnerRenderedAnyFrame=false for every case.
defects.mechanism: A loading flag wrapped around a fire-and-forget `emit` — the actual network work happens in the parent (useSlugMigration.onSlugSwitch, which IS async) and the child has no handle on it.
defects.reproduction: Call `inst.setupState.onSlugSwitch()` on the mounted component and read `slugSwitching` synchronously on return: already false; `.animate-spin` absent for 6 consecutive frames.
defects.proposedCure: Make the port's onSlugSwitch return Promise<void> and await it here — one change repairs the spinner, the disabled guard, and gives the dead catch block (C-16) a real rejection to catch.

defects.defect: `const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized)` makes 'admin token' the catch-all branch: any input that is not exactly four lowercase hyphenated words is submitted as an admin credential, and the parent then wipes the user's persisted identity before trying it.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:205,213; useSlugMigration.ts:51-57 (`deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value)`); demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:129-132 → clearAuth() at :44-48 (nulls slug ref, safeRemoveItem(localStorage, SLUG_KEY), clearPersistedToken()). Live emissions from the real component: "cool-blue-fox" → ["switchSlug","cool-blue-fox",true]; "cool2-blue-fox-jump" → ["switchSlug","cool2-blue-fox-jump",true].
defects.mechanism: One text field carrying two disjoint credential types, disambiguated by a negated shape test that treats 'unrecognisable' as 'privileged'.
defects.reproduction: Set slugInput to a 3-word typo ("cool-blue-fox") and invoke onSlugSwitch on the mounted component: emits switchSlug with isAdmin=true. Currently latent behind C-2 in this component; the byte-identical code is LIVE in SlugEditLayer.vue:46,54.
defects.proposedCure: Make the admin route explicit and non-inferred (the `ADMIN_TOKEN=` prefix as the only admin trigger); reject anything that is neither with a shape hint; never clear the existing session before the server accepts the new credential.

defects.defect: The slug input has no accessible name — placeholder-only, no label, no aria-label, no name attribute.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:12; measured on the mounted component: inputAria { label: null, describedby: null, invalid: null, name: null, type: "search" }. WCAG 4.1.2 / 3.3.2.
defects.mechanism: Placeholder used as label; the design-system SearchBar takes no label prop and the consumer supplies none.
defects.reproduction: Mount, enter edit mode, read `host.querySelector('input').getAttribute('aria-label')` → null.
defects.proposedCure: Pass `aria-label="Slug or admin token"` (it lands on the input via the same $attrs passthrough that breaks C-2) plus a visible label where layout allows.

defects.defect:
The async error message is never announced and never associated with the field: the error `

` has no aria-live/role=alert, and the input gets neither aria-describedby nor aria-invalid.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:124-126; measured after forcing setError(): errorP { ariaLive: null, role: null }; querySelectorAll("[aria-live], [role=alert]").length === 0; inputAria.describedby null, .invalid null. WCAG 4.1.3 / 3.3.1.
defects.mechanism: Error state modelled as decorative text rather than a status message bound to the control it describes.
defects.reproduction: Mount, call the exposed `setError(...)`, query the component for live regions → 0.
defects.proposedCure:
role="alert" + an id on the

; bind aria-describedby and aria-invalid="true" on the input while slugError is non-empty.

defects.defect: The identity pill is a non-focusable <span> behind a hover-only Popover, so the only copy explaining what a slug is cannot be reached by keyboard or touch; the logged-in bar has exactly one tabbable control.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:45-60 (`trigger="hover"`, `<span class="slug-pill cursor-help">`); measured: pill { tag:"SPAN", tabIndex:-1, role:null, ariaDescribedby:null }, `pill.focus()` → activeElement !== pill, tabbablesInBar = ["BUTTON/Account menu"], popoverAfterHover true (mouse only). WCAG 2.1.1 / 1.4.13.
defects.mechanism: A disclosure implemented as decoration — cursor-help promises an affordance the markup does not provide.
defects.reproduction: Mount with userSlug set; call pill.focus() → not focused; enumerate tabbables → one button only; dispatch pointerenter → popover text appears.
defects.proposedCure: Make it a real disclosure: glass-ui Tooltip/Popover anchored on a <button> (or tabindex=0 + role), with a trigger mode that accepts focus as well as hover — reusing the existing component-type name per edict 4.

defects.defect: `variant="ghost"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7's Button (the axes are `emphasis` and `tone`), so it leaks into the DOM as a junk attribute and both edit-mode buttons render with the DEFAULT filled `secondary` emphasis instead of the intended quiet treatment.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:19,31; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts (ButtonProps has emphasis/tone/size/iconOnly/loading — no `variant`); _shared/axes.d.ts: tone is "NEVER a `variant` member". Measured DOM: { aria:"Sign in with slug", variantAttr:"ghost", emphasis:"secondary" } and { aria:"Cancel slug edit", variantAttr:"ghost", emphasis:"secondary" }.
defects.mechanism: Pre-7.0 API residue; Vue templates admit arbitrary fallthrough attributes so an unknown prop is silently accepted.
defects.reproduction: Mount, enter edit mode, read `btn.getAttribute('variant')` → "ghost" and `btn.dataset.emphasis` → "secondary". `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0, no diagnostic.
defects.proposedCure: Use `emphasis="quiet"`; if a true ghost rung is wanted it belongs in glass-ui's ButtonEmphasis union, not a demo override.

defects.defect: Zero tests cover the component, and named single-line mutations that break the product keep every gate green — a vacuous gate.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar" test/ e2e/` → only a prose comment at e2e/smoke/flows/login-register.spec.ts:6-9 stating the surface is unused; demo/test/ holds 3 unrelated files; `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → EXIT=0; eslint.config.js:153-154,182 disable vue/no-unused-vars, no-unused-components and no-unused-properties.
defects.mechanism: The component's entire observable behaviour lies outside the tested surface, so both BLOCKERs survived every gate in the repo.
defects.reproduction: Replace the whole <template> with <div/>, or invert line 205 to `const isAdmin = looksLikeSlug(normalized)`, or change looksLikeSlug's regex to /^$/, or delete the emit at line 213 — `vitest run`, `playwright test`, `vue-tsc` and `eslint` all still pass.
defects.proposedCure: Delete this component (C-1) and give the surviving slug surface three tests: a real form submit emits switchSlug exactly once; focus lands in the field after the transition settles; a rejected login renders and announces its message. All three would have failed on day one here.

defects.defect: The entire slug protocol (looksLikeSlug, normalizeTokenInput, the submit routine, onCopySlug) is duplicated verbatim in SlugEditLayer.vue, and the two copies have already drifted — different 'already signed in' strings, one surface that renders an unreachable error and one that renders none at all.

defects.defect: Motion: an untokenized magic 50ms delay, a Transition mode="out-in" + nextTick focus race that almost certainly leaves the input unfocused in a real browser, and a max-height transition arm that is a no-op while its overflow:hidden side effect still clips.

Under mode="out-in" Vue mounts the incoming branch only in the outgoing branch's afterLeave, long after nextTick, so searchBarRef is null and ?. swallows the focus. animations.css:104-119 gives .vj-morph-*-active a max-height transition parameterised by --vj-morph-collapse/--vj-morph-expanded plus overflow:hidden; this site sets neither (scoped block :239-243 is a comment and an @reference only). CREDIT: reduced motion is satisfied for free by the global guard (animations.css:80).

defects.reproduction: NEGATIVE in jsdom — probe P1 reports `input present = true, activeElement = INPUT, focused input? = true`, because jsdom reports no transition duration so Vue resolves the leave synchronously. The failure is real-browser-only and I could not produce the frame: the component mounts in no browser (D-1). LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS for the focus arm. defects.defect: Overflow, truncation and RTL were never designed: no min-w-0, no max-width, no truncate, not even whitespace-nowrap. A 48-character slug measures 502.44px — 1.29× the 390px arm and 1.57× the 320px arm.
defects.evidence: Probe Q3: pill class = `slug-pill cursor-help` (nothing else), root class = `flex items-center gap-1.5 mb-2 pt-0.5 relative min-h-9` (no flex-wrap, no min-w-0). Measured in the live document: a 48-char .slug-pill renders 502.44 × 28.95px. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §2 / VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.2 bind 1440/390/320/actual-400%-zoom. Both live siblings at least add whitespace-nowrap (ProfileSection.vue:73, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:48). RTL: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1 requires "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose" — the pill (:47-52) has no isolation.
defects.mechanism: unbounded content in an unconstrained flex row; the overflow state was never enumerated
defects.reproduction: Mount probe Q3 for the class inventory; inject a 48-char .slug-pill into a .app-layout host on the live app and read getBoundingClientRect → w 502.44.
defects.proposedCure: min-w-0 on the flex parent, truncate + a max-inline-size on the pill (the full slug already lives in the hover Popover at :54-59 and in "Copy slug"), and dir="ltr"/unicode-bidi:isolate on the value span.

defects.reproduction: grep -c "hasSavedPalettes" demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue → 2; grep -n 'emit("copy"|\$emit(.copy' on the same file → empty; grep -rn resetEditMode demo/ → only the declaration and the defineExpose.

""; if (msg.includes("409")) ... }` — useSlugMigration.ts:78-82 documents this exact pattern as already repaired: "branch on the typed ApiProblem.status, not .message substrings — the server titles ... never contain '409'/'404'/'429', so those branches matched nothing and the authored copy below never showed." defects.defect: Even if it were remounted, its topology is not the Account composition the constitution ratifies — it is an inline identity strip in the Library body, with no recovery-credential-rotation affordance and no secret-retention region, plus a hover Popover that explains rather than affords.

It owns registration/recovery when signed out and identity, recovery-credential rotation and logout when active; secret retention temporarily replaces its action region... W23 owns the rendered composition and journey while W15 supplies auth/outbox state." PaletteSlugBar.vue:2 is a flex strip; there is no rotation control and no secret-retention region anywhere in the file. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.6: "do not compensate for an unnecessary action with tooltip proliferation. Subtraction precedes explanation" — vs the w-56 hover card at :54-59 on a cursor-help span explaining what a slug is.
