defects.reproduction: Read VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.6 against PaletteSlugBar.vue:2, :54-59, and the absent rotation/secret-retention affordances.
defects.proposedCure: Deletion (D-1). The composition W23 owns replaces it; remounting would install a shape the constitution has already superseded.

defects.defect: RETRACTED FINDING, recorded because the retraction is evidence. I flagged `border-muted-foreground` (:65) as a dead Tailwind class — both live siblings pointedly avoid it with inline styles, which reads exactly like a routed-around broken idiom. Measurement disproved it. The surviving design observation is that the admin state renders grey here while the ratified successor gives admin the gold identity.
defects.evidence: Live measurement in the running document: withBothClasses → border rgb(124,102,80) / color rgb(124,102,80); onlyTextMuted → border rgb(198,180,159); onlyBorderMuted → border rgb(124,102,80) / color rgb(28,25,23). The class resolves — RETRACTED. Surviving observation: PaletteSlugBar.vue:63-68 renders admin as `text-muted-foreground border-muted-foreground` (grey), while ProfileSection.vue:96 renders it `class="slug-pill cursor-default whitespace-nowrap gold-shimmer" style="border-color: var(--color-gold); color: var(--color-gold)"` — the ratified gold identity (owner feedback: "golden shimmer pill"). Two admin identities in one codebase; the orphan has the un-designed one.
defects.mechanism: divergent state treatment between an orphan and its successor — and, for the retracted arm, inference-from-siblings standing in for measurement
defects.reproduction: Inject the three class combinations into a .app-layout host on http://localhost:9000 and read getComputedStyle().borderTopColor — values above. The retraction is fully reproducible.
defects.proposedCure: None for the retracted arm. For the surviving arm: the admin identity is one composition (gold-shimmer, --color-gold) owned at the root, not two per-surface improvisations — D-1's deletion resolves it.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the application's ONLY login-failure copy is imperatively pushed into this never-mounted orphan through a template ref (`slugBarRef`) that is never bound to any element, so a wrong slug in the live dock fails completely silently: no message, no announcement, no state. Four links, each verified by file:line and exhaustive grep — useSlugMigration.ts:83-87 writes into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; the ref is created at :30 and returned at :121 but usePalettePorts.ts:257's only consumer (App.vue:153-156) reads three unrelated keys, so it is never bound; SlugEditLayer.vue:54 calls onSlugSwitch un-awaited and onSlugSwitch never rethrows, making SlugEditLayer's own catch unreachable; and SlugEditLayer declares `slugError` at :13 yet never renders it (template :75-119) while :56 tears the form down synchronously. The design defect is not staleness — it is that an error surface was made a private child capability (defineExpose + parent-held instance ref) instead of a property of the auth composition, so deleting the host silently deleted the app's failure affordance with zero type, test, or e2e signal. D-1 (the orphan itself) is the enabling condition; D-2 is the shipped, user-facing hole.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for balance, since this seat was instructed not to hunt for reasons the component is fine: two things genuinely pass and are stated as such in the report. (1) Owner edict 6 (animations are never deleted) — the component consumes the global `vj-morph` family rather than hand-rolling a fourth transition name, and reduced motion is honoured for free by the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:80 ("The global prefers-reduced-motion guard below neutralises all three"); no per-site work, no violation. (2) Owner edict 8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) — PaletteSlugBar.vue:131-145 are all runtime imports with no type-only import mis-declared. Edict 1 (no god modules) also passes at 243 focused lines. One further negative is recorded honestly as a RETRACTION (D-16): I inferred that `border-muted-foreground` was a dead class because both live siblings avoid it with inline styles; live measurement showed it resolves correctly (border rgb(124,102,80) with the class, rgb(198,180,159) without), and I retracted it. The evidence law earned its keep there — the inference was strong, plausible, and wrong.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the Tags filter is inert: SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 binds `:checked` / `@update:checked`, but glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox has props ["modelValue","defaultValue","disabled","value","id","class","asChild","as","name","required"] and emits exactly ["update:modelValue"] (measured from the shipped bundle; `grep -rl "update:checked" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns nothing). A real mount+click emits only ["update:modelValue"], so `toggleTag` is unreachable and `update:selectedTags` never fires — the tag filter never reaches `currentFilterOpts()`. Because `modelValue` is unbound the control is UNCONTROLLED: it ticks visually, never reports, and never resets when "Clear all filters" empties `pm.selectedTags` — so the UI desynchronises permanently. The identical break sits on the tag WRITE path at TagEditPopover.vue:27-30; these are the demo's only two Checkbox usages, so no correct example exists to have caught it. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundness, §5 of the report: every one of the 11 import specifiers at SearchFilterBar.vue:127-145 resolves within or below its own layer — no feature→shell, component→boot, or demo→src-internal edge exists. The library reach is HONEST and my "stale self-installed tarball" hypothesis was refuted by `tsc --traceResolution`: `@mkbabb/value.js/css` resolves through the repo's own package.json#exports self-name resolution to dist/subpaths/css.d.ts — the same edge a real npm consumer traverses. verbatimModuleSyntax clean (one type-only import, correctly marked). Vue 3.5 idioms correct (reactive props destructure, useTemplateRef in the sibling). My "dead CSS token" hypothesis was refuted by live measurement — --type-small/--leading-small/--radius-md/--duration-fast/--ease-standard/--font-serif/--accent all resolve. Every glass-ui prop OTHER than `variant` and Checkbox's `checked` was verified correct against measured props/emits. No console or page errors from this component in any of the four browse captures.)

defects.defect: The Tags filter is inert — the component binds `:checked` / `@update:checked`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not have. The control is left uncontrolled: it ticks visually, never emits anything the parent listens for, and never resets when the filter state is cleared.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Spec: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts:4-12,19 declares `modelValue?: CheckedState | null` and `"update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any`. Measured runtime: props=["modelValue","defaultValue","disabled","value","id","class","asChild","as","name","required"] emits=["update:modelValue"]. `grep -rl "update:checked" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches. Mount probe output: EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"] · DOM: <button data-slot="checkbox" … checked="false" role="checkbox" … data-state="checked"> (the `checked` prop landed as a raw fallthrough attribute; data-state flipped from the control's own internal state). `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0. Identical defect at demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:27-30 (the tag WRITE path) — the demo's only other Checkbox usage.
defects.mechanism: Consumer speaks a retired design-system API; Vue admits unknown attrs as fallthrough and unknown on* handlers as native listeners, so the prop/emit rename is silent at both runtime and typecheck.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config <scratch cfg pointing root at repo>; probe file mounts glass-ui Checkbox with {checked:false, 'onUpdate:checked', 'onUpdate:modelValue'}, clicks [role=checkbox], asserts the emit ledger → EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"]. In-app: open /#/browse ⋮ → Tags, tick a tag; the badge stays 0 and the wall does not change; then Clear all filters and the tick remains.
defects.proposedCure: Controlled v-model shape: `<Checkbox :model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)" />`, same at TagEditPopover.vue:27-30. Architecturally: make the class of defect impossible — FilterMenu becomes stateless over one `v-model:query` object (see L-4 cure), so no local/uncontrolled state can desynchronise from the wall; and close the gate that let glass-ui 7 land un-migrated (a vue/no-undef-properties-class rule for glass-ui components, since vue-tsc exits 0 on all of these today).

defects.defect: `variant="ghost"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7's Button — the string lands as a raw DOM attribute and the button renders at the default `emphasis="secondary"`. 51 sites across 20 demo files.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:5 and :111-115. Spec: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:3-9 — `export type ButtonEmphasis = "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"; interface ButtonProps { emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis; tone?: Tone; … }` — no `variant`. Live DOM at localhost:9000/#/browse: {hasVariantAttr:"ghost", dataEmphasis:"secondary", dataTone:"neutral", bg:"oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686 / 0.52)", class:"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule …", size:"32x40"}. Button.props.emphasis.default === "secondary" (measured from the bundle). Visual confirmation: audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png — the ⋮ trigger is a filled chip, and BrowsePane.vue:69-76 `variant="outline"` Retry renders as a solid filled pill. Census: 51 `<Button variant=…>` sites — outline 28, ghost 19, primary-audacious 2, destructive 1, default 1.
defects.mechanism: Same as L-1: consumer speaks a retired design-system axis. glass-ui 7 replaced shadcn's single `variant` with orthogonal `emphasis` × `tone`; the demo was never migrated, and per-instance Tailwind size overrides were added to compensate.
defects.reproduction: node -e 'const m=await import("./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js"); console.log(Object.keys(m.Button.props))' → no "variant". Then in the live app: document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Filters"]').getAttribute('variant') === "ghost" while .dataset.emphasis === "secondary"; getBoundingClientRect() === 32x40 despite class="h-8 w-8".
defects.proposedCure: Migrate the axis, no compat map (edict 2): ghost→emphasis="quiet", outline→emphasis="secondary", default→emphasis="primary", destructive→emphasis="primary" tone="danger". Delete the per-instance `h-8 w-8` / `h-7 w-full` overrides in favour of `size` (edict 5 — the measured 32x40 shows the override half-loses anyway). Wire a lint rule so a glass-ui prop rename fails loud instead of exiting 0.

defects.defect: The colour filter is the only one of five that never reaches the wire; BrowsePane re-implements the API's own OKLab matcher client-side over a single 50-row page, while the transport for the server-side filter is built, wired, and dead.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:336-349 (`colorSearchParams`, `displayedBrowse`, `const radius = 0.15`, `Math.hypot(c.L-L, c.a-a, c.b-b) <= radius`) vs api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-180 (`colorMatcherFor`, `query.colorRadius ?? 0.15`, `Math.sqrt(dL*dL+da*da+db*db) <= radius`) — same predicate, same default, same empty-array rule, same .some(). Transport exists: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-31 declares colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius, :50-53 serialises them; api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:89-92 validates them. Never set: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-60 `currentFilterOpts()` emits limit/sort/q/tier/tags only; `grep -rn "colorL" demo/` → 2 hits, both the declaration and the serialiser. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts:19). Comment at BrowsePane.vue:353-354: "API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant".
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership across the client/server boundary; an optimisation note became the only implementation, so the concept has two homes and the canonical one is unreachable.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'colorL' demo/ → only api/palettes.ts:27,50. Read useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-60 — no color* key. Therefore any colour search narrows only the loaded page: a matching palette on keyset page 2 of the commons is invisible and the wall reports empty.
defects.proposedCure: Delete colorSearchParams and displayedBrowse. Put `color: { L, a, b, radius } | null` in the shared filter state next to tier/tags and add three lines to currentFilterOpts(). crud-list.ts becomes the single home for OKLab distance; Math.hypot leaves the demo entirely. Pair with publishing `deltaE(a,b)` from @mkbabb/value.js/color so the API stops hand-rolling it too (`grep -rn "deltaE\|colorDistance" src/` → zero hits in a colour library).

defects.defect: The five filters this one component emits have four different owners, and three of them are homed in the *dialog* sub-feature. There is no filter-state module; useBrowsePalettes is a 240-line god module holding filter state + keyset pagination + CRUD.
defects.evidence: sort → useBrowsePalettes.ts:116; tier/selectedTags/clearFilters → demo/palettes/browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts:91-100 (imported by BrowsePane.vue:255-265 from './browser/dialog'); colorSearch → BrowsePane.vue:351 (pane-local); text → useBrowsePalettes.ts:43 AND :57. That file's own header at :17-18 documents the mismatch: "Browse filter handlers (onTierChange / onTagsChange / onClearFilters): mutate pm.tierFilter / pm.selectedTags and reload." activeFilterCount (SearchFilterBar.vue:189-195) reads tier+selectedTags from PROPS but colorSearchActive from a LOCAL ref (:171); onClearAll (:227-232) must fire TWO events to reset one concept, caught by BrowsePane.vue:328-332 and :357-359. `wc -l demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts` = 240.
defects.mechanism: No unique semantic home for the 'browse query' concept, so each filter landed wherever its handler was first written; the god module had no room for it.
defects.reproduction: Read the six emit sites in SearchFilterBar.vue:154-161 and follow each binding in BrowsePane.vue:15-26 to its handler. Four distinct modules, two of them (dialog composables, pane-local) semantically wrong.
defects.proposedCure: NEW demo/palettes/browse/useBrowseQuery.ts owning { text, sort, tier, tags, color, radius } + toListOptions(): ListPalettesOptions + activeCount + clear(). useBrowsePalettes becomes useBrowsePage (paging + fetch only); vote/rename/delete/visibility/fork lift into usePaletteMutations.ts; useDialogBrowseActions.ts is DELETED. SearchFilterBar becomes a stateless FilterMenu over one `v-model:query` — which also makes L-1's desync arithmetically impossible and collapses the double-fired clear.

defects.defect: A hand-rolled 6-digit-hex regex gates the field one line in front of the full CSS Color Level 4 parser it already imports; rejected input is silently replaced by the swatch colour, and the field's own placeholder advertises a syntax the regex refuses.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` — with hexToOklab (:205-211) calling parseColorIn, and placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)" at :92, pickerHex default "#4488cc" at :170. Measured library capability: parseCssColor+convertColor resolve all of `hsl(210 60% 50%)` → oklab 0.5883 -0.0443 -0.1319, `oklch(0.7 0.15 250)` → 0.7000 -0.0513 -0.1410, `rebeccapurple` → 0.4403 0.0882 -0.1339, `#48c` → 0.6136 -0.0415 -0.1175, `color(display-p3 0.2 0.4 0.8)` → 0.5340 -0.0363 -0.1775. The regex accepts one of the five. The `"none"` guard at :207-209 is unreachable given the gate — it defends the impossible while the possible failure is silenced.
defects.mechanism: A second, narrower, incompatible parser placed in front of the canonical total parser; failure masked by a fallback instead of surfaced (edict 2: masking fallbacks).
defects.reproduction: Type `rebeccapurple` (or `hsl(210 60% 50%)`, or `#48c`) into the Find-by-Colour field and press Search. The emitted colorSearch triple is that of #4488cc, not the typed colour. No error, no visual difference from success — colorSearchActive goes true and the badge increments.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex. `parseColorIn(text, "oklab")` inside a try, surfacing PickerColorError as field-invalid state via glass-ui Input's existing `invalid` prop (measured present). The library is a total parser; stop putting a partial one in front of it.

defects.defect: One component carries two colour engines: SearchFilterBar reaches the library for colour while its only child, MiniColorPicker, hand-rolls the full HSV↔RGB↔hex conversion — inside the demo of a colour library.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:132 imports ./MiniColorPicker.vue, rendered :66-81. MiniColorPicker.vue imports only vue + ../../../ui/popover + ../../../ui/button — no value.js. Its :88-114 is an HSV→RGB sextant switch + toHex padder; :118-134 the RGB→HSV inverse, carrying its own hue hack at :126 `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue`. @mkbabb/value.js/color publishes hsv, rgb, convertColor, toRgba8 (src/subpaths/color.ts); demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:56 already declares HSV channel metadata. MEMORY records the hue-drift lesson at library level (stableHue in useColorModel). The two engines meet via a watch→emit→prop→watch round trip (MiniColorPicker.vue:116,118 ↔ SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178).
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership of a concept the library exists to own; a library-level lesson re-learned badly at component level.
defects.reproduction: grep -n '^import' demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue → vue + two ui shims, no @mkbabb/value.js. Then read :88-134.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both conversion blocks. `convertPickerColor(color, "hsv")` and `colorToCss(color)` from demo/color-session/ do all of it; the SV canvas becomes a thin h/s/v view over one AnyColor (ColorField.vue in the proposed lattice). One colour engine per demo.

defects.defect: Text search composes two incompatible matchers in series — a MongoDB $text search on the server and a substring filter on the client — producing three distinct behavioural regimes for one field.
defects.evidence: Server: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:95-96 `const q = query.q?.trim(); if (q) f.$text = { $search: q };` (stemmed, whole-word, index-driven). Client: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:43-45 `useFilteredList(remotePalettes, deps.searchQuery, (p,q) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q))` (substring). Gate: useBrowsePalettes.ts:57 `...(q.length >= 2 ? { q } : {})`. Regimes: 0 chars → neither; 1 char → client substring only; ≥2 → server $text THEN client substring.
defects.mechanism: Two homes for one concept across the client/server boundary, composed serially rather than one being canonical.
defects.reproduction: Search `blu` on a commons containing "Blue Ridge": $text has no whole-word token `blu`, the server returns nothing, the wall is empty. Search `ocean sunset`: $text OR-matches and returns rows, then the client requires the literal contiguous string in name/slug and discards nearly all of them.
defects.proposedCure: One matcher. The API owns the text index — delete filteredBrowse from the browse path and lower the q gate to 1 character. useFilteredList survives for PalettesPane's genuinely local list.

defects.defect: The library type `Channel = number | "none"` forces every consumer to invent its own policy; four demo sites do so and none agree. The library publishes no projection off it.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:205-211 → THROW ("Hex color produced missing OKLab channels"); demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:127-128 → return null; demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownColors.ts:39-42,52 → THROW on L/C with a different message, COERCE H→0; demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:39-41 → pass "none" through as display text. src/subpaths/color.ts exports the `Channel` type and no resolver. Related: `grep -rn "deltaE\|colorDistance" src/` → zero hits.
defects.mechanism: Missing library-level projection → four ad-hoc homes for one policy.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'channels' demo/ | grep '"none"' — four call sites, four disciplines.
defects.proposedCure: Publish from @mkbabb/value.js/color: `resolveChannels(color): Result<readonly [number,number,number], ColorIssue>` — one home, one policy, four call sites collapse. Publish `deltaE(a, b)` in the same pass so L-3's duplicate distance metric has a canonical home.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a 19-directory alias layer whose entire content is 20 lines of pure re-export; 24 demo files reach glass-ui through it and directly in the same file, and it hides which glass-ui subpath a symbol lives on.
defects.evidence: demo/ui/button/index.ts = `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; demo/ui/input/index.ts = `export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";` (a DIFFERENT subpath, invisible at the import site). `find demo/ui -name "*.ts" | wc -l` = 19; non-comment non-blank lines across all barrels = 20. `for f in $(grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo/ | grep -v '^demo/ui/'); do grep -q 'from "\.\..*ui/[a-z-]*"' $f && echo $f; done | wc -l` = 24 — e.g. BrowsePane.vue imports Card from ../ui/card (:180) and SearchBar from @mkbabb/glass-ui/search (:194). demo/DESIGN.md:384 defends the layer while citing `@components/ui/alert`, an alias W43/RF-15 deleted (`grep -rn '"@components/' demo/ src/` → 0). Counter-evidence recorded: for these five symbols the shim is the only path (Button 22/0, Input 4/0, Popover 5/0, Checkbox 2/0, RadioGroup 2/0), so the 'dual path' hypothesis is refuted per-symbol; the defect is the arbitrary coverage line.
defects.mechanism: Alias/shim layer (edict 2) with zero added ergonomics, covering an arbitrary subset of the design system so the same file must use two idioms.
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/*/index.ts — 20 lines of substance across 19 files. Then read demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:180 and :194.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ (19 files, −20 lines) and import @mkbabb/glass-ui / @mkbabb/glass-ui/forms at the point of use. Zero behaviour change, one idiom, and the subpath becomes legible at the import site.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's `paths` block advertises a value.js public surface that package.json#exports does not have — three phantom keys pointing at files that do not exist, two real exports omitted — and its own header states the wrong map.
defects.evidence: `node -p "Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' ')"` → `./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize` (7 keys, NO root "."). tsconfig.demo.json paths keys → `@mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize`. Phantoms: bare root (target ./dist/index.d.ts — absent; `ls dist/` shows subpaths/ + 3 chunks), /parsing (dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts — absent), /units (absent). Omitted: /css and /value (both real exports). The header asserts "the bare `.` root + the 7 subpath barrels … a CLOSED 8-key set". vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports so it "can never drift"; tsconfig hand-maintains a second, drifted copy. Latent break: `import … from "@mkbabb/value.js"` typechecks via paths but has no Vite alias (no `.` export) → falls to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Currently zero such demo imports (grep → one prose mention at demo/shared/utils.ts:12).
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained second copy of a generated map — a false public surface advertised by the very config that is meant to be the trust boundary.
defects.reproduction: Compare the two key sets above; `ls dist/subpaths/` shows color css easing math quantize transform value — no parsing, no units, and no dist/index.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the six @mkbabb/value.js* paths entries. `tsc --traceResolution` proves TypeScript already resolves the whole map through Node self-name resolution honouring `exports` exactly as a real consumer does (measured on /css) — strictly more faithful than the paths shortcut. Removing them makes drift impossible rather than merely discouraged.

defects.defect: The palette-browser barrel header claims eslint enforces its seam 'standing'. It does not: three of G-DEMO-3b's four file globs are deleted trees, and the banned import specifier can no longer occur.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:1-18 — "never a raw internal .vue file — the G-DEMO-3b boundary (eslint.config.js) enforces it standing." eslint.config.js:230-256 scopes it to demo/color-picker/**, demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/** and bans group `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`. Measured: demo/@/components MISSING, demo/@/lib MISSING, demo/@/composables MISSING (W43/RF-15 killed demo/@ and every @… alias); `grep -rn '"@components/' demo/ src/ | wc -l` → 0. G-DEMO-1 and G-DEMO-3a (:257-303) are scoped entirely to demo/@/composables/** and are therefore inert. demo/palettes/** — where the feature actually lives — is in no rule's scope. Honest counter-evidence: `grep -rn 'from "[^"]*browser/[a-z]*/[A-Z][A-Za-z]*\.vue"' demo/` → nothing; the convention holds by discipline with the guardrail disconnected.
defects.mechanism: Enforcement rot — a lint rule whose globs and banned specifiers were invalidated by a tree restructure, leaving a claim of enforcement with no mechanism.
defects.reproduction: for g in demo/color-picker demo/@/components demo/@/lib demo/@/composables; do [ -d $g ] && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING; done → EXISTS MISSING MISSING MISSING. grep -rn '"@components/' demo/ src/ → 0 hits.
defects.proposedCure: Re-point the globs at the real trees (demo/palettes/**, demo/picker/**, demo/shell/**, demo/workbenches/**, demo/scenes/**) and re-express the ban as a relative-path group (**/palettes/browser/*/*.vue) — or delete the rules and stop claiming enforcement in the barrel headers. A rule whose glob does not exist reads as green, which is worse than no rule.

defects.defect: Vestigial single-child flex root; the component's name no longer describes what it is (a single popover trigger, not a bar).
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:2 `<div class="flex items-center gap-1.5">` wraps exactly one child, the <Popover> at :3-123. A flex container with gap and one item is a no-op; it also blocks attribute fallthrough to the trigger.
defects.mechanism: Residue of an earlier multi-control bar; the wrapper outlived its contents.
defects.reproduction: Read SearchFilterBar.vue:2-123 — one child element.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the wrapper, make <Popover> the root, and rename to FilterMenu.vue as part of the L-4 lattice move.
